A/B Test Analysis (AI variants)

How to run

This skill is executable. Collect the inputs below, then run python3 scripts/run_skill.py ai-platform/ab-test-analysis --input <name>=<value> … --out <dir> (see --explain ai-platform/ab-test-analysis). Report the run.json results; do not hand-write the deliverables the script produces (ab-results.csv, ab-report.md, ab.json). A sample ratio mismatch fails the run (exit 1) on purpose: every output is still written, and the decision reads "untrustworthy". Each output passes --verify, which re-derives it from the results and the config recorded in ab.json.

Starting points

  • Existing — you bring the per-variant results of an experiment that has run (plus its pre-registered config); the skill checks the split, tests every metric and returns ship / don't ship / inconclusive.
  • Only for existing: an A/B analysis always reads results from an experiment that already ran; pre-launch sizing without results belongs in the experiment design, not here.

When to use

  • ADLC improve stage: a prompt, model, retrieval or agent change ran as an online experiment and the team needs ship / don't ship / inconclusive with the statistics behind it.
  • Trust check before reading lifts: is the traffic split what the config promised (SRM)?
  • Planning a re-run: achieved power for the declared MDE and the n per arm it needs.
  • NOT for: offline eval sets or LLM-as-judge scoring (llm-eval-harness), staged rollout gates (ai-release-plan), production drift and alerting (llm-observability), sequential or Bayesian designs (this is fixed-horizon frequentist).

Inputs

InputRequiredSourceIf missing
results — aggregated or unit-level CSVyesexperimentation platform export or warehouse queryrun stops (exit 2), asks once
config — kv-csv (assets/ab-config.csv)noExperiment owner (pre-registration)defaults used and labelled: control = variant named control else first variant, alpha 0.05, power 0.8, equal split, srm_alpha 0.001, direction higher_better; MDE and guardrails To be baselined · owner: Experiment owner

Aggregated: one row per variant (and per metric when several). Binary metrics use conversions/users; continuous metrics use metric_sum and metric_sumsq (sum of squares). Unit-level: one row per randomised unit; converted is 0/1, value is continuous, guardrail columns are named in guardrails. Guardrails take a direction, e.g. escalated:lower_better;csat:higher_better. mde is absolute (0.02) or relative to control (5%).

Procedure

  1. Read ../../../shared/quality-bar.md.
  2. Confirm the config was fixed before the experiment ran (alpha, MDE, primary metric, guardrails). Post-hoc changes invalidate the p-values; record them in the report notes.
  3. Run the agent. scripts/ab_test.py checks SRM, then tests each declared metric per treatment against control, applies Holm across treatments, computes power, and applies the decision rule.
  4. If SRM is detected (exit 1), stop: send the split table to the platform owner and do not quote any lift.
  5. Read the Guardrails section: a guardrail with no declared direction blocks a ship on any significant move.
  6. Inconclusive with low achieved power → quote the n per arm needed for the MDE; do not call it "no effect".
  7. Run the self-check.

Output

  • ab-results.csv — metric, role, variant, n, rate_or_mean, diff, ci_low, ci_high, rel_lift, p_value, p_adj, significant (control rows read n/a / control).
  • ab-report.md — Summary (decision first, settings with their basis), Sample ratio check, Results (primary metric and power), Guardrails, Decision (per treatment and overall, with the rule), Method & limits.
  • ab.json — config as given, effective settings and provenance, every statistic, decisions.

Self-check

  • [ ] SRM checked first; an SRM run is reported as untrustworthy, not as a result
  • [ ] Every default is labelled; MDE and guardrails come from the Experiment owner or read TBD with that owner
  • [ ] Holm-adjusted p-values drive significance when there is more than one treatment
  • [ ] Guardrail breaches block a ship; undeclared guardrail directions are flagged
  • [ ] Inconclusive results state power / required n instead of "no difference"
  • [ ] Limits stated: fixed-horizon, independent units, statistical not product sign-off

References

  • references/method.md — formulas, decision rule, worked numbers used in the tests
  • references/sources.md — SRM (Fabijan et al., Kohavi et al.), Welch, Holm, incomplete beta; verified URLs and dates
  • assets/ab-config.csv, assets/results-aggregated-template.csv, assets/results-unit-template.csv — input layouts
  • scripts/ab_test.py — analysis and --verify (argparse; stdlib)

Agent Architecture

How to run

This skill is executable. Collect the inputs below, then run python3 scripts/run_skill.py ai-platform/agent-architecture --input <name>=<value> … --out <dir> (see --explain ai-platform/agent-architecture). Report the run.json results; do not hand-write the deliverables the scripts produce (pattern.md, design-check.csv). A failed design check (exit 1) is the gate working: fix the doc or contracts and re-run.

Starting points

  • New — an agent idea: answer the six decision-tree questions and draft the design doc from assets/agent-design-doc.md; the skill picks the pattern and gates the draft and its tool contracts before build.
  • Existing — an agent already running: bring its design doc, tool contracts and the six answers re-taken with production evidence; the skill re-derives the pattern, flags a doc whose declared pattern no longer matches the tree, and re-gates sections and contracts.

When to use

  • Designing a new agentic system or reviewing one: pattern, state, tools, control flow, HITL, failure handling.
  • Framework-neutral by default; LangGraph patterns are given because they are the house standard (see ../../../shared/stack-conventions.md).
  • NOT for: writing an MCP server (mcp-server-builder), retrieval tuning (rag-pipeline-design), scoring quality (llm-eval-harness).

Inputs required

InputRequiredSource
Job to be done, in one sentence, with the success metricyesuser
Actions the system may take (read-only vs write; external side effects)yesuser
Available tools/APIs/data sources and their auth modelyesuser / repo
Autonomy appetite: who approves what, and the blast radius of a wrong actionyesuser; default to conservative if unstated
Latency and cost envelopenouser; mark To be baselined · owner to be named
Non-functional constraints (data residency, PII, audit)nouser

If the job statement or the action list is missing, ask once. Never design an agent for an undefined task.

Procedure

  1. Read ../../../shared/quality-bar.md, ../../../shared/stack-conventions.md, ../../../shared/token-efficiency.md.
  2. Decide the pattern with references/decision-tree.md. Default order of preference: deterministic workflow → single agent with bounded tools → multi-agent. Escalate only when the previous level fails a stated criterion. Record the criterion that forced the escalation.
  3. Design state and graph with references/langgraph-patterns.md: typed state schema, nodes, edges, interrupt points, checkpointer, retry policy. One graph diagram (Mermaid) and one state table.
  4. Write tool contracts with references/mcp-tool-contracts.md and assets/tool-contract.schema.json. Every tool: name, purpose, input schema, output schema, side-effect class (read / write / irreversible), idempotency, auth scope, timeout, error shape.
  5. Place HITL checkpoints with references/hitl-placement.md. Minimum: before any irreversible side effect and before any external communication. State what the human sees and what they can do (approve / edit / reject).
  6. Fill the failure-modes table from references/failure-modes.md: loops, tool misuse, context overflow, prompt injection, cascading multi-agent errors, cost runaway. Each has detection + mitigation + owner.
  7. Produce the design doc from assets/agent-design-doc.md. Include evaluation hooks (hand off to llm-eval-harness) and observability fields (trace id, step count, tokens, cost, tool calls).
  8. Run the self-check.

Output

  • agent-design-<name>.md from the template: decision, state schema, graph, tool contracts, HITL, failure modes, NFRs, open questions.
  • Tool contracts additionally as JSON (one file per tool) when the user is going to implement.

Self-check

  • [ ] The pattern decision names the criterion that ruled out the simpler option
  • [ ] State schema is typed; every field has an owner node and a reset rule
  • [ ] Every tool has a side-effect class and an idempotency statement
  • [ ] HITL before every irreversible or external-facing action
  • [ ] Failure table covers loops, tool misuse, context overflow, prompt injection at minimum
  • [ ] Step, token, cost, and wall-clock budgets are set (or To be baselined · owner to be named)
  • [ ] No vendor benchmark claims; no "the model will figure it out"

References

  • references/decision-tree.md — workflow vs single agent vs multi-agent
  • references/langgraph-patterns.md — state, graph, interrupts, checkpoints, retries
  • references/mcp-tool-contracts.md — contract rules and anti-patterns
  • references/hitl-placement.md — where humans go and what they see
  • references/failure-modes.md — failure modes with detection and mitigation
  • scripts/pattern.py — six decision-tree answers → pattern.md (pattern, rationale, rejected patterns)
  • scripts/design_check.py — design doc + tool contracts → design-check.csv; exit 1 on a missing section or invalid contract, or (with --answers) when the doc's declared pattern differs from the decision tree's

AI-BOM Licence Check

In a conversation: check the licences now

The reply is the licence check: its first line is Gate: FAIL / PASS / PENDING — <the component(s) that decided it>, never only a request for files. It is not legal advice; say so and name Legal counsel for every review and unknown.

  • The request names components ("we fine-tuned Llama 3.1 and trained on a CC BY-NC dataset — can we ship commercially?"), or says a BOM or policy is attached but its contents are not in the conversation: give the check in this reply from the stated facts, in this order:
    1. Gate line — any deny, or commercial/redistribution use of a non-commercial licence, is FAIL; otherwise PENDING until the BOM and policy are complete.
    2. Components table — component | type (model/dataset/library/service) | licence as stated | spdx_id | use | decision | reason | flags. Normalise only to ids in assets/license-catalog.csv (e.g. CC-BY-NC-4.0, LicenseRef-Llama-3.1-Community); an unrecognised string stays unknown and goes to Legal counsel. Use rules decide what policy cannot override: a CC BY-NC dataset in commercial use is deny (non-commercial licence, commercial use). Llama 3.1 is review / conditional, never a plain allow: licence from Meta needed above 700M monthly active users, display "Built with Llama", Acceptable Use Policy, ship the agreement and Notice file, derived model names begin with "Llama".
    3. Blocked — each deny with the fix: replace the component, relicense it, or change the use.
    4. Needs review — conditional and unknown licences, routed to Legal counsel.
    5. Obligations — notices, attribution and flow-down terms to ship with the release.
    6. What I need to finish — ask once for the full BOM (component,type,version,license,source_url,use, every model, dataset, library and hosted service) and the organisation's licence policy (license,decision,notes). Without a policy, every other decision is To be baselined · owner: Legal counsel; blank versions or licences are To be baselined · owner: Engineering lead.
  • No components named ("check our AI licences"): ask once for the BOM in the CSV layout above and the licence policy; do not decide any licence from memory.
  • Asked to approve without a policy or skip the gate ("just approve the usual permissive ones", "it's only NC, ship it"): decline in one line — decisions come only from Legal counsel's policy and the documented use rules. Still normalise each licence, show every decision as To be baselined · owner: Legal counsel, and keep a non-commercial licence in commercial use as deny / gate FAIL.

Starting points

  • New — a system heading to its first release: list the components in the CSV layout; the skill normalises each licence, applies your policy and writes the AI-BOM.
  • Existing — bring the CycloneDX AI-BOM kept from the last release (this skill's aibom.json, or an SBOM export with a giri-skills:use property per entry); every entry is re-checked against today's policy and catalog. An entry without a use, or of a type outside model/data/library/framework/service, stops the run rather than being guessed or dropped.

When to use

  • ADLC govern stage: before an AI release, or when a model, dataset, library or API is added or upgraded.
  • "Can we ship this?" — every component's licence against the organisation's licence policy, with the use it will be put to.
  • Producing an AI bill of materials in a CycloneDX-shaped JSON for a release record.
  • NOT for: vulnerability or dependency CVE scanning (security-review), finding personal data (pii-data-inventory), choosing a model (model-selection), a legal opinion on a licence (route to Legal counsel).

Inputs

InputRequiredSourceIf missing
bom — component,type,version,license,source_url,use CSV, or an existing CycloneDX JSON BOM (giri-skills:use property per entry)yesengineering lead; model cards, dataset cards, package metadatarun stops (exit 2), asks once

system — AI system namenoproduct ownerreport title TBD (owner: Engineering lead); JSON omits metadata

type: model | dataset | library | service. use: internal | commercial | redistribution. Other values stop the run (exit 2). Blank version or licence → TBD (owner: Engineering lead); a blank licence counts as unknown.

Procedure

  1. Read ../../../shared/quality-bar.md.
  2. List every model, dataset, library and hosted service the AI system depends on, with the licence string exactly as published and the intended use.
  3. Run the skill. scripts/aibom.py normalises each licence through assets/license-catalog.csv (references/method.md); unknown strings stay unknown and go to review.
  4. Decisions come only from the policy. Commercial or redistribution use of a non-commercial licence is denied; Llama's conditional commercial terms turn an allow into a review.
  5. Any deny fails the gate (exit 1). Resolve each Blocked row (replace, relicense, or change use), then re-run.
  6. Send Needs review rows to Legal counsel; ship the Obligations (notices, attribution, flow-down terms) with the release.
  7. Run the self-check.

Output

  • aibom.csv — component, type, version, license_raw, spdx_id, decision, reason, flags, use.
  • aibom.json — CycloneDX-shaped subset (specVersion 1.6): components typed machine-learning-model / data / library, services, licenses (SPDX id or expression; name for unknown), externalReferences, decision/flags in properties.
  • license-report.md — Summary (gate), Components, Blocked, Needs review, Obligations, Method.

Self-check

  • [ ] Every spdx_id is from the catalog or unknown; no licence guessed
  • [ ] Every decision came from the policy, a documented use rule, or is TBD for Legal counsel
  • [ ] Commercial/redistribution use of a non-commercial licence is denied and the run exits 1
  • [ ] aibom.json passes --verify; it is described as a CycloneDX-shaped subset, not a validated SBOM
  • [ ] Obligations listed for every shipped component; limits and "not legal advice" stated

References

  • references/sources.md — SPDX list 3.29.0, publisher licence pages, CycloneDX 1.6 schema, with dates checked
  • references/method.md — normalisation, expressions, decision and use rules, gate
  • assets/license-catalog.csv — SPDX/LicenseRef catalog with flags, obligations and source URL per row
  • assets/license-policy.example.csv — example policy for Legal counsel to replace
  • scripts/aibom.py — checker, CycloneDX writer and --verify (argparse; stdlib)

How to run (automation, when commands can run)

This skill is executable. Collect the inputs below, then run python3 scripts/run_skill.py ai-platform/ai-bom-license-check --input <name>=<value> … --out <dir> (see --explain ai-platform/ai-bom-license-check). Report the run.json results; do not hand-write the deliverables the script produces (aibom.csv, aibom.json, license-report.md). Gate: any denied component fails the run (exit 1) on purpose; all three outputs are still written. Not legal advice.

bodyHtml:
AI SLO Definition

In a conversation: draft the SLO spec now

The reply is the SLO spec draft, never only a request for the log. No log rows are in the conversation, so no observed value is printed; every number the log would give is a marker.

  • The request names the feature and says logs exist ("a week of pilot logs", "here are two days of logs") but no rows are in the conversation: write the spec in this reply, in this order:
    1. Summary — line 1: Status: proposed — no objective is agreed until the Product owner signs it. Then how the objectives are set: scripts/slo.py is run on the pilot log without targets (python3 scripts/run_skill.py ai-platform/ai-slo-definition --input log=<pilot-log.csv> --input system="<feature>" --out <dir>), and each objective is proposed from the observed data.
    2. SLIs and objectives — table sli | good ÷ eligible | proposal rule | objective | threshold | status for the four SLIs: availability (status = ok ÷ every request); latency (ok requests with latency_ms <= threshold; failed requests count against availability only); quality (quality_pass = 1 ÷ labelled rows); cost (cost_usd <= threshold ÷ rows with a cost). Proposal rules from references/method.md: availability and quality take the highest ladder level not above the observed SLI (availability 0.9 / 0.95 / 0.99 / 0.995 / 0.999 / 0.9995 / 0.9999; quality 0.8 / 0.85 / 0.9 / 0.95 / 0.98 / 0.99); latency threshold = observed nearest-rank p95 of ok requests rounded up to the next 100 ms at objective 0.95; cost threshold = observed p95 cost rounded up to the next 0.001 USD at objective 0.95. Every objective cell reads To be baselined · owner: Product owner and every status proposed; none is called agreed. Without quality_pass or cost_usd in the log, that SLI is "not measured" with its owner.
    3. Error budgets — error budget = 1 − objective; budget consumed = (1 − SLI) ÷ (1 − objective); above 1 is breached. Proposals are never gated; only agreed targets are.
    4. Alerting policy — Google SRE workbook multiwindow burn-rate alerts at a 30-day window: fast-burn page 14.4x over 1 h with a 5 m short window (2% of budget); slow-burn page 6x over 6 h / 30 m (5%); ticket 1x over 3 d / 6 h (10%). An alert fires when both windows burn at or above the threshold. The SLO window is To be baselined · owner: SRE lead until agreed; a pilot shorter than 3 days cannot show the ticket window.
    5. Method & limits — nearest-rank percentiles, the log must cover normal traffic, quality depends on labelling; then the next step: take the proposals to the Product owner and SRE lead, then re-run with the agreed targets file (sli,objective,threshold,window_days).
  • Agreed targets and a measurement are asked for ("measure against our targets", "errors spiked — check the SLOs and alerts"): give the same sections with the stated targets as objectives, the observed / consumed / burn columns as To be baselined · owner: SRE lead until the log is run, and state the gate: consumed above 1 on an agreed SLO is breached and the run exits 1 with every output written; a firing alert on an unbreached SLO is at-risk.
  • No feature and no log mentioned at all: ask once, in one list, for the request log (timestamp, latency_ms, status, optional quality_pass, cost_usd), any agreed targets, and the feature name. Do not invent latency, availability or cost figures.
  • Asked to "just set sensible SLOs" or to lower an objective so a breach passes: decline in one line — objectives come from observed data and the Product owner's agreement, not from typical industry numbers, and a breached objective is not lowered to pass the gate without the Product owner. Never print a suggested target number; show To be baselined · owner: Product owner and the proposal rules above.
  • Distribution drift ("have our confidence scores shifted since launch?"): that is drift-monitor; this skill measures SLIs against objectives.

Starting points

  • New — no SLOs yet: bring a pilot request log; every objective is proposed from the observed data and marked for the Product owner to agree.
  • Existing — bring the production request log and the targets already agreed; the skill measures each SLI against them, computes budget burn and flags breaches.

When to use

  • ADLC requirements stage: turn "it should be fast and reliable" into measurable SLIs, objectives and error budgets before build sign-off.
  • Drafting first objectives from a pilot or shadow log: the skill proposes them from observed data for the Product owner to accept or change.
  • Checking a release or a week of traffic against agreed targets, and wiring the burn-rate alert policy.
  • NOT for: dashboards, trace schemas and live monitoring (llm-observability); input or score drift (drift-monitor); monthly API spend forecasts (llm-cost-model); judging answer quality itself (llm-eval-harness produces the quality_pass labels).

Inputs

InputRequiredSourceIf missing
log — request log CSVyesplatform / API gateway logs (copy assets/log-template.csv)run stops (exit 2), asks once
targets — sli,objective,threshold,window_daysnoProduct owner + SRE lead (copy assets/targets-template.csv)objectives proposed from the data, each To be baselined · owner: Product owner; never presented as agreed
system — feature namenoProduct ownertitle reads "AI feature"

An SLI with an agreed target but no eligible rows in the log exits 2. Without quality_pass or cost_usd values, those SLIs are listed as not measured with a named owner.

Procedure

  1. Read ../../../shared/quality-bar.md.
  2. Confirm the log covers normal traffic (ideally several days; the 6 h and 3 d alert windows need that much history).
  3. Run without targets first if none are agreed; take the proposals to the Product owner and SRE lead.
  4. Run with the agreed targets. scripts/slo.py applies references/method.md.
  5. Read Summary, then Error budgets (consumed > 1 is breached), then Alerting policy (which alerts fire now).

# AI SLO Definition

## In a conversation: draft the SLO spec now
The reply **is the SLO spec draft**, never only a request for the log. No log rows are in the conversation, so no observed value is printed; every number the log would give is a marker.
- **The request names the feature and says logs exist** ("a week of pilot logs", "here are two days of logs") but no rows are in the conversation: write the spec **in this reply**, in this order:
  1. **Summary** — line 1: `Status: proposed — no objective is agreed until the Product owner signs it.` Then how the objectives are set: `scripts/slo.py` is run on the pilot log **without targets** (`python3 scripts/run_skill.py ai-platform/ai-slo-definition --input log=<pilot-log.csv> --input system="<feature>" --out <dir>`), and each objective is proposed from the observed data.
  2. **SLIs and objectives** — table `sli | good ÷ eligible | proposal rule | objective | threshold | status` for the four SLIs: availability (`status = ok` ÷ every request); latency (ok requests with `latency_ms <= threshold`; failed requests count against availability only); quality (`quality_pass = 1` ÷ labelled rows); cost (`cost_usd <= threshold` ÷ rows with a cost). Proposal rules from `references/method.md`: availability and quality take the highest ladder level not above the observed SLI (availability `0.9 / 0.95 / 0.99 / 0.995 / 0.999 / 0.9995 / 0.9999`; quality `0.8 / 0.85 / 0.9 / 0.95 / 0.98 / 0.99`); latency threshold = observed nearest-rank p95 of ok requests rounded up to the next 100 ms at objective 0.95; cost threshold = observed p95 cost rounded up to the next 0.001 USD at objective 0.95. Every objective cell reads `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: Product owner]` and every status `proposed`; none is called agreed. Without `quality_pass` or `cost_usd` in the log, that SLI is "not measured" with its owner.
  3. **Error budgets** — error budget = 1 − objective; budget consumed = (1 − SLI) ÷ (1 − objective); above 1 is breached. Proposals are never gated; only agreed targets are.
  4. **Alerting policy** — Google SRE workbook multiwindow burn-rate alerts at a 30-day window: fast-burn page 14.4x over 1 h with a 5 m short window (2% of budget); slow-burn page 6x over 6 h / 30 m (5%); ticket 1x over 3 d / 6 h (10%). An alert fires when both windows burn at or above the threshold. The SLO window is `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: SRE lead]` until agreed; a pilot shorter than 3 days cannot show the ticket window.
  5. **Method & limits** — nearest-rank percentiles, the log must cover normal traffic, quality depends on labelling; then the next step: take the proposals to the Product owner and SRE lead, then re-run with the agreed `targets` file (`sli,objective,threshold,window_days`).
- **Agreed targets and a measurement are asked for** ("measure against our targets", "errors spiked — check the SLOs and alerts"): give the same sections with the stated targets as objectives, the observed / consumed / burn columns as `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: SRE lead]` until the log is run, and state the gate: consumed above 1 on an agreed SLO is breached and the run exits 1 with every output written; a firing alert on an unbreached SLO is at-risk.
- **No feature and no log mentioned at all**: ask once, in one list, for the request log (`timestamp, latency_ms, status`, optional `quality_pass`, `cost_usd`), any agreed targets, and the feature name. Do not invent latency, availability or cost figures.
- **Asked to "just set sensible SLOs" or to lower an objective so a breach passes**: decline in one line — objectives come from observed data and the Product owner's agreement, not from typical industry numbers, and a breached objective is not lowered to pass the gate without the Product owner. Never print a suggested target number; show `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: Product owner]` and the proposal rules above.
- **Distribution drift** ("have our confidence scores shifted since launch?"): that is `drift-monitor`; this skill measures SLIs against objectives.

## Starting points
- **New** — no SLOs yet: bring a pilot request log; every objective is proposed from the observed data and marked for the Product owner to agree.
- **Existing** — bring the production request log and the targets already agreed; the skill measures each SLI against them, computes budget burn and flags breaches.

## When to use
- ADLC requirements stage: turn "it should be fast and reliable" into measurable SLIs, objectives and error budgets before build sign-off.
- Drafting first objectives from a pilot or shadow log: the skill proposes them from observed data for the Product owner to accept or change.
- Checking a release or a week of traffic against agreed targets, and wiring the burn-rate alert policy.
- NOT for: dashboards, trace schemas and live monitoring (`llm-observability`); input or score drift (`drift-monitor`); monthly API spend forecasts (`llm-cost-model`); judging answer quality itself (`llm-eval-harness` produces the `quality_pass` labels).

## Inputs
| Input | Required | Source | If missing |
|---|---|---|---|
| `log` — request log CSV | yes | platform / API gateway logs (copy `assets/log-template.csv`) | run stops (exit 2), asks once |
| `targets` — `sli,objective,threshold,window_days` | no | Product owner + SRE lead (copy `assets/targets-template.csv`) | objectives proposed from the data, each `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: Product owner]`; never presented as agreed |
| `system` — feature name | no | Product owner | title reads "AI feature" |

An SLI with an agreed target but no eligible rows in the log exits 2. Without `quality_pass` or `cost_usd` values, those SLIs are listed as not measured with a named owner.

## Procedure
1. Read `../../../shared/quality-bar.md`.
2. Confirm the log covers normal traffic (ideally several days; the 6 h and 3 d alert windows need that much history).
3. Run without `targets` first if none are agreed; take the proposals to the Product owner and SRE lead.
4. Run with the agreed `targets`. `scripts/slo.py` applies `references/method.md`.
5. Read Summary, then Error budgets (consumed > 1 is breached), then Alerting policy (which alerts fire now).
6. On exit 1: open an incident or a reliability work item for each breached SLI; do not lower the objective to pass the gate without the Product owner.
7. Run the self-check.

## Output
- `slos.csv` — `sli, objective, threshold, observed, budget_consumed, burn_rate, status, note` (burn_rate = last 1 h; status met | at-risk | breached | proposed).
- `slo-spec.md` — **Summary**, **SLIs and objectives**, **Error budgets**, **Alerting policy** (burn per window, thresholds, fires), **Method**.
- `slo.json` — exact counts and fractions per SLI and window, verdict.

## Self-check
- [ ] Every observed value comes from the log; percentiles are nearest-rank
- [ ] Every proposed objective carries `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: Product owner]`; none is called agreed
- [ ] Burn-rate thresholds and windows match `references/sources.md` (SRE workbook, checked 2026-10-18)
- [ ] A breached agreed SLO exits 1 with full outputs
- [ ] Limits stated: sample log, short logs cannot show long windows, quality depends on labelling

## References
- `references/method.md` — SLI definitions, budget and burn formulas, proposal rules, hand-checked worked example
- `references/sources.md` — Google SRE workbook burn-rate policy with URL and date checked
- `assets/targets-template.csv`, `assets/log-template.csv` — input layouts
- `scripts/slo.py` — calculator and `--verify` (argparse; stdlib; exit 0 / 1 breached / 2 input)

## How to run (automation, when commands can run)

Collect the inputs below, then run `python3 scripts/run_skill.py ai-platform/ai-slo-definition --input <name>=<value> … --out <dir>` (see `--explain ai-platform/ai-slo-definition`). An agreed SLO with budget consumed above 1 fails the run (exit 1) on purpose, with every output still written. Both tabular outputs pass `--verify`, which recomputes budgets, alerts and statuses from the counts in `slo.json`.

bodyHtml:
AI Transparency Notice (user notice, system card, Art. 50 checklist)

In a conversation: write the notice and checklist now

The reply is the transparency pack draft, never only a request for the facts CSV. Facts the user states fill the templates; every other fact is a marker, never typical wording.

  • The request names the system and its situation (e.g. "billing chatbot launching in the EU") but the facts CSV and classification.json are not in the conversation: write, in this reply, in this order:
    1. How it is produced — one line: the Product owner fills assets/facts-template.csv (each row with a source); optionally pass classification.json from eu-ai-act-classifier; run python3 scripts/run_skill.py ai-platform/ai-transparency-notice --input facts=<facts.csv> [--input classification=<classification.json>] --out <dir>.
    2. User notice — the sentences from assets/notice-sentences.csv, one per line, each tagged with the fact it traces to: "You are chatting with {system_name}. It is an AI system, not a person." / "{provider} runs it." / "It is here to {purpose}." / "It uses {data_sources}." / "It is not for {not_intended_for}." / "Keep in mind that it {known_limitations}." / "People stay in charge: {human_oversight}." / "Questions? Contact {contact}." / "Last updated: {last_updated}." — plus the synthetic, deep_fake, emotion, biometric sentences only when that yes/no fact is yes. Fill a placeholder only from a stated fact; otherwise To be baselined · owner: Product owner.
    3. Reading grade — Flesch-Kincaid grade against the ceiling (max_grade, default 8). Report it as [TO BE BASELINED — computed by the run] while placeholders remain; above the ceiling the run exits 1 and the long facts are rewritten, not the notice.
    4. Art. 50 disclosure checklist — table duty | article | addressee | applies | provided | status | owner with the seven rows from assets/art50-duties.csv: interaction (Art. 50(1), Product owner), synthetic-content marking (Art. 50(2), Engineering lead), emotion recognition and biometric categorisation (Art. 50(3), Privacy officer), deep fake and public-interest text (Art. 50(4), Content lead), timing and accessibility (Art. 50(5), Product owner). applies follows the yes/no fact (unknown → to confirm); status is provided / partial / missing / to confirm / not applicable; Art. 50(5) is at most partial (placement and grade only).
    5. System card outline — Overview (with classification, else To be baselined · owner: Compliance lead), Intended use, Not intended for, Data, Model, Human oversight, Limitations, Contact, Change log.
    6. Limits — this is not a legal determination and claims no compliance; exemptions are not assessed; counsel reviews the checklist before launch.
  • Only some facts are known ("we only know the name, provider and purpose — fill the rest with typical wording"): fill those three, mark every other fact To be baselined · owner: Product owner and the classification for the Compliance lead; say in one line that wording is not invented because each notice sentence must trace to a fact.
  • No system named at all: ask once, in one list, for the facts in assets/facts-template.csv (name, provider, purpose, data sources, oversight, limitations, not-intended-for, contact, the yes/no flags, notice placement) and the classifier output.
  • Asked to state that the system is compliant or to drop a checklist row: decline in one line — the checklist records evidence and owners, and compliance is a legal determination for counsel.

Starting points

  • New: the system's facts (and the classifier output) give the user notice, the system card and the Art. 50 checklist.
  • Existing: add the notice users see today (published_notice); notice-redline.md marks each sentence unchanged, changed, added or removed, and every removed sentence is a published claim the facts no longer support.

When to use

  • ADLC deploy stage: before users first see an AI assistant, chatbot or content generator.
  • "What do we tell users, and what does Article 50 expect us to disclose?" — notice plus a duty-by-duty checklist with evidence and owners.
  • Reviewer pack: a system card whose every row cites the source of the fact.
  • NOT for: deciding the EU AI Act risk tier (eu-ai-act-classifier), the risk register (ai-governance-risk), staged rollout (ai-release-plan), legal sign-off (route to counsel — this skill never claims compliance).

Inputs

InputRequiredSourceIf missing
facts — kv-csv key,value,source,notesyesProduct owner (copy assets/facts-template.csv)run stops (exit 2), asks once
classification — classification.jsonnooutput of ai-platform/eu-ai-act-classifiersystem card classification line is To be baselined · owner: Compliance lead
max_grade — reading gradenoaccessibility or brand standard8
strict — true/falsenorelease ownerfalse: notice written with TBD markers, exit 0

Each missing fact is To be baselined · owner: Product owner in the card and notice. Yes/no facts (generates_synthetic_content, emotion_recognition, biometric_categorisation, interacts_directly, deep_fake, public_interest_text) accept only yes or no; anything else exits 2.

Procedure

  1. Read ../../../shared/quality-bar.md.
  2. The Product owner fills assets/facts-template.csv, writing each fact as a plain phrase that completes its template sentence, with a source for every row.
  3. Optionally run ai-platform/eu-ai-act-classifier first and pass its classification.json.
  4. Run the agent. scripts/transparency_notice.py assembles the notice from assets/notice-sentences.csv, grades it (references/readability.md), writes the system card and evaluates assets/art50-duties.csv (references/method.md).
  5. Grade above max_grade → exit 1: rewrite the long facts, not the notice.
  6. Work every missing and to confirm checklist row with its owner. Treat partial on Art. 50(5) as a prompt for an accessibility review.
  7. Have counsel review the checklist before launch; run the self-check.

Output

  • notice.md — the user-facing notice (one sentence per line, ≤ 15 sentences).
  • system-card.md — Overview (with classification), Intended use, Not intended for, Data, Model, Human oversight, Limitations, Contact, Change log (grade, checklist counts, facts not supplied).
  • disclosure-checklist.csv — duty, article, addressee, applies, provided, status, evidence, owner.
  • transparency.json — grade, max_grade, grade_ok, word_count, sentence_count, syllable_count, notice_sentences, notice_missing_facts, missing_facts, checklist counts, classification.

Self-check

  • [ ] Every notice sentence comes from a template and a fact; --verify re-grades notice.md to the same numbers
  • [ ] Grade within max_grade, or the run failed and says so
  • [ ] Every checklist row has an owner; nothing says "compliant"
  • [ ] Missing facts are TBD for the Product owner; missing classification is TBD for the Compliance lead
  • [ ] Limits stated: heuristic syllable count, exemptions not assessed, not a legal determination

References

  • references/sources.md — Article 50, 111(4), 113 text checked 2026-10-18; Flesch–Kincaid source
  • references/readability.md — grade formula, syllable heuristic and its limits
  • references/method.md — notice assembly, card rules, checklist rules
  • assets/facts-template.csv, assets/notice-sentences.csv, assets/art50-duties.csv — input layout, templates, duty catalog
  • scripts/transparency_notice.py — builder and --verify (argparse; stdlib)

How to run (automation, when commands can run)

This skill is executable. Collect the inputs below, then run python3 scripts/run_skill.py ai-platform/ai-transparency-notice --input <name>=<value> … --out <dir> (see --explain ai-platform/ai-transparency-notice). Report the run.json results; do not hand-write the deliverables the script produces (notice.md, system-card.md, disclosure-checklist.csv, transparency.json). A notice above the reading-grade ceiling fails the run (exit 1) on purpose; every output is still written so the facts can be rewritten in plainer words.

bodyMd:
# AI Transparency Notice (user notice, system card, Art. 50 checklist)

## In a conversation: write the notice and checklist now
The reply **is the transparency pack draft**, never only a request for the facts CSV. Facts the user states fill the templates; every other fact is a marker, never typical wording.
- **The request names the system and its situation** (e.g. "billing chatbot launching in the EU") but the facts CSV and `classification.json` are not in the conversation: write, **in this reply**, in this order:
  1. **How it is produced** — one line: the Product owner fills `assets/facts-template.csv` (each row with a source); optionally pass `classification.json` from `eu-ai-act-classifier`; run `python3 scripts/run_skill.py ai-platform/ai-transparency-notice --input facts=<facts.csv> [--input classification=<classification.json>] --out <dir>`.
  2. **User notice** — the sentences from `assets/notice-sentences.csv`, one per line, each tagged with the fact it traces to: "You are chatting with {system_name}. It is an AI system, not a person." / "{provider} runs it." / "It is here to {purpose}." / "It uses {data_sources}." / "It is not for {not_intended_for}." / "Keep in mind that it {known_limitations}." / "People stay in charge: {human_oversight}." / "Questions? Contact {contact}." / "Last updated: {last_updated}." — plus the `synthetic`, `deep_fake`, `emotion`, `biometric` sentences only when that yes/no fact is yes. Fill a placeholder only from a stated fact; otherwise `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: Product owner]`.
  3. **Reading grade** — Flesch-Kincaid grade against the ceiling (`max_grade`, default 8). Report it as `[TO BE BASELINED — computed by the run]` while placeholders remain; above the ceiling the run exits 1 and the long facts are rewritten, not the notice.
  4. **Art. 50 disclosure checklist** — table `duty | article | addressee | applies | provided | status | owner` with the seven rows from `assets/art50-duties.csv`: interaction (Art. 50(1), Product owner), synthetic-content marking (Art. 50(2), Engineering lead), emotion recognition and biometric categorisation (Art. 50(3), Privacy officer), deep fake and public-interest text (Art. 50(4), Content lead), timing and accessibility (Art. 50(5), Product owner). `applies` follows the yes/no fact (unknown → `to confirm`); status is provided / partial / missing / to confirm / not applicable; Art. 50(5) is at most `partial` (placement and grade only).
  5. **System card outline** — Overview (with classification, else `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: Compliance lead]`), Intended use, Not intended for, Data, Model, Human oversight, Limitations, Contact, Change log.
  6. **Limits** — this is not a legal determination and claims no compliance; exemptions are not assessed; counsel reviews the checklist before launch.
- **Only some facts are known** ("we only know the name, provider and purpose — fill the rest with typical wording"): fill those three, mark every other fact `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: Product owner]` and the classification for the Compliance lead; say in one line that wording is not invented because each notice sentence must trace to a fact.
- **No system named at all**: ask once, in one list, for the facts in `assets/facts-template.csv` (name, provider, purpose, data sources, oversight, limitations, not-intended-for, contact, the yes/no flags, notice placement) and the classifier output.
- **Asked to state that the system is compliant** or to drop a checklist row: decline in one line — the checklist records evidence and owners, and compliance is a legal determination for counsel.

## Starting points
- **New:** the system's facts (and the classifier output) give the user notice, the system card and the Art. 50 checklist.
- **Existing:** add the notice users see today (`published_notice`); notice-redline.md marks each sentence unchanged, changed, added or removed, and every removed sentence is a published claim the facts no longer support.

## When to use
- ADLC deploy stage: before users first see an AI assistant, chatbot or content generator.
- "What do we tell users, and what does Article 50 expect us to disclose?" — notice plus a duty-by-duty checklist with evidence and owners.
- Reviewer pack: a system card whose every row cites the source of the fact.
- NOT for: deciding the EU AI Act risk tier (`eu-ai-act-classifier`), the risk register (`ai-governance-risk`), staged rollout (`ai-release-plan`), legal sign-off (route to counsel — this skill never claims compliance).

## Inputs
| Input | Required | Source | If missing |
|---|---|---|---|
| `facts` — kv-csv `key,value,source,notes` | yes | Product owner (copy `assets/facts-template.csv`) | run stops (exit 2), asks once |
| `classification` — `classification.json` | no | output of `ai-platform/eu-ai-act-classifier` | system card classification line is `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: Compliance lead]` |
| `max_grade` — reading grade | no | accessibility or brand standard | 8 |
| `strict` — true/false | no | release owner | false: notice written with TBD markers, exit 0 |

Each missing fact is `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: Product owner]` in the card and notice. Yes/no facts (`generates_synthetic_content`, `emotion_recognition`, `biometric_categorisation`, `interacts_directly`, `deep_fake`, `public_interest_text`) accept only yes or no; anything else exits 2.

## Procedure
1. Read `../../../shared/quality-bar.md`.
2. The Product owner fills `assets/facts-template.csv`, writing each fact as a plain phrase that completes its template sentence, with a source for every row.
3. Optionally run `ai-platform/eu-ai-act-classifier` first and pass its `classification.json`.
4. Run the agent. `scripts/transparency_notice.py` assembles the notice from `assets/notice-sentences.csv`, grades it (`references/readability.md`), writes the system card and evaluates `assets/art50-duties.csv` (`references/method.md`).
5. Grade above `max_grade` → exit 1: rewrite the long facts, not the notice.
6. Work every `missing` and `to confirm` checklist row with its owner. Treat `partial` on Art. 50(5) as a prompt for an accessibility review.
7. Have counsel review the checklist before launch; run the self-check.

## Output
- `notice.md` — the user-facing notice (one sentence per line, ≤ 15 sentences).
- `system-card.md` — Overview (with classification), Intended use, Not intended for, Data, Model, Human oversight, Limitations, Contact, Change log (grade, checklist counts, facts not supplied).
- `disclosure-checklist.csv` — `duty, article, addressee, applies, provided, status, evidence, owner`.
- `transparency.json` — `grade`, `max_grade`, `grade_ok`, `word_count`, `sentence_count`, `syllable_count`, `notice_sentences`, `notice_missing_facts`, `missing_facts`, checklist counts, classification.

## Self-check
- [ ] Every notice sentence comes from a template and a fact; `--verify` re-grades `notice.md` to the same numbers
- [ ] Grade within `max_grade`, or the run failed and says so
- [ ] Every checklist row has an owner; nothing says "compliant"
- [ ] Missing facts are TBD for the Product owner; missing classification is TBD for the Compliance lead
- [ ] Limits stated: heuristic syllable count, exemptions not assessed, not a legal determination

## References
- `references/sources.md` — Article 50, 111(4), 113 text checked 2026-10-18; Flesch–Kincaid source
- `references/readability.md` — grade formula, syllable heuristic and its limits
- `references/method.md` — notice assembly, card rules, checklist rules
- `assets/facts-template.csv`, `assets/notice-sentences.csv`, `assets/art50-duties.csv` — input layout, templates, duty catalog
- `scripts/transparency_notice.py` — builder and `--verify` (argparse; stdlib)

## How to run (automation, when commands can run)
This skill is executable. Collect the inputs below, then run `python3 scripts/run_skill.py ai-platform/ai-transparency-notice --input <name>=<value> … --out <dir>` (see `--explain ai-platform/ai-transparency-notice`). Report the `run.json` results; do not hand-write the deliverables the script produces (`notice.md`, `system-card.md`, `disclosure-checklist.csv`, `transparency.json`). A notice above the reading-grade ceiling fails the run (exit 1) on purpose; every output is still written so the facts can be rewritten in plainer words.

bodyHtml:
AI Vendor Assessment (weighted scoring + third-party AI risk)

In a conversation: score the vendors now

The reply is the assessment (or its skeleton): line 1 is Recommendation: <option> | no clear winner | pending — <reason>, never only a request for files. It corresponds to python3 -I scripts/vendor_assess.py --options <file> --criteria <file> [--risk <file>] [--previous <file>] [--require-clear-winner] --out-dir <out>, which writes scores.csv, sensitivity.csv and vendor-report.md; name that command (with the case's flags) and those files. Say: "a decision aid, not a contract or legal review; vendor claims are recorded, not verified; a missing score is never imputed".

Never

  • Never invent or propose weights ("use whatever weights make sense"): weights come from the decision owner (sponsor). No criteria file → ask once for criterion,weight,description; the run stops (exit 2). Do not compute a ranking.
  • Never impute a blank score: the option is complete = no, has no weighted score or rank, is excluded from the recommendation; gap To be baselined · owner: Procurement lead.
  • Never assume a risk answer ("assume the big vendors are compliant"): risk reads not assessed To be baselined · owner: Third-party risk manager; recommendation Conditional on a third-party risk review To be baselined · owner: Third-party risk manager.
  • Never treat unknown as a red flag: it is unanswered (owner Third-party risk manager). n/a is not applicable.
  • Never use last year's scores in today's scores.

Procedure — compute row by row from the supplied files, never estimate

  1. Weights: w_c = raw_c ÷ Σ raw (state "normalised to 1.000" and the raw sum).
  2. Complete options = a 1-5 score for every criterion. Score outside 1-5, unknown criterion or duplicate row → stops (exit 2).
  3. Weighted score = Σ w_c × score, 3 dp (compare at full precision). Rank descending; equal scores share a rank.
  4. Sensitivity: for each criterion and factor 0.8 then 1.2, multiply that raw weight only, renormalise (new sum), rescore complete options. top_changed = yes if the first option differs from the baseline first or first place ties. Rank stability % = runs with no ÷ (2 × criteria) × 100. Show all 2 × criteria runs in a table: criterion | change | weight_after | top | top_score | runner_up | margin | top_changed.
  5. Red flags per option from assets/third-party-ai-risk-questions.csv: TPR-01 eq:yes (trains on customer data) · TPR-02 retention gt:30 days · TPR-03 residency eq:no · TPR-04 sub-processors eq:no · TPR-05 SOC 2 eq:no · TPR-06 ISO/IEC 27001 eq:no · TPR-07 ISO/IEC 42001 eq:no (in_progress is not red) · TPR-08 model-change notice lt:30 days · TPR-09 incident notice gt:72 hours · TPR-10 IP indemnity eq:no · TPR-11 exit eq:no. Blank/no row/unknown = unanswered.
  6. Recommendation: clear winner = baseline top complete option that is not tied, has no red flags and is first in every sensitivity run. Otherwise **No clear winner.** Reasons: … (tie / "top-scoring X has red flags: TPR-nn" / "the top option changes under <criterion> <±20%>") and name the highest-scoring option without red flags. With require_clear_winner, no clear winner → run stops (exit 1), outputs still written; say "stops (exit 1)". Without it, no clear winner is exit 0.
  7. Previous (scores.csv from the last assessment): per option score then, now, change (now − then, signed 3 dp), rank then, now, red flags raised and cleared; options absent last time = new option; options only in the previous file = no longer assessed.

Reply layout

  1. Working table first: option | score per criterion | Σ w × score (shown) | weighted score | rank | complete | red flags | unanswered. Then the sensitivity table and stability %, then the risk table per option, then the Recommendation, then Changes since last assessment (when previous is given), then Method/limits.

No scores or weights in the conversation (options named, or files said to be attached): lay out the same sections now — one Scores row per option with each cell To be baselined · owner: Procurement lead, the sensitivity table columns, the 11-question risk checklist per option with To be baselined · owner: Third-party risk manager — and say scripts/vendor_assess.py will compute weighted scores, ±20% sensitivity, rank stability and red flags. Ask once, in one list, for the scores CSV with sources (option,criterion,score,source), the criteria weights CSV from the decision owner, and the risk answers (option,question_id,answer,evidence).

Choosing an LLM on eval scores, token prices and latency: line 1 routes it to model-selection; offer this skill for vendor, contract and third-party risk comparison.

Starting points

  • New: a shortlist scored on your weighted criteria, with risk answers, gives the ranking, sensitivity and red flags before procurement.
  • Existing: add the scores.csv from the last assessment (previous), e.g. at renewal; the report adds each option's score and rank then and now, red flags raised or cleared, and options new or no longer assessed.

When to use

  • ADLC strategy stage: a shortlist of AI vendors, platforms or providers (and possibly an in-house build) must be compared on agreed criteria before procurement.
  • "Does the winner survive if we weight cost higher?" — the ±20% sensitivity answers it per criterion.
  • Third-party AI risk screen before contract: red flags on data use, retention, residency, assurance, change notice, incident SLA, indemnity and exit.
  • NOT for: choosing a model from eval scores, prices and latency (model-selection), forecasting token spend (llm-cost-model), legal contract review or drafting, or verifying vendor certificates (inspect the reports themselves).

criteria — criterion, weight, descriptionyesdecision owner (sponsor)run stops (exit 2), asks once

# AI Vendor Assessment (weighted scoring + third-party AI risk)

## In a conversation: score the vendors now
The reply **is the assessment** (or its skeleton): line 1 is `Recommendation: <option> | no clear winner | pending — <reason>`, never only a request for files. It corresponds to `python3 -I scripts/vendor_assess.py --options <file> --criteria <file> [--risk <file>] [--previous <file>] [--require-clear-winner] --out-dir <out>`, which writes `scores.csv`, `sensitivity.csv` and `vendor-report.md`; name that command (with the case's flags) and those files. Say: "a decision aid, not a contract or legal review; vendor claims are recorded, not verified; a missing score is never imputed".

**Never**
- Never invent or propose weights ("use whatever weights make sense"): weights come from the decision owner (sponsor). No criteria file → ask once for `criterion,weight,description`; the run **stops (exit 2)**. Do not compute a ranking.
- Never impute a blank score: the option is `complete = no`, has no weighted score or rank, is excluded from the recommendation; gap `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: Procurement lead]`.
- Never assume a risk answer ("assume the big vendors are compliant"): risk reads `not assessed [TO BE BASELINED — owner: Third-party risk manager]`; recommendation `Conditional on a third-party risk review [TO BE BASELINED — owner: Third-party risk manager].`
- Never treat `unknown` as a red flag: it is unanswered (owner Third-party risk manager). `n/a` is not applicable.
- Never use last year's scores in today's scores.

**Procedure — compute row by row from the supplied files, never estimate**
1. Weights: w_c = raw_c ÷ Σ raw (state "normalised to 1.000" and the raw sum).
2. Complete options = a 1-5 score for every criterion. Score outside 1-5, unknown criterion or duplicate row → **stops (exit 2)**.
3. Weighted score = Σ w_c × score, 3 dp (compare at full precision). Rank descending; equal scores share a rank.
4. Sensitivity: for each criterion and factor 0.8 then 1.2, multiply that raw weight only, renormalise (new sum), rescore complete options. `top_changed = yes` if the first option differs from the baseline first or first place ties. Rank stability % = runs with `no` ÷ (2 × criteria) × 100. Show all 2 × criteria runs in a table: `criterion | change | weight_after | top | top_score | runner_up | margin | top_changed`.
5. Red flags per option from `assets/third-party-ai-risk-questions.csv`: TPR-01 eq:yes (trains on customer data) · TPR-02 retention gt:30 days · TPR-03 residency eq:no · TPR-04 sub-processors eq:no · TPR-05 SOC 2 eq:no · TPR-06 ISO/IEC 27001 eq:no · TPR-07 ISO/IEC 42001 eq:no (`in_progress` is not red) · TPR-08 model-change notice lt:30 days · TPR-09 incident notice gt:72 hours · TPR-10 IP indemnity eq:no · TPR-11 exit eq:no. Blank/no row/`unknown` = unanswered.
6. Recommendation: clear winner = baseline top complete option that is not tied, has no red flags and is first in every sensitivity run. Otherwise `**No clear winner.** Reasons: …` (tie / "top-scoring X has red flags: TPR-nn" / "the top option changes under <criterion> <±20%>") and name the highest-scoring option without red flags. With `require_clear_winner`, no clear winner → run **stops (exit 1)**, outputs still written; say "stops (exit 1)". Without it, no clear winner is exit 0.
7. Previous (`scores.csv` from the last assessment): per option score then, now, change (now − then, signed 3 dp), rank then, now, red flags raised and cleared; options absent last time = `new option`; options only in the previous file = `no longer assessed`.

**Reply layout**
1. Working table first: `option | score per criterion | Σ w × score (shown) | weighted score | rank | complete | red flags | unanswered`. Then the sensitivity table and stability %, then the risk table per option, then the Recommendation, then **Changes since last assessment** (when `previous` is given), then Method/limits.

**No scores or weights in the conversation** (options named, or files said to be attached): lay out the same sections now — one Scores row per option with each cell `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: Procurement lead]`, the sensitivity table columns, the 11-question risk checklist per option with `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: Third-party risk manager]` — and say `scripts/vendor_assess.py` will compute weighted scores, ±20% sensitivity, rank stability and red flags. Ask once, in one list, for the scores CSV with sources (`option,criterion,score,source`), the criteria weights CSV from the decision owner, and the risk answers (`option,question_id,answer,evidence`).

**Choosing an LLM on eval scores, token prices and latency**: line 1 routes it to `model-selection`; offer this skill for vendor, contract and third-party risk comparison.

## Starting points
- **New:** a shortlist scored on your weighted criteria, with risk answers, gives the ranking, sensitivity and red flags before procurement.
- **Existing:** add the `scores.csv` from the last assessment (`previous`), e.g. at renewal; the report adds each option's score and rank then and now, red flags raised or cleared, and options new or no longer assessed.

## When to use
- ADLC strategy stage: a shortlist of AI vendors, platforms or providers (and possibly an in-house build) must be compared on agreed criteria before procurement.
- "Does the winner survive if we weight cost higher?" — the ±20% sensitivity answers it per criterion.
- Third-party AI risk screen before contract: red flags on data use, retention, residency, assurance, change notice, incident SLA, indemnity and exit.
- NOT for: choosing a model from eval scores, prices and latency (`model-selection`), forecasting token spend (`llm-cost-model`), legal contract review or drafting, or verifying vendor certificates (inspect the reports themselves).

## Inputs
| Input | Required | Source | If missing |
|---|---|---|---|
| `options` — option, criterion, score 1–5, source | yes | evaluation team; one row per option × criterion | run stops (exit 2), asks once |
| `criteria` — criterion, weight, description | yes | decision owner (sponsor) | run stops (exit 2), asks once |
| `risk` — option, question_id, answer, evidence | no | Third-party risk manager from vendor responses | risk "not assessed" `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: Third-party risk manager]`; recommendation is conditional |
| `questions` — questionnaire with thresholds | no | Third-party risk manager (copy the shipped file) | shipped defaults (30-day retention, 30-day change notice, 72-hour incident notice) |
| `require_clear_winner` — true/false | no | decision owner | false: "no clear winner" exits 0 |

A blank score is missing: the option is marked incomplete, excluded from ranking and recommendation, and the gap is `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: Procurement lead]`. A score outside 1–5, an unknown criterion or a duplicate row stops the run (exit 2).

## Procedure
1. Read `../../../shared/quality-bar.md`.
2. Agree criteria and weights with the decision owner before scoring; record a source for every score.
3. Send vendors `assets/third-party-ai-risk-questions.csv`; record answers (and `n/a` for a build option) in the risk CSV.
4. Run the agent. `scripts/vendor_assess.py` normalises weights, scores complete options, runs ±20% sensitivity per criterion and applies the red-flag rules (`references/method.md`).
5. If there is no clear winner, take the stated reasons to the decision owner (re-score, renegotiate terms, or re-weight) and re-run.
6. Run the self-check.

## Output
- `scores.csv` — `option, weighted_score, rank, complete, red_flags, missing_criteria, risk_unanswered` (ranked complete options first, then incomplete ones).
- `sensitivity.csv` — `criterion, change, weight_before, weight_after, top_option, top_score, runner_up, margin, top_changed` (two rows per criterion).
- `vendor-report.md` — **Summary**, **Scores** (with score matrix), **Sensitivity**, **Third-party risk**, **Recommendation**, **Method**.

## Self-check
- [ ] Every score has a source; no score was imputed
- [ ] Weights normalisation is stated
- [ ] The recommendation is a complete option with no red flags that stays first under every ±20% change — or "no clear winner" with reasons
- [ ] Unanswered risk questions and incomplete options name an owner
- [ ] Limits stated: decision aid, not a legal or contract review; vendor claims not verified

## References
- `references/method.md` — scoring, ranking, sensitivity, red-flag and recommendation rules
- `references/sources.md` — standards named in the questionnaire, with URLs and dates checked
- `assets/third-party-ai-risk-questions.csv` — 11 questions with answer types and red-flag rules
- `assets/options-template.csv`, `assets/criteria-template.csv`, `assets/risk-template.csv` — input layouts
- `scripts/vendor_assess.py` — scorer and `--verify` mode (argparse; stdlib)

## How to run (automation, when commands can run)
This skill is executable. Collect the inputs below, then run `python3 scripts/run_skill.py ai-platform/ai-vendor-assessment --input <name>=<value> … --out <dir>` (see `--explain ai-platform/ai-vendor-assessment`). Report the `run.json` results; do not hand-write the deliverables the script produces (`scores.csv`, `sensitivity.csv`, `vendor-report.md`). "No clear winner" is a finding, not a failure (exit 0) unless `require_clear_winner=true`, which makes it a gate (exit 1, outputs still written).

In a conversation: write the agreement assessment now

The reply is the agreement assessment draft, never only a request for the CSV. No label rows are in the conversation, so no alpha, kappa or count is printed; each is a marker until the run.

  • The request describes a labelling round (annotators, items, label set, purpose) but the labels are not in the conversation: write the report skeleton in this reply, in the order of agreement-report.md:
    1. Summary — gate verdict first: Gate: not set — the minimum alpha is the data owner's decision (ask them for it; never choose one), or the stated minimum against alpha [TO BE BASELINED — computed by the run]. Line 2: how it is computed — export one row per rating as item_id, annotator, label and run scripts/agreement.py (python3 scripts/run_skill.py ai-platform/annotation-agreement --input labels=<labels.csv> [--input guidelines=<guidelines.md>] [--input min_agreement=<alpha>] --out <dir>).
    2. Agreement — Krippendorff's alpha (nominal) is the headline; then percent agreement, pairwise Cohen's kappa per annotator pair and Fleiss' kappa (n/a with the reason when items have different numbers of ratings). State the interpretation bands as conventions, not tests: Krippendorff ≥ 0.800 commonly relied on, 0.667–0.800 tentative conclusions only, < 0.667 discard; Landis & Koch for kappa (< 0 poor, 0.00–0.20 slight, 0.21–0.40 fair, 0.41–0.60 moderate, 0.61–0.80 substantial, 0.81–1.00 almost perfect).
    3. Disputed items — table item_id | labels (label:count) | majority (or tie) | agreement, lowest first, to send to an adjudicator.
    4. Guideline gaps — per-label agreement (label | n | agreement | defined_in_guidelines); a low-agreement label is one below overall percent agreement; a gap is such a label the guidelines do not define, plus boundary rules for the top confusion pairs. Without guidelines: To be baselined · owner: Annotation lead.
    5. Method & limits — ratings must be independent; items with one rating are excluded and counted; nominal labels only; no confidence intervals; agreement measures consistency, not correctness.
  • Each item has only one annotator: say agreement cannot be computed without two or more independent ratings per item, report no score, and recommend double-labelling a sample.
  • No labelling round described at all: ask once for the labels export, the guidelines and the data owner's minimum alpha.
  • Asked to pick the threshold, declare labels defined without guidelines, or report a score anyway: decline in one line (the threshold is the data owner's; definitions come from written guidelines; no score without paired ratings) and show the marker.

  • New: labels from a pilot round (and draft guidelines) give alpha, disputed items and the label boundaries to sharpen before labelling at scale.
  • Existing: add the agreement.json from the previous round (previous); the report adds alpha, percent agreement, disputed items and per-label agreement then vs now, and names labels whose agreement fell.

When to use

  • ADLC data stage: before human labels become an eval golden set, an LLM-as-judge calibration set or fine-tuning data.
  • Pilot labelling round: find disputed items and the label boundaries the guidelines must sharpen before labelling at scale.

- **Each item has only one annotator**: say agreement cannot be computed without two or more independent ratings per item, report no score, and recommend double-labelling a sample.
- **No labelling round described at all**: ask once for the labels export, the guidelines and the data owner's minimum alpha.
- **Asked to pick the threshold, declare labels defined without guidelines, or report a score anyway**: decline in one line (the threshold is the data owner's; definitions come from written guidelines; no score without paired ratings) and show the marker.

## Starting points
- **New:** labels from a pilot round (and draft guidelines) give alpha, disputed items and the label boundaries to sharpen before labelling at scale.
- **Existing:** add the `agreement.json` from the previous round (`previous`); the report adds alpha, percent agreement, disputed items and per-label agreement then vs now, and names labels whose agreement fell.

## When to use
- ADLC data stage: before human labels become an eval golden set, an LLM-as-judge calibration set or fine-tuning data.
- Pilot labelling round: find disputed items and the label boundaries the guidelines must sharpen before labelling at scale.
- Gate: labels may be used only when alpha meets the minimum the data owner set.
- NOT for: scoring model outputs against labels (`llm-eval-harness`), data quality or PII scans (`data-readiness-assessment`, `pii-data-inventory`), building the training file (`finetune-dataset-builder`), ordinal or interval scales (nominal labels only).

## Inputs
| Input | Required | Source | If missing |
|---|---|---|---|
| `labels` — `item_id, annotator, label` | yes | labelling tool export (one row per rating) | run stops (exit 2), asks once |
| `guidelines` — Markdown | no | Annotation lead | `defined_in_guidelines` and the gap list read `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: Annotation lead]` |
| `min_agreement` — alpha threshold | no | eval / data owner | no gate; the report says none was set |

A blank `label` means "not rated" and is skipped. Two ratings of the same item by the same annotator stop the run (exit 2).

## Procedure
1. Read `../../../shared/quality-bar.md`.
2. Confirm ratings were independent (annotators did not see each other's labels); agreement on shared work is inflated.
3. Run the agent. `scripts/agreement.py` builds the coincidence matrix and computes alpha, Fleiss' kappa (equal ratings per item only), pairwise Cohen's kappa, per-label agreement and confusion pairs.
4. Read Disputed items worst-first; send them to an adjudicator.
5. Read Guideline gaps: define each low-agreement label the guidelines do not mention, and write a boundary rule for the top confusion pairs.
6. Re-label a fresh sample after the guideline change and re-run; compare alpha.
7. Run the self-check.

## Output
- `agreement.json` — every statistic, per-item agreement, pairs, confusion pairs, gate result, settings for `--verify`.
- `disputed-items.csv` — `item_id, labels, majority, agreement` (labels as `label:count`; `majority` is the plurality label or `tie`), lowest agreement first.
- `label-agreement.csv` — `label, n, agreement, defined_in_guidelines`.
- `agreement-report.md` — **Summary** (gate verdict first), **Agreement**, **Disputed items**, **Guideline gaps**, **Method & limits**.

## Self-check
- [ ] Alpha is reported with its band labelled as a convention (Krippendorff 0.667 / 0.800); kappas with Landis & Koch bands, also a convention
- [ ] Fleiss' kappa is n/a (with the reason) when items have different numbers of ratings — alpha is the headline
- [ ] Items with one rating are excluded and counted, not scored
- [ ] Guideline gaps come from the supplied guidelines; without them the gap list is TBD for the Annotation lead
- [ ] Limits stated: nominal only, no confidence intervals, agreement is not correctness

## References
- `references/method.md` — formulas, the worked examples the tests reproduce, per-label agreement definition
- `references/sources.md` — Cohen 1960, Fleiss 1971, Krippendorff 2011, Landis & Koch 1977; verified URLs and dates
- `assets/labels-template.csv`, `assets/guidelines-template.md` — input layouts
- `scripts/agreement.py` — statistics and `--verify` (argparse; stdlib)

## How to run (automation, when commands can run)
This skill is executable. Collect the inputs below, then run `python3 scripts/run_skill.py ai-platform/annotation-agreement --input <name>=<value> … --out <dir>` (see `--explain ai-platform/annotation-agreement`). Report the `run.json` results; do not hand-write the deliverables the script produces (`agreement.json`, `disputed-items.csv`, `label-agreement.csv`, `agreement-report.md`). Alpha below `min_agreement` fails the run (exit 1) with every output written. If no item has two or more ratings the run exits 1 and reports no score. Each output passes `--verify`, which re-derives it from the labels and the settings recorded in `agreement.json`.

Conversation Design (intents, fallback, hand-off, coverage)

How to run

This skill is executable. Collect the inputs below, then run python3 scripts/run_skill.py ai-platform/conversation-design --input <name>=<value> … --out <dir> (see --explain ai-platform/conversation-design). Accuracy below a supplied min_accuracy fails the run (exit 1) on purpose; the outputs are still written so the misses are visible.

Starting points

  • New: first-draft intents and unlabelled sample messages give a coverage figure, the messages nothing catches, thin and confusable intents, and the persona keys still to decide.
  • Existing: your live intent catalog, persona and labelled real messages give per-intent precision and recall, misroutes and an accuracy gate for edits to the catalog.

When to use

  • ADLC requirements stage: before building an assistant, to agree the intent catalog, response types, fallback and the human hand-off path.
  • "How much of what users actually say do our intents cover?" — route a sample of real messages and read coverage and gaps.
  • Regression check after editing intents: run with labelled utterances and a min_accuracy gate.
  • NOT for: prompt wording or system prompts (prompt-spec), grading LLM answers (llm-eval-harness), single- vs multi-agent design (agent-architecture), production NLU benchmarking (this router is lexical).

Inputs

InputRequiredSourceIf missing
intents — intent,description,examples,response_type,handoff,owneryesConversation designer (copy assets/intents-template.csv)run stops (exit 2), asks once
utterances — utterance[,expected_intent]yeschat logs, search logs, call-centre notes, sampled and de-identifiedrun stops (exit 2), asks once
persona — kv-csv name, tone, reading_level, escalation_channel, disallowed_topicsnoConversation designer / brand voice guideeach missing key is To be baselined · owner: Conversation designer
min_accuracy — 0–1noproduct ownerno gate; accuracy reported only

expected_intent may be an intent name, fallback (out of scope on purpose) or blank (unlabelled; counts toward coverage only). An unknown label, a bad response_type, a handoff other than yes/no, a duplicate intent or an intent named fallback stops the run (exit 2) with the line number.

Procedure

  1. Read ../../../shared/quality-bar.md.
  2. Strip personal data from the utterance sample. Outputs echo at most 80 characters of each utterance, but the run reads all of it.
  3. Run the agent. scripts/conversation_design.py routes each utterance by TF-IDF cosine (references/method.md); below 0.25 it goes to fallback.
  4. With labels it computes accuracy, per-intent precision/recall and confusion pairs; it flags intent pairs whose example sets reach cosine 0.40.
  5. With min_accuracy, accuracy below it (or no labels to measure it) exits 1.
  6. Work the Gaps list with each intent's owner: add missed phrasings, split or merge confusable intents, confirm out-of-scope messages.
  7. Run the self-check.

Output

  • routing.csv — utterance (≤ 80 chars), predicted_intent, score, expected_intent, correct, nearest_intent.
  • intent-quality.csv — intent, examples, precision, recall, confusable_with, response_type, handoff, routed, labelled, owner.
  • conversation-spec.md — Summary, Persona, Intents, Fallback and hand-off (mermaid flowchart), Coverage (uncovered utterances, confusion pairs), Gaps (each with an owner), Method.

Self-check

  • [ ] routing.csv re-derives exactly (--verify) and no output echoes more than 80 characters of an utterance (--leak-check)
  • [ ] Every gap names an owner; missing persona keys are TBD for the Conversation designer
  • [ ] The flowchart shows fallback and a path to a person
  • [ ] Threshold values (0.25 route, 0.40 confusable) are stated in the report
  • [ ] Limits stated: lexical router, sample-based, not a production NLU benchmark

References

  • references/method.md — tokenising, TF-IDF formula, thresholds, metrics, limits
  • assets/intents-template.csv, assets/utterances-template.csv, assets/persona-template.csv — input layouts
  • scripts/conversation_design.py — router, metrics, spec writer, --verify and --leak-check (argparse; stdlib)

`expected_intent` may be an intent name, `fallback` (out of scope on purpose) or blank (unlabelled; counts toward coverage only). An unknown label, a bad `response_type`, a `handoff` other than yes/no, a duplicate intent or an intent named `fallback` stops the run (exit 2) with the line number.

## Procedure
1. Read `../../../shared/quality-bar.md`.
2. Strip personal data from the utterance sample. Outputs echo at most 80 characters of each utterance, but the run reads all of it.
3. Run the agent. `scripts/conversation_design.py` routes each utterance by TF-IDF cosine (`references/method.md`); below 0.25 it goes to `fallback`.
4. With labels it computes accuracy, per-intent precision/recall and confusion pairs; it flags intent pairs whose example sets reach cosine 0.40.
5. With `min_accuracy`, accuracy below it (or no labels to measure it) exits 1.
6. Work the Gaps list with each intent's owner: add missed phrasings, split or merge confusable intents, confirm out-of-scope messages.
7. Run the self-check.

## Output
- `routing.csv` — `utterance` (≤ 80 chars), `predicted_intent`, `score`, `expected_intent`, `correct`, `nearest_intent`.
- `intent-quality.csv` — `intent, examples, precision, recall, confusable_with, response_type, handoff, routed, labelled, owner`.
- `conversation-spec.md` — **Summary**, **Persona**, **Intents**, **Fallback and hand-off** (mermaid flowchart), **Coverage** (uncovered utterances, confusion pairs), **Gaps** (each with an owner), **Method**.

## Self-check
- [ ] `routing.csv` re-derives exactly (`--verify`) and no output echoes more than 80 characters of an utterance (`--leak-check`)
- [ ] Every gap names an owner; missing persona keys are TBD for the Conversation designer
- [ ] The flowchart shows fallback and a path to a person
- [ ] Threshold values (0.25 route, 0.40 confusable) are stated in the report
- [ ] Limits stated: lexical router, sample-based, not a production NLU benchmark

## References
- `references/method.md` — tokenising, TF-IDF formula, thresholds, metrics, limits
- `assets/intents-template.csv`, `assets/utterances-template.csv`, `assets/persona-template.csv` — input layouts
- `scripts/conversation_design.py` — router, metrics, spec writer, `--verify` and `--leak-check` (argparse; stdlib)
