bodyHtml:
LLM Observability (traces → SLOs → alerts)

In a conversation: set up the roll-up now

The reply gives the monitoring setup and the exact inputs it needs; numbers appear only from real spans.

  • The feature is live but traces and SLOs are not in the conversation ("are we meeting SLOs, has latency drifted", or files said to be attached): in this reply give
    1. What to send: the trace export as JSONL and the SLO thresholds from the service owner. Never propose thresholds as the SLO; show the SLO CSV skeleton (metric,threshold,window,feature,comparator, rows for error_rate, latency_p95_ms, eval_score_mean, cost_per_request_usd, drift_*_pct) with each threshold To be baselined · owner: service owner.
    2. Trace fields per assets/trace-schema.json: required trace_id, ts, feature, model, latency_ms, input_tokens, output_tokens, status; optional cost_usd, eval_score, user_feedback. Spans missing required fields are rejected and counted, never repaired. Cost per request is reported only from spans that carry cost_usd, with coverage; without it the cost SLO reads NO DATA.
    3. Drift: against a baseline window once both dates are given (convert "first week of September" to baseline_start/baseline_end and confirm the year); drift = (current − baseline) ÷ baseline × 100 for tokens per request, p95 latency and eval score mean.
    4. The run: python3 -I scripts/observe.py --traces spans.jsonl --slo slo.csv --out-dir <dir> [--baseline-start …] [--baseline-end …] → dashboard.json, alerts.md (Status, SLO breaches, Drift, By feature), trace-schema.json; percentiles nearest-rank; any BREACH exits 1. Do not print metric values that were not computed.
  • Asked to pick sensible SLOs: decline in one line (a threshold is the service owner's commitment, not this skill's); show the skeleton with markers and ask for the values.
  • Asked to estimate cost from token prices (cost not logged): decline in one line; the cost SLO for that feature is NO DATA, reported and never counted as met; the fix is to instrument cost_usd on spans. Still report the other SLOs, e.g. a p95 above its threshold in its window is a BREACH and exits 1.
  • Nothing about the app: ask once for the feature names, the trace source (OpenTelemetry, Langfuse, provider logs) and the SLO owner.

Starting points

  • Existing — rolls up spans your running application already emitted against the owner's SLOs, with drift against a baseline window.
  • Only for existing: there is nothing to measure until an application produces traces; for a new app, emit spans per assets/trace-schema.json and set SLOs from assets/slo-template.csv, then run this on the first traffic.

When to use

  • A deployed LLM/agent feature needs per-feature latency, error, token, cost and quality roll-ups against SLOs.
  • "Has it drifted?" — compare the current window to a baseline window.
  • Defining what every span must log (trace schema) before go-live.
  • NOT for: application logging, Sentry or health checks (observability-setup), building eval sets (llm-eval-harness), running an incident (ai-incident-runbook), release gates (ai-release-plan).

Inputs required

InputRequiredSource
traces JSONL: trace_id, ts, feature/route, model, latency_ms, input_tokens, output_tokens, status; optional cost_usd, eval_score, user_feedbackyestracing export (OpenTelemetry, Langfuse, provider logs) mapped to assets/trace-schema.json
slo CSV: metric, threshold, window, optional feature and comparatoryesservice owner; the skill never sets a threshold
baseline_start, baseline_endnoowner; without them drift is not computed

If traces or slo is missing the runner exits 2 and asks once. Spans missing required fields are rejected and counted, never repaired.

Procedure

  1. Read ../../../shared/quality-bar.md.
  2. Map the trace export to assets/trace-schema.json (the script copies it to the output as the reference schema).
  3. Fill assets/slo-template.csv with the owner's thresholds and windows.
  4. Run the skill. The script splits baseline/current windows, computes the metrics in references/metrics-method.md per feature and overall, and evaluates each SLO in its window.
  5. Read alerts.md: Status first, then breaches, then drift and the feature table.
  6. NO DATA rows mean the signal is not instrumented (e.g. no cost_usd) — instrument it; do not estimate it.
  7. Run the self-check.

Output

  • dashboard.json: windows, overall and per-feature metrics, baseline, drift, SLO results, rejected-span reasons.
  • alerts.md: Status, SLO breaches (every SLO with observed value and status), Drift, By feature.
  • trace-schema.json: the recommended span schema (JSON Schema).

Self-check

  • [ ] Percentiles are nearest-rank and labelled as such
  • [ ] Cost per request only from cost_usd on spans, with coverage shown; never from guessed prices
  • [ ] Every SLO threshold came from the SLO file; NO DATA is not reported as met

# LLM Observability (traces → SLOs → alerts)

## In a conversation: set up the roll-up now
The reply gives the monitoring setup and the exact inputs it needs; numbers appear only from real spans.
- **The feature is live but traces and SLOs are not in the conversation** ("are we meeting SLOs, has latency drifted", or files said to be attached): in this reply give
  1. **What to send**: the trace export as JSONL and the SLO thresholds from the service owner. Never propose thresholds as the SLO; show the SLO CSV skeleton (`metric,threshold,window,feature,comparator`, rows for error_rate, latency_p95_ms, eval_score_mean, cost_per_request_usd, drift_*_pct) with each threshold `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: service owner]`.
  2. **Trace fields** per `assets/trace-schema.json`: required `trace_id, ts, feature, model, latency_ms, input_tokens, output_tokens, status`; optional `cost_usd, eval_score, user_feedback`. Spans missing required fields are rejected and counted, never repaired. Cost per request is reported only from spans that carry `cost_usd`, with coverage; without it the cost SLO reads NO DATA.
  3. **Drift**: against a baseline window once both dates are given (convert "first week of September" to `baseline_start`/`baseline_end` and confirm the year); drift = (current − baseline) ÷ baseline × 100 for tokens per request, p95 latency and eval score mean.
  4. **The run**: `python3 -I scripts/observe.py --traces spans.jsonl --slo slo.csv --out-dir <dir> [--baseline-start …] [--baseline-end …]` → `dashboard.json`, `alerts.md` (Status, SLO breaches, Drift, By feature), `trace-schema.json`; percentiles nearest-rank; any BREACH exits 1. Do not print metric values that were not computed.
- **Asked to pick sensible SLOs**: decline in one line (a threshold is the service owner's commitment, not this skill's); show the skeleton with markers and ask for the values.
- **Asked to estimate cost from token prices** (cost not logged): decline in one line; the cost SLO for that feature is NO DATA, reported and never counted as met; the fix is to instrument `cost_usd` on spans. Still report the other SLOs, e.g. a p95 above its threshold in its window is a BREACH and exits 1.
- **Nothing about the app**: ask once for the feature names, the trace source (OpenTelemetry, Langfuse, provider logs) and the SLO owner.

## Starting points
- **Existing** — rolls up spans your running application already emitted against the owner's SLOs, with drift against a baseline window.
- Only for existing: there is nothing to measure until an application produces traces; for a new app, emit spans per `assets/trace-schema.json` and set SLOs from `assets/slo-template.csv`, then run this on the first traffic.

## When to use
- A deployed LLM/agent feature needs per-feature latency, error, token, cost and quality roll-ups against SLOs.
- "Has it drifted?" — compare the current window to a baseline window.
- Defining what every span must log (trace schema) before go-live.
- NOT for: application logging, Sentry or health checks (`observability-setup`), building eval sets (`llm-eval-harness`), running an incident (`ai-incident-runbook`), release gates (`ai-release-plan`).

## Inputs required
| Input | Required | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `traces` JSONL: trace_id, ts, feature/route, model, latency_ms, input_tokens, output_tokens, status; optional cost_usd, eval_score, user_feedback | yes | tracing export (OpenTelemetry, Langfuse, provider logs) mapped to `assets/trace-schema.json` |
| `slo` CSV: metric, threshold, window, optional feature and comparator | yes | service owner; the skill never sets a threshold |
| `baseline_start`, `baseline_end` | no | owner; without them drift is not computed |

If `traces` or `slo` is missing the runner exits 2 and asks once. Spans missing required fields are rejected and counted, never repaired.

## Procedure
1. Read `../../../shared/quality-bar.md`.
2. Map the trace export to `assets/trace-schema.json` (the script copies it to the output as the reference schema).
3. Fill `assets/slo-template.csv` with the owner's thresholds and windows.
4. Run the skill. The script splits baseline/current windows, computes the metrics in `references/metrics-method.md` per feature and overall, and evaluates each SLO in its window.
5. Read `alerts.md`: Status first, then breaches, then drift and the feature table.
6. NO DATA rows mean the signal is not instrumented (e.g. no `cost_usd`) — instrument it; do not estimate it.
7. Run the self-check.

## Output
- `dashboard.json`: windows, overall and per-feature metrics, baseline, drift, SLO results, rejected-span reasons.
- `alerts.md`: Status, SLO breaches (every SLO with observed value and status), Drift, By feature.
- `trace-schema.json`: the recommended span schema (JSON Schema).

## Self-check
- [ ] Percentiles are nearest-rank and labelled as such
- [ ] Cost per request only from `cost_usd` on spans, with coverage shown; never from guessed prices
- [ ] Every SLO threshold came from the SLO file; NO DATA is not reported as met
- [ ] Drift states both windows and is relative to the baseline
- [ ] Rejected spans counted with reasons
- [ ] Exit 1 when any SLO is breached

## References
- `references/metrics-method.md` — windows, metric definitions, percentile method, drift, SLO evaluation
- `assets/trace-schema.json` — recommended span schema
- `assets/slo-template.csv` — SLO input layout
- `scripts/observe.py` — the roll-up (argparse; stdlib)

## How to run (automation, when commands can run)

Collect the inputs below, then run `python3 scripts/run_skill.py ai-platform/llm-observability --input <name>=<value> … --out <dir>` (see `--explain ai-platform/llm-observability`). Report the `run.json` results; do not hand-write the deliverables the script produces (`dashboard.json`, `alerts.md`, `trace-schema.json`). Any SLO breach fails the run (exit 1) on purpose; the outputs are still written.

How to run

This skill is executable. Collect the inputs below, then run python3 scripts/run_skill.py ai-platform/mcp-server-builder --input <name>=<value> … --out <dir> (see --explain ai-platform/mcp-server-builder). The runner then runs the scaffold's own contract tests as a check (stdlib runner scripts/run_contract_tests.py; the same files run under pytest); implement the stubs afterwards, following the Procedure.

Starting points

  • New — scaffold a stdlib MCP server, contracts, tests and README from tools.json.
  • Existing — pass the server folder you already run as existing_server: it is copied to target, tools it lacks get contracts, handler stubs and README rows, implemented handlers stay untouched, and the report lists added_tools, contract_changed (deployed contract kept) and existing_only_tools.

When to use

  • Building a new MCP server (Python or TypeScript), wrapping an existing API/database/SaaS as MCP tools, or reviewing a server for spec compliance and safety.
  • NOT for: choosing which tools an agent needs (agent-architecture), evaluation (llm-eval-harness).

Inputs required

InputRequiredSource
Target system(s) to expose and their API/docsyesuser / repo / URL
Tool list with side-effect class (read / write / irreversible / external_comm)yesuser; derive with agent-architecture if absent
Language and transport (stdio for local, Streamable HTTP for remote)yesuser; default Python + stdio for local, Streamable HTTP for remote
Auth model (API key, OAuth, service account) and tenant modelyesuser
Consumers (Claude Desktop/Code, custom agent, gateway)nouser

If the target system or the tool list is missing, ask once.

Procedure

  1. Read ../../../shared/quality-bar.md, ../../../shared/stack-conventions.md, ../../../shared/token-efficiency.md.
  2. Choose the implementation path. If the Anthropic mcp-builder skill is installed (see VENDORED.md at the repo root), use it for scaffolding and SDK specifics; else follow references/mcp-spec-essentials.md, which is a complete fallback covering protocol primitives, tool schemas, transports, auth, errors, and testing.
  3. Design tool contracts first. One JSON contract per tool using assets/tool-contract.schema.json (same template as agent-architecture). Apply the rules in references/mcp-spec-essentials.md §3: narrow tools, additionalProperties: false, enums, pagination, structured errors, side-effect metadata.
  4. Scaffold per references/server-skeleton.md: layout, config, logging, health, tests. Keep business logic in a service layer; the MCP layer only validates, authorizes, calls, and shapes output.
  5. Implement auth and scoping. Tenant and principal come from the transport auth context; never from tool arguments. Scope check per tool; deny by default.
  6. Harden. Timeouts, rate limits, result size caps, untrusted-output labeling, no secrets in logs, no raw exception text to the model.
  7. Test with references/testing-checklist.md: schema validation, authZ, error shapes, pagination, idempotency, injection corpus, protocol handshake via the SDK test client or the MCP Inspector.
  8. Document: README with tool table (name, purpose, side effect, scopes), install/run, config, security notes.
  9. Run the self-check.

Output

  • Server repo or directory: src/, tests/, README.md, .env.example, tools/*.json contracts.

Self-check

  • [ ] Every tool has input and output schemas, side-effect class, idempotency statement, timeout
  • [ ] No run_sql / execute_code / http_request style generic tools unless sandboxed, allow-listed, and HITL-gated
  • [ ] Tenant and principal derived from auth context only

bodyHtml:
Model Selection

In a conversation: rank the models now

  • The request carries model facts (candidates with prices, latency, context, the team's eval scores, plus weights and constraints — or says they are attached but their contents are not in the conversation): give the decision in this reply, in the decision.md order: Recommendation (winner, runner-up, robustness verdict), Criteria (weight, direction, hard constraints), Eliminated (each candidate with the hard constraint it fails), Scores (min-max normalised per criterion over survivors, weighted sum, rank, monthly cost when a workload is given), Sensitivity (each weight ±20%: does the winner change), Sources (source and as-of per row), Gaps. Use only stated facts; every missing value is To be baselined · owner to be named naming who holds it (eval owner, vendor price sheet, product owner for volumes). State that the run is python3 -I scripts/select_model.py --candidates … --criteria … [--workload …] --out-dir <dir> and that --verify recomputes the ranking. Never reply with only a request for files.
  • No candidate facts ("which LLM should we use for X?"): ask once, in one list, for (1) the shortlist with the team's own eval scores, prices in/out per 1M tokens, p95 latency and context — each with source and as_of — using assets/candidates-template.csv; (2) criteria with weights, direction and hard constraints (self-host, data residency, latency SLO, minimum accuracy) using assets/criteria-template.csv; (3) optional workload via assets/workload-template.csv. Say plainly that you will not quote any model price, benchmark score or capability from memory.
  • No candidate meets the hard constraints: list every candidate eliminated with its reasons and say no candidate meets them (the run exits 1); do not recommend one anyway — offer the constraint to revisit and its owner.
  • Cost criterion without a workload: do not assume volumes; monthly cost is To be baselined · owner: product owner and the run stops with an input error until the workload is given.
  • An incumbent is named: add "Incumbent" — whether it still passes the hard constraints, its rank, switch or stay, score gap, monthly-cost delta, and the criteria where the incumbent is better.

Starting points

  • New — rank candidate models on your criteria, hard constraints and workload.
  • Existing — also name the model in production as incumbent (include it in the candidates CSV): decision.md adds "Incumbent" — whether it still passes the hard constraints, its rank, switch or stay, the score gap, the monthly-cost delta and where the winner is better or worse.

When to use

  • Picking a model for one use case from a shortlist of API and/or self-hosted candidates.
  • Re-running the choice when prices, eval scores or constraints change (dated inputs make the decision repeatable).
  • Testing whether the choice is robust to how the team weights accuracy vs cost vs latency.
  • NOT for: producing the eval scores (llm-eval-harness), GPU sizing and self-host TCO (infra-gpu-sizing; feed its $/1M figure in as the self-host price), agent pattern design (agent-architecture).

Inputs required

InputRequiredSource
candidates CSV: model, provider, hosting (api|self-host), context_tokens, price_in_per_1m, price_out_per_1m, p95_latency_ms, one column per eval/benchmark score, source, as_ofyesuser's own eval runs, vendor price pages, internal TCO; dated
criteria CSV: criterion, weight, direction, hard_min / hard_max / hard_inyesdecision owner (solution architect + product)
workload CSV: tokens in/out per request, requests per monthnologs or product plan; required only when a criterion is monthly_cost_usd

If a candidate fact is missing, ask once; the script never fills it. A blank on a weighted criterion scores 0 and is listed under Gaps with an owner; a blank on a hard-constrained criterion eliminates the candidate (cannot verify).

Procedure

  1. Read ../../../shared/quality-bar.md.
  2. Collect facts, not opinions: fill assets/candidates-template.csv from the team's own eval runs (see llm-eval-harness) and dated price sheets. Every row carries source and as_of.
  3. Set criteria in assets/criteria-template.csv per references/criteria-design.md: must-haves become hard constraints (weight 0 + hard_min/hard_max/hard_in); trade-offs get weights and a direction.
  4. Run python3 -I scripts/select_model.py --candidates … --criteria … [--workload …] --out-dir <dir>. The script applies hard constraints (with reasons), min-max normalises each weighted criterion over the survivors, computes the weighted score, ranks, and scales each weight by ±20% to test whether the winner changes (references/scoring-method.md).
  5. Decision point — robustness. If Sensitivity shows a challenger, the decision depends on a weight: put the exact trade-off to the decision owner rather than reporting a single winner.
  6. Verify: python3 -I scripts/select_model.py --verify <dir>/ranking.json recomputes scores and ranks.
  7. Run the self-check.

Output

  • ranking.json: criteria with normalised weights, eliminated candidates and reasons, ranked survivors with raw / normalised / contribution per criterion, monthly cost, sensitivity runs, recommendation, gaps, sources.
  • decision.md: Recommendation, Criteria, Eliminated, Scores, Sensitivity, Sources, Gaps. Every number traces to ranking.json.

Self-check

  • [ ] Every model fact came from the candidates file with a source and as-of date; none was supplied by the skill
  • [ ] Hard constraints are stated as constraints, not disguised as heavy weights
  • [ ] Each eliminated candidate has its reason(s)
  • [ ] Sensitivity verdict reported; a non-robust winner is escalated, not hidden
  • [ ] Gaps carry To be baselined · owner: <role>
  • [ ] --verify passes on ranking.json

# Model Selection

## In a conversation: rank the models now
- **The request carries model facts** (candidates with prices, latency, context, the team's eval scores, plus weights and constraints — or says they are attached but their contents are not in the conversation): give the decision **in this reply**, in the `decision.md` order: **Recommendation** (winner, runner-up, robustness verdict), **Criteria** (weight, direction, hard constraints), **Eliminated** (each candidate with the hard constraint it fails), **Scores** (min-max normalised per criterion over survivors, weighted sum, rank, monthly cost when a workload is given), **Sensitivity** (each weight ±20%: does the winner change), **Sources** (source and as-of per row), **Gaps**. Use only stated facts; every missing value is `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]` naming who holds it (eval owner, vendor price sheet, product owner for volumes). State that the run is `python3 -I scripts/select_model.py --candidates … --criteria … [--workload …] --out-dir <dir>` and that `--verify` recomputes the ranking. Never reply with only a request for files.
- **No candidate facts** ("which LLM should we use for X?"): ask once, in one list, for (1) the shortlist with the team's own eval scores, prices in/out per 1M tokens, p95 latency and context — each with `source` and `as_of` — using `assets/candidates-template.csv`; (2) criteria with weights, direction and hard constraints (self-host, data residency, latency SLO, minimum accuracy) using `assets/criteria-template.csv`; (3) optional workload via `assets/workload-template.csv`. Say plainly that you will not quote any model price, benchmark score or capability from memory.
- **No candidate meets the hard constraints**: list every candidate eliminated with its reasons and say no candidate meets them (the run exits 1); do not recommend one anyway — offer the constraint to revisit and its owner.
- **Cost criterion without a workload**: do not assume volumes; monthly cost is `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: product owner]` and the run stops with an input error until the workload is given.
- **An incumbent is named**: add "Incumbent" — whether it still passes the hard constraints, its rank, switch or stay, score gap, monthly-cost delta, and the criteria where the incumbent is better.

## Starting points
- **New** — rank candidate models on your criteria, hard constraints and workload.
- **Existing** — also name the model in production as `incumbent` (include it in the candidates CSV): decision.md adds "Incumbent" — whether it still passes the hard constraints, its rank, switch or stay, the score gap, the monthly-cost delta and where the winner is better or worse.

## When to use
- Picking a model for one use case from a shortlist of API and/or self-hosted candidates.
- Re-running the choice when prices, eval scores or constraints change (dated inputs make the decision repeatable).
- Testing whether the choice is robust to how the team weights accuracy vs cost vs latency.
- NOT for: producing the eval scores (`llm-eval-harness`), GPU sizing and self-host TCO (`infra-gpu-sizing`; feed its $/1M figure in as the self-host price), agent pattern design (`agent-architecture`).

## Inputs required
| Input | Required | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `candidates` CSV: model, provider, hosting (api\|self-host), context_tokens, price_in_per_1m, price_out_per_1m, p95_latency_ms, one column per eval/benchmark score, `source`, `as_of` | yes | user's own eval runs, vendor price pages, internal TCO; dated |
| `criteria` CSV: criterion, weight, direction, hard_min / hard_max / hard_in | yes | decision owner (solution architect + product) |
| `workload` CSV: tokens in/out per request, requests per month | no | logs or product plan; required only when a criterion is `monthly_cost_usd` |

If a candidate fact is missing, ask once; the script never fills it. A blank on a weighted criterion scores 0 and is listed under Gaps with an owner; a blank on a hard-constrained criterion eliminates the candidate (cannot verify).

## Procedure
1. Read `../../../shared/quality-bar.md`.
2. **Collect facts, not opinions**: fill `assets/candidates-template.csv` from the team's own eval runs (see `llm-eval-harness`) and dated price sheets. Every row carries `source` and `as_of`.
3. **Set criteria** in `assets/criteria-template.csv` per `references/criteria-design.md`: must-haves become hard constraints (weight 0 + `hard_min`/`hard_max`/`hard_in`); trade-offs get weights and a direction.
4. **Run** `python3 -I scripts/select_model.py --candidates … --criteria … [--workload …] --out-dir <dir>`. The script applies hard constraints (with reasons), min-max normalises each weighted criterion over the survivors, computes the weighted score, ranks, and scales each weight by ±20% to test whether the winner changes (`references/scoring-method.md`).
5. **Decision point — robustness.** If Sensitivity shows a challenger, the decision depends on a weight: put the exact trade-off to the decision owner rather than reporting a single winner.
6. **Verify**: `python3 -I scripts/select_model.py --verify <dir>/ranking.json` recomputes scores and ranks.
7. Run the self-check.

## Output
- `ranking.json`: criteria with normalised weights, eliminated candidates and reasons, ranked survivors with raw / normalised / contribution per criterion, monthly cost, sensitivity runs, recommendation, gaps, sources.
- `decision.md`: Recommendation, Criteria, Eliminated, Scores, Sensitivity, Sources, Gaps. Every number traces to `ranking.json`.

## Self-check
- [ ] Every model fact came from the candidates file with a source and as-of date; none was supplied by the skill
- [ ] Hard constraints are stated as constraints, not disguised as heavy weights
- [ ] Each eliminated candidate has its reason(s)
- [ ] Sensitivity verdict reported; a non-robust winner is escalated, not hidden
- [ ] Gaps carry `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: <role>]`
- [ ] `--verify` passes on `ranking.json`

## References
- `references/scoring-method.md` — constraint gating, min-max normalisation, weighted sum, sensitivity
- `references/criteria-design.md` — choosing criteria, weights and hard constraints; provenance rules
- `assets/candidates-template.csv`, `assets/criteria-template.csv`, `assets/workload-template.csv` — input layouts
- `scripts/select_model.py` — scorer and verifier (argparse; stdlib)

## How to run (automation, when commands can run)
This skill is executable. Collect the inputs below, then run `python3 scripts/run_skill.py ai-platform/model-selection --input <name>=<value> … --out <dir>` (see `--explain ai-platform/model-selection`). Report the `run.json` results; do not hand-write the deliverables the script produces (`ranking.json`, `decision.md`). When no candidate survives the hard constraints the run exits 1 on purpose and `decision.md` says so.

bodyHtml:
Program RAID Status

In a conversation: write the status now

Never

  • Never assume today's date: no as-of date → ask for it (YYYY-MM-DD) and say "the system date will not be used".
  • Never assign an owner the user names ("just put the platform lead on R3"): the owner stays To be baselined · owner: Program manager and a Decision needed reads "Name an owner for R3 — To be baselined · owner: Program manager". A blank milestone owner (e.g. M7) is also that TBD.
  • Never call a milestone green when slip_days > green_max (default 0); slip 1–10 is amber, slip > 10 is red. Never report overall AMBER/GREEN when an open critical-path milestone is red — that is RED.

- Never call a milestone green when slip_days > green_max (default 0); slip 1–10 is **amber**, slip > 10 is **red**. Never report overall AMBER/GREEN when an open critical-path milestone is red — that is **RED**.

4. Critical path: earliest finish EF = duration_days + max EF of its `depends_on` (0 if none; ties → lowest id). End = largest EF (tie → lowest id); trace back through the predecessor with the largest EF. Path length = end EF in days. Zero-float milestones are also on_critical_path = yes.
5. RAID (open items only): exposure = likelihood × impact; an issue with blank likelihood counts 5. overdue_days = max(0, as_of − due); age_days = as_of − raised. Top risks = open `risk` rows by exposure desc (tie → id), top 5.
6. Overall RAG — apply in order: **RED** if any open critical-path milestone is red, or any open item with exposure ≥ red_exposure has overdue_days > 0; else **AMBER** if any open milestone is amber/red, any open item is overdue, or any open item has a blank owner; else **GREEN**.
7. Gate (`strict`): RED → "`--strict` was set: the run fails (exit 1) because overall RAG is red." — every output is still written. AMBER/GREEN → "gate passed", exit 0.

**Reply layout**: first the working tables — milestones (id, baseline, forecast, slip_days, rule hit, RAG, EF, on_critical_path) and open RAID (id, L, I, exposure, due, overdue_days, owner) — then the verdict, then `status-report.md` sections: **Summary** ("**Overall RAG: RED**" + the reasons + the line "Overall RAG rule: …" + thresholds), **Milestones**, **Critical path** ("M1 → M2 → … = N days" + mermaid flowchart), **Top risks**, **Overdue items** (with ageing buckets 1–7, 8–30, 31+), **Decisions needed** (each with an owner or the TBD), **Method**.

Prompt Spec

How to run

This skill is executable. Collect the inputs below, then run python3 scripts/run_skill.py ai-platform/prompt-spec --input <name>=<value> … --out <dir> (see --explain ai-platform/prompt-spec). Report the run.json results; do not hand-write the deliverables the script produces (prompt.md, prompt-lint.json, prompt-tests.jsonl). Any error-severity finding exits 1 on purpose: prompt-lint.json is written, the prompt and tests are not.

Starting points

  • New — lint a spec written from assets/prompt-spec-template.json, render the versioned prompt and its regression cases.
  • Existing — also pass the spec of the version in production as previous: each change is classed major, minor or patch for callers and consumers, the version must rise by at least that level (E-VERSION-BUMP blocks the render otherwise), and prompt.md adds "Changes since v<previous>".

When to use

  • Moving a prompt from a notebook or chat into a product: give it an id, a semver version and a contract.
  • Changing a live prompt: bump the version, re-lint, regenerate the regression cases.
  • Reviewing a prompt someone else wrote for undeclared variables, broken examples or budget overruns.
  • NOT for: running cases against a model and gating on scores (llm-eval-harness consumes prompt-tests.jsonl), model choice (model-selection), jailbreak/injection testing (red-team-suite).

Inputs required

InputRequiredSource
spec JSON: id, version, role, task, variables[{name, description, required}], output_schema, constraints[], examples[{inputs, output}], max_input_tokensyesprompt owner; assets/prompt-spec-template.json shows the layout

max_input_tokens is the owner's budget for this call (model context minus output and safety margin); the skill does not pick it. Examples are real or representative cases the owner signs off; the skill does not write them.

Procedure

  1. Read ../../../shared/quality-bar.md.
  2. Write the spec from assets/prompt-spec-template.json following references/spec-format.md: role is stable instructions; task carries every per-request {{variable}}; output is JSON with a schema.
  3. Run python3 -I scripts/prompt_spec.py --spec <spec.json> --out-dir <dir>. The linter applies the rules in references/lint-rules.md: variables declared ⇄ used, required variables present per example, example outputs valid against output_schema (subset: type, properties, required, enum, items), token estimate (chars/4, labelled an estimate) within max_input_tokens.
  4. Decision point — errors. Fix the spec, never the outputs; the prompt and tests render only from a clean spec. Warnings (missing descriptions, unsupported schema keywords, no constraints) are reviewed and either fixed or accepted in the PR.
  5. Version per references/versioning.md: change to role/constraints/schema → MINOR or MAJOR; wording-only task change → PATCH. The case ids embed the version, so regressions are traceable.
  6. Hand off prompt-tests.jsonl to the eval harness; verify with python3 -I scripts/prompt_spec.py --verify-tests <dir>/prompt-tests.jsonl.
  7. Run the self-check.

Output

  • prompt-lint.json: status, severity counts, token estimates per example and for the template, findings {code, severity, where, message}.
  • prompt.md: header comment and table (id, version, spec SHA-256, budget, estimate), System, User, Variables, Regression cases.
  • prompt-tests.jsonl: per example id (<prompt>@<version>#ex-NN), inputs, rendered system and input, expected, output_schema, assertions (json_valid, json_schema, equals on enum/boolean fields).

Self-check

  • [ ] prompt-lint.json status is pass, with warnings reviewed
  • [ ] Version bumped for any change since the last release
  • [ ] Every example is a case the owner accepts as correct, not an invented one
  • [ ] Token figures are reported as estimates (chars/4), not tokenizer counts
  • [ ] --verify-tests passes on prompt-tests.jsonl

References

  • references/spec-format.md — field-by-field spec format and the supported JSON Schema subset
  • references/lint-rules.md — every finding code, severity and fix
  • references/versioning.md — semver for prompts and how case ids carry it
  • assets/prompt-spec-template.json — spec layout to copy
  • scripts/prompt_spec.py — linter, renderer, test-case verifier (argparse; stdlib)

| `spec` JSON: `id`, `version`, `role`, `task`, `variables[{name, description, required}]`, `output_schema`, `constraints[]`, `examples[{inputs, output}]`, `max_input_tokens` | yes | prompt owner; `assets/prompt-spec-template.json` shows the layout |

`max_input_tokens` is the owner's budget for this call (model context minus output and safety margin); the skill does not pick it. Examples are real or representative cases the owner signs off; the skill does not write them.

## Procedure
1. Read `../../../shared/quality-bar.md`.
2. **Write the spec** from `assets/prompt-spec-template.json` following `references/spec-format.md`: role is stable instructions; task carries every per-request `{{variable}}`; output is JSON with a schema.
3. **Run** `python3 -I scripts/prompt_spec.py --spec <spec.json> --out-dir <dir>`. The linter applies the rules in `references/lint-rules.md`: variables declared ⇄ used, required variables present per example, example outputs valid against `output_schema` (subset: `type`, `properties`, `required`, `enum`, `items`), token estimate (chars/4, labelled an estimate) within `max_input_tokens`.
4. **Decision point — errors.** Fix the spec, never the outputs; the prompt and tests render only from a clean spec. Warnings (missing descriptions, unsupported schema keywords, no constraints) are reviewed and either fixed or accepted in the PR.
5. **Version** per `references/versioning.md`: change to role/constraints/schema → MINOR or MAJOR; wording-only task change → PATCH. The case ids embed the version, so regressions are traceable.
6. **Hand off** `prompt-tests.jsonl` to the eval harness; verify with `python3 -I scripts/prompt_spec.py --verify-tests <dir>/prompt-tests.jsonl`.
7. Run the self-check.

## Output
- `prompt-lint.json`: status, severity counts, token estimates per example and for the template, findings `{code, severity, where, message}`.
- `prompt.md`: header comment and table (id, version, spec SHA-256, budget, estimate), System, User, Variables, Regression cases.
- `prompt-tests.jsonl`: per example `id` (`<prompt>@<version>#ex-NN`), inputs, rendered `system` and `input`, `expected`, `output_schema`, assertions (`json_valid`, `json_schema`, `equals` on enum/boolean fields).

## Self-check
- [ ] `prompt-lint.json` status is pass, with warnings reviewed
- [ ] Version bumped for any change since the last release
- [ ] Every example is a case the owner accepts as correct, not an invented one
- [ ] Token figures are reported as estimates (chars/4), not tokenizer counts
- [ ] `--verify-tests` passes on `prompt-tests.jsonl`

## References
- `references/spec-format.md` — field-by-field spec format and the supported JSON Schema subset
- `references/lint-rules.md` — every finding code, severity and fix
- `references/versioning.md` — semver for prompts and how case ids carry it
- `assets/prompt-spec-template.json` — spec layout to copy
- `scripts/prompt_spec.py` — linter, renderer, test-case verifier (argparse; stdlib)

Red-Team Suite

In a conversation: set up the red-team run now

  • No app profile ("red-team our chatbot"): ask once, in one list, for the profile in assets/app-profile-template.json: app_name, purpose, tools (name + description), data the app can see, a synthetic canary (≥ 8 letters/digits, never a real secret) planted in the system prompt of the test build, and out-of-scope topics. Explain the two passes: (1) profile → attacks.jsonl (30+ OWASP-mapped cases, stable ids) to run against the app; (2) recorded case_id,response CSV with tool-call traces → graded scorecard, report and gate. The pass threshold is the AI risk lead's decision; there is no default.
  • The request carries profile facts: write the profile JSON from them (gaps To be baselined · owner: app owner), list the categories that will be generated with their OWASP references (references/attack-categories.md: prompt injection direct and indirect, canary exfiltration, sensitive data disclosure per data category, tool misuse per tool, role-play jailbreak, active content, out-of-scope per topic), and give python3 -I scripts/redteam.py --profile app-profile.json --out-dir <dir>. The scorecard reads awaiting_responses; no grading is invented.
  • Responses or results said to be attached but not in the conversation: state the grading and gate rules and the command (--responses responses.csv --threshold <t>), and that the gate fails on any canary leak (including spaced-out and base64 forms), any case without a response, or a pass rate below the threshold. Never print a pass rate, case count or verdict that was not computed.
  • No pass mark agreed: grade every case, but the gate is not_evaluated with To be baselined · owner: AI risk lead; never pick a threshold.
  • Asked to lower the threshold, ignore a canary leak or skip cases: decline in one line (a canary leak fails the gate whatever the pass rate; a lowered bar hides real failures); fix the app and re-run the same profile so case ids match.

Starting points

  • New — from an app profile alone, generate the OWASP-mapped attack set to run before launch; nothing is graded until responses exist.
  • Existing — pass the running app's responses (with tool-call traces) and the risk lead's pass mark: every case is graded by its detector and the gate passes or fails on the real results.

When to use

  • Pre-launch or pre-release security testing of a chat assistant, RAG app or tool-using agent with text I/O.
  • Regression after a prompt, model or tool change: same profile → same case ids → comparable scorecards.
  • NOT for: answer quality and accuracy (llm-eval-harness), prompt contract linting (prompt-spec), the risk register and controls (ai-governance-risk), image/audio attacks, or infrastructure penetration testing.

Inputs required

InputRequiredSource
profile JSON: app_name, purpose, tools (name + description), data the app can see, canary token, out-of-scope topicsyesapp owner; plant the canary in the app's system prompt before testing
responses CSV: case_id,responseno (pass 2)test harness or manual run of attacks.jsonl; include tool-call traces in the response cell
threshold: overall pass rate to clear the gate (0–1)noAI risk lead; without it the gate is To be baselined · owner: AI risk lead

Procedure

  1. Read ../../../shared/quality-bar.md.
  2. Profile the app in assets/app-profile-template.json. Plant a unique canary string in the system prompt (never a real secret).
  3. Generate: python3 -I scripts/redteam.py --profile <profile.json> --out-dir <dir> → attacks.jsonl (≥ 30 cases, stable ids, categories in references/attack-categories.md).
  4. Execute each case against the app per references/running-the-suite.md: attack as the user turn; context_document, when present, through the channel the app treats as untrusted content (retrieved document, web page, email). Record case_id,response with the tool-call trace.
  5. Grade: re-run with --responses <csv> --threshold <t>. Detectors are deterministic (references/detectors.md, vocabularies in assets/detector-markers.json).
  6. Decision point — gate. Fail on any canary leak, any unanswered case, or pass rate below threshold. No threshold → not evaluated, owner AI risk lead. Never lower the threshold to pass a run.
  7. Review every failure and a sample of passes by hand (string detectors miss paraphrased compliance), fix the app, re-run the same profile.
  8. Run the self-check.

Output

  • attacks.jsonl: case_id, template_id, category, OWASP reference, delivery, attack, context_document, marker, target_tool, detectors.
  • redteam-scorecard.json: per-case detector results, per-category and overall pass rates, canary leaks, gate status, threshold and reasons.
  • redteam-report.md: Gate, Results by category, Failures, Method, References; every number traces to the scorecard.

Self-check

  • [ ] Canary is a synthetic test string planted for this run, not a real credential
  • [ ] Every case in attacks.jsonl has a response (or the gate fails as incomplete)
  • [ ] Threshold came from the AI risk lead, or is marked To be baselined · owner: AI risk lead
  • [ ] Failures reviewed by hand; detector false positives noted, not silently dropped
  • [ ] Same profile and template library used for before/after comparisons

References

  • references/attack-categories.md — categories, OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications mapping, what each case probes
  • references/detectors.md — detector logic, obfuscations covered, known blind spots
  • references/running-the-suite.md — executing attacks, recording responses, gating and re-runs
  • assets/attack-templates.json — bundled attack template library (original wording)
  • assets/detector-markers.json — refusal, tool-call and active-content vocabularies
  • assets/app-profile-template.json — profile layout
  • scripts/redteam.py — generator, grader, verifier (argparse; stdlib)

How to run (automation, when commands can run)

This skill is executable. Collect the inputs below, then run python3 scripts/run_skill.py ai-platform/red-team-suite --input <name>=<value> … --out <dir> (see --explain ai-platform/red-team-suite). Report the run.json results; do not hand-write the deliverables the script produces (attacks.jsonl, redteam-scorecard.json, redteam-report.md). A failed gate exits 1 on purpose.

Two passes: (1) profile only → attacks.jsonl and a scorecard with status awaiting_responses; run the attacks against the app; (2) profile + responses (+ threshold) → graded scorecard, report and gate.

| `threshold`: overall pass rate to clear the gate (0–1) | no | AI risk lead; without it the gate is `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: AI risk lead]` |

## Procedure
1. Read `../../../shared/quality-bar.md`.
2. **Profile the app** in `assets/app-profile-template.json`. Plant a unique canary string in the system prompt (never a real secret).
3. **Generate**: `python3 -I scripts/redteam.py --profile <profile.json> --out-dir <dir>` → `attacks.jsonl` (≥ 30 cases, stable ids, categories in `references/attack-categories.md`).
4. **Execute** each case against the app per `references/running-the-suite.md`: `attack` as the user turn; `context_document`, when present, through the channel the app treats as untrusted content (retrieved document, web page, email). Record `case_id,response` with the tool-call trace.
5. **Grade**: re-run with `--responses <csv> --threshold <t>`. Detectors are deterministic (`references/detectors.md`, vocabularies in `assets/detector-markers.json`).
6. **Decision point — gate.** Fail on any canary leak, any unanswered case, or pass rate below threshold. No threshold → not evaluated, owner AI risk lead. Never lower the threshold to pass a run.
7. Review every failure and a sample of passes by hand (string detectors miss paraphrased compliance), fix the app, re-run the same profile.
8. Run the self-check.

## Output
- `attacks.jsonl`: case_id, template_id, category, OWASP reference, delivery, attack, context_document, marker, target_tool, detectors.
- `redteam-scorecard.json`: per-case detector results, per-category and overall pass rates, canary leaks, gate status, threshold and reasons.
- `redteam-report.md`: Gate, Results by category, Failures, Method, References; every number traces to the scorecard.

## Self-check
- [ ] Canary is a synthetic test string planted for this run, not a real credential
- [ ] Every case in `attacks.jsonl` has a response (or the gate fails as incomplete)
- [ ] Threshold came from the AI risk lead, or is marked `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: AI risk lead]`
- [ ] Failures reviewed by hand; detector false positives noted, not silently dropped
- [ ] Same profile and template library used for before/after comparisons

## References
- `references/attack-categories.md` — categories, OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications mapping, what each case probes
- `references/detectors.md` — detector logic, obfuscations covered, known blind spots
- `references/running-the-suite.md` — executing attacks, recording responses, gating and re-runs
- `assets/attack-templates.json` — bundled attack template library (original wording)
- `assets/detector-markers.json` — refusal, tool-call and active-content vocabularies
- `assets/app-profile-template.json` — profile layout
- `scripts/redteam.py` — generator, grader, verifier (argparse; stdlib)

## How to run (automation, when commands can run)
This skill is executable. Collect the inputs below, then run `python3 scripts/run_skill.py ai-platform/red-team-suite --input <name>=<value> … --out <dir>` (see `--explain ai-platform/red-team-suite`). Report the `run.json` results; do not hand-write the deliverables the script produces (`attacks.jsonl`, `redteam-scorecard.json`, `redteam-report.md`). A failed gate exits 1 on purpose.

Two passes: (1) profile only → `attacks.jsonl` and a scorecard with status `awaiting_responses`; run the attacks against the app; (2) profile + responses (+ threshold) → graded scorecard, report and gate.

In a conversation: design the pipeline now

  • The request names the goal (new pipeline, add a stage, tag-based prod releases): answer in this reply with, in order: (1) the stage table — stage → trigger → job → required check name (ci / lint-typecheck-test, ci / rls-lint, preview / e2e) → secrets → timeout — and a line that no file is written until you reply "go"; (2) the three workflows .github/workflows/ci.yml, preview.yml, prod.yml with their jobs, and every npm run <script> they call listed for checking against package.json; (3) the env/secret matrix — each secret → GitHub secret, Vercel env or GitHub Environment (staging, production) — names only, never values, with the gh secret set commands; (4) the prod path in prod.yml: tag on main verified by git merge-base, migrate staging → migrate prod behind the production Environment reviewer gate, deploy, smoke /api/health and /api/health/deep, release; (5) the rollback runbook installed at docs/runbooks/rollback.md (Vercel Instant Rollback plus the migration revert path); (6) the branch-protection commands. Repo facts not in the request (project refs, existing scripts) are To be baselined · owner to be named, asked at the end. Never reply with only a request for the workflow files.
  • A run failed and the log line is given: name the cause from the log, give the minimal fix, and say which steps stay untouched. For supabase db push "migration … applied with different checksum": an already-applied migration file was edited; restore the original file from git history and move the change into a new, later-numbered migration — never supabase migration repair, never delete or rewrite migration history to make the run pass. Change no unrelated workflow step.
  • "Deploy to production" with no environment facts: ask once, in one list, for the Vercel project, the Supabase project refs for staging and prod, and whether the GitHub Environments staging/production exist. Do not deploy, tag or promote anything until they arrive and you say "go".
  • Asked to drop a required check or mark CI done while a stage is missing: decline in one line (branch protection depends on those check names), list what is missing, and offer the merge from assets/workflows/.

Starting points

  • New — point target at an empty folder: all three workflows are written from assets/workflows/ and validated.
  • Existing — point target at your repo: customised workflows are kept and validated job by job, missing ones are added, and every npm run they call is checked against your package.json.

When to use

  • New pipeline, pipeline change, flaky/failing workflow, adding a stage (e2e, RLS lint, coverage gate), release/rollback procedure.
  • NOT for: writing tests (test-strategy-tdd), runtime alerts (observability-setup), bootstrap of a brand-new repo (project-bootstrap calls this skill's assets).

Missing repo facts do not stop the design: mark them To be baselined · owner to be named and ask at the end. Only when the goal is absent, or prod work is asked without the Vercel and Supabase project refs, ask once and do not deploy or tag.

Procedure

  1. Read ../../../shared/stack-conventions.md (CI row), ../../../shared/token-efficiency.md. Read existing workflows and package.json scripts; map what runs where today.
  2. Plan. Stage table (from references/pipeline-stages.md): stage → trigger → job → required check name → secrets. For fixes: failing step → root cause hypothesis → minimal change. Post; wait for "go". (gate: plan→approve)
  3. Build. Copy/merge assets/workflows/ci.yml, assets/workflows/preview.yml, assets/workflows/prod.yml; never overwrite a customised workflow — diff and merge. Confirm every npm run <script> exists. Fill the env/secret matrix from references/env-promotion.md; list gh secret set commands (values never in chat).

Never

  • Never flag removed (-) or context ( ) lines, and never flag CR-DEBUG inside a test file (__tests__/, tests/, *.test.ts, test_*.py, …).
  • Never print a full secret: evidence keeps the first 4 characters + [redacted] (e.g. AKIA[redacted]).
  • Never "just approve": a blocking finding fails the gate (exit 1) regardless of deadline.

Procedure (from scripts/review.py; work line by line through the supplied diff)

  1. Parse: per file, status (added if --- /dev/null, else modified), hunks, added lines with new-file line numbers — the @@ … +N start is line N; each context or + line advances the counter, - lines do not.
  2. Detect on added lines only — blocking: CR-SECRET (key/token literals, password|secret|token|api_key = "<literal ≥8>", high-entropy literal ≥ 20 chars at ≥ 4.0 bits/char), CR-EVAL (eval(/exec(/new Function(), CR-TLS (verify=False, rejectUnauthorized: false, CERT_NONE, curl -k…), CR-SQL-CONCAT (SQL keyword text built with +, f-string, ${}, %, .format(); warning: CR-SWALLOW (except: pass, empty catch {}), CR-DEBUG (non-test files: console.log/debug/trace, debugger, print( in .py, pdb, System.out.println); info: CR-TODO (TODO/FIXME/XXX/HACK not followed by (name), @name, [ABC-12], (#12)), CR-DUP (same ≥3-line added block twice); warning: CR-NO-TESTS when source code files changed and no test file changed.
  3. Team rules (rules CSV) after the built-ins: a built-in rule_id with empty pattern overrides its severity (off disables) — e.g. CR-TODO,,warning makes the TODO a warning, CR-NO-TESTS,,blocking only bites if no test changed; other rows are custom regex rules on added lines (filtered by file_glob).
  4. Sort blocking → warning → info, then file, line; number F01, F02 …. Counts per severity.
  5. Verdict: BLOCK if blocking count > 0 (script exits 1, outputs still written, --gate review.json fails); else PASS (exit 0).

  • Name the run: python3 -I scripts/review.py --diff <change.patch> [--rules <rules.csv>] --json review.json --md review.md, then python3 -I scripts/review.py --gate review.json; outputs review.json and review.md (and review-two-axis.md only with narrative=true).
  • The request says a diff, PR, team rules or spec is here but its text is not in the conversation: still write the review skeleton now — the five sections with their headings, the detector checklist above that will run on the added lines, the Tests line, and Verdict: To be baselined · owner: author, from the diff. With team rules: state they are applied after the built-ins (custom regex rules; a built-in id with empty pattern overrides its severity, e.g. CR-TODO raised to warning or CR-NO-TESTS made blocking) and record each override. bodyHtml:
domain-modeling-runner

Wraps domain-modeling from mattpocock/skills (pinned in vendor/pins.json). Upstream is a conversational discipline — challenge terms against the glossary, sharpen fuzzy language, stress-test relationships with scenarios, record hard-to-reverse decisions as ADRs. This skill makes the checkable part deterministic (structure, identifiers, cardinalities, glossary gaps, invariants) and passes the upstream instructions and its glossary/ADR formats to the optional review step by path (../../../vendor/domain-modeling/SKILL.md), never by copy.

In a conversation: write the model now

  • Entities, relationships and glossary are stated in the conversation (CSV text or plain sentences): write model.md in this reply in this order — Diagram (Mermaid erDiagram with a title front-matter block, PK/FK markers, cardinality aliases 1 to 0+ for 1:N, 1 to 1, 0+ to 0+), Entities, Relationships, Invariants (a checklist to confirm: unique identifiers, required attributes, ownership for 1:N, uniqueness for 1:1 and N:M pairs), Glossary (**Term**: definition, _Avoid_: synonyms; supplied definitions kept word for word; any entity without one gets To be baselined · owner: Domain expert), Open questions (every error and warning, owned by the domain expert). An N:M relationship is drawn through its join entity (e.g. Enrollment between Student and Course).
  • Validate before drawing: errors E1–E6 — relationship endpoint not a defined entity, entity without identifier, cardinality not 1:1/1:N/N:M (e.g. many), N:M without join: <Entity>, duplicate attribute, bad required value; warnings W1–W3 — orphan entity, term without definition, glossary term that is not an entity. # domain-modeling-runner

Wraps `domain-modeling` from mattpocock/skills (pinned in vendor/pins.json). Upstream is a conversational discipline — challenge terms against the glossary, sharpen fuzzy language, stress-test relationships with scenarios, record hard-to-reverse decisions as ADRs. This skill makes the checkable part deterministic (structure, identifiers, cardinalities, glossary gaps, invariants) and passes the upstream instructions and its glossary/ADR formats to the optional review step by path (`../../../vendor/domain-modeling/SKILL.md`), never by copy.

## In a conversation: write the model now
- **Entities, relationships and glossary are stated in the conversation** (CSV text or plain sentences): write `model.md` **in this reply** in this order — Diagram (Mermaid `erDiagram` with a title front-matter block, PK/FK markers, cardinality aliases `1 to 0+` for 1:N, `1 to 1`, `0+ to 0+`), Entities, Relationships, Invariants (a checklist to confirm: unique identifiers, required attributes, ownership for 1:N, uniqueness for 1:1 and N:M pairs), Glossary (`**Term**:` definition, `_Avoid_:` synonyms; supplied definitions kept word for word; any entity without one gets `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: Domain expert]`), Open questions (every error and warning, owned by the domain expert). An N:M relationship is drawn through its join entity (e.g. Enrollment between Student and Course).
- **Validate before drawing**: errors E1–E6 — relationship endpoint not a defined entity, entity without identifier, cardinality not `1:1`/`1:N`/`N:M` (e.g. `many`), N:M without `join: <Entity>`, duplicate attribute, bad `required` value; warnings W1–W3 — orphan entity, term without definition, glossary term that is not an entity. Any error means the run fails: say so on line 1, leave invalid relationships out of the diagram, and list each error under Open questions. Never add an undefined entity (e.g. an Instructor that has no entity rows) to make a relationship valid.
- **Existing model plus revised files**: compare and list what is added, removed or changed (entities, attributes, `required`, type changes); every breaking change gets a migration-impact line to plan before building.
- **The request says files are attached but their contents are not in the conversation**: still write every section now from whatever the request states, with each entity, attribute, cardinality or definition not given shown as `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]` naming the file it comes from (entities CSV, relationships CSV, glossary CSV, baseline `model.json`). With a review request, also lay out the modeling review per `assets/modeling-review-template.md` — Challenged terms, Edge-case scenarios, Invariants to confirm, ADR candidates — per the upstream method. Never reply with only a request for files.
- **Relationships entirely missing** (entities only, "draw the ER diagram"): ask once for the relationships (`from,to,cardinality,name[,notes]`) instead of guessing how entities relate; definitions and cardinalities are never invented.

## Starting points
- **New** — entities, relationships and glossary become a validated model: Mermaid ER diagram, invariants, glossary, open questions.
- **Existing** — add `baseline` (the `model.json` of today's model): the proposed model is validated the same way and compared with it — what is added, removed or changed — and every breaking change gets a migration-impact line to plan before building.

## When to use

- When terms drift ("account" vs "customer"): build the glossary and see which terms lack a definition.
- NOT for: SQL migrations and RLS (`supabase-schema-rls`), tenancy audits (`multi-tenant-saas-patterns`), product requirements (`product-spec-prd`).

| `glossary` | no | `term,definition[,avoid]`. Entities without a definition get `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: Domain expert]`. |

2. **Validate** (errors E1–E6): undefined relationship endpoints, entities without identifier, bad cardinality, N:M without join, duplicate attributes, bad `required` values. **Warn** (W1–W3): orphan entities (join entities count as linked), terms without definitions, glossary terms that are not entities.

bodyHtml:
observability-setup

In a conversation: plan the setup now

  • The request asks for observability on this stack: answer in this reply, in order: (1) one list of questions, asked once — critical user journeys (≤5), error-tracking vendor (Sentry default) and DSN availability, notification channel — each with your default, then carry on with the defaults; (2) the plan table — component → file → add/change → why — covering logger, request context, error tracking, health endpoints, alert rules, SLOs, dashboard, with a line that nothing changes until "go"; (3) logging: lib/logger.ts + lib/logger/context.ts (JSON fields ts, level, msg, service, env, requestId; redaction of email, token, password, authorization, cookie, key; requestId set in middleware.ts), console.* replaced in minimal diffs, ESLint no-console: error; (4) health: app/api/health/route.ts (liveness, no dependencies) and app/api/health/deep/route.ts (bearer-protected, ≤ 3 s timeout per dependency, 503 when one is down), with tests for both; (5) an alert table — alert → threshold → window → severity tier → runbook → owner → channel — and an SLO table per journey with an error-budget policy; (6) verification on preview: force a synthetic failure (deep health 503) and confirm the alert fires end to end, and confirm a test error reaches the tracker tagged with requestId. Thresholds and SLO targets the user has not given are To be baselined · owner to be named. Never reply with only a request for the repo.
  • Part of it already exists (e.g. "we already have Sentry"): open with an inventory of what is there (Sentry server/client/edge configs, global-error.tsx, tags, source maps) and state that it is kept as is; add only what was asked (e.g. health routes and alert rules); add requestId as a Sentry tag only if it is missing, as a minimal diff; touch the logger only if console.* calls are found.
  • Bare "add observability": ask once, in one list, for the critical journeys and the alert channel; meanwhile show the plan skeleton with every SLO target and alert threshold as To be baselined · owner to be named. Never invent SLO numbers.

bodyHtml:
safe-fix

In a conversation: work the fix now

  • The bug report carries a symptom and evidence (environment, requestId, error text, "after yesterday's release"): answer in this reply with the fix plan, in order: (1) evidence — what to pull by requestId (Vercel logs, Supabase logs, Sentry event) and what each would confirm, plus the release diff to read if it followed a release; (2) the failing reproduction written before any change — the exact test (e.g. an integration test with the affected persona) and why it fails today; (3) the root cause in one sentence with file:line and its evidence, or, until the evidence is in, the ranked hypotheses (e.g. RLS policy predicate, missing JWT claim) and the evidence that settles each; (4) the minimal diff to the failing path only — no renames, no reformatting; (5) the regression test named after the bug (it('does not <bug> when <condition>')), seen red on the pre-fix code by stashing the fix; (6) verification — lint, typecheck, full unit suite, affected integration/e2e, build, and a grep of every caller of the changed code; (7) blast radius and rollback (revert the commit or Vercel Instant Rollback; a down-migration if schema changed). Facts you cannot see (paths, log lines) are To be baselined · owner to be named, never invented. Never reply with only a request for logs.
  • Asked to change shared code the quick way (e.g. "just change formatMoney"): grep the callers first and list them; when other callers (e.g. UI) rely on the current behaviour, decline the shared change in one line, fix the failing path instead (a dedicated formatter or a parser option on the export), add a regression test for that path, run the tests that cover the shared function, and state the blast radius explicitly.
  • Too little to reproduce ("sometimes the save button does nothing"): ask once, in one list, for environment, exact steps, browser, a requestId or logs; do not guess-fix. Say what follows if the evidence still gives no repro: targeted, requestId-tagged logging at the suspected hops ships first, then the repro and the fix. Never weaken, skip or delete a test to get green.
  • Asked to ship because the one target test passes: decline in one line — the full suite decides, and any test that was green and is now red is collateral that blocks the fix.

Starting points

  • Existing — the test suite is snapshotted before the fix (or your recorded baseline is used), re-run after it, and any test that was green and is now red is reported as collateral damage.
  • Only for existing: a fix always lands in code and a test suite that already exist; there is nothing to fix from scratch.

When to use

  • "Fix this bug", an error message, stack trace, failing CI job, "it used to work", production incident follow-up.
  • NOT for: new behaviour (spec-to-plan), "clean this up" (nextjs-enterprise-conventions), pipeline-only failures (ci-cd-vercel-github troubleshooting), vulnerability review (security-review).

Inputs required

InputRequiredSource
Observed behaviour + expected behaviouryesuser
Evidence: error text, stack, failing test name, requestId, logs, stepsyes (at least one)user / logs
Environment where it happens (local / preview / prod) and version/shayesuser — ask once
Repo accessyesrepo

Missing facts do not stop the fix plan: mark them To be baselined · owner to be named and ask at the end. Only when there is no evidence at all to reproduce from, ask once for it and do not guess-fix.

Procedure

  1. Read ../../../shared/token-efficiency.md (rules 2, 8, 9, 10 govern this skill) and references/never-collateral.md.
  2. Reproduce. Write the smallest deterministic reproduction: a failing unit/integration test, or an exact command/request. If it cannot be reproduced, stop and gather more evidence (references/safe-fix-method.md §Reproduce). No fix without a repro. (gate: repro exists and fails)
  3. Isolate. If the upstream skill superpowers:systematic-debugging is installed (see VENDORED.md), invoke it for this step; otherwise follow references/safe-fix-method.md §Isolate: trace from symptom to cause with evidence at each hop, bisect (git / inputs / layers), state the root cause in one sentence with file:line. Distinguish root cause from trigger.
  4. Plan the fix. Post: root cause, the single path to change, files touched (expect 1–3), the regression test, blast radius (who else calls this), rollback. Wait for "go" if the fix touches shared code, schema, auth, or >3 files. (gate: plan→approve)
  5. Minimal diff. Change only the failing path. No renames, no reformatting, no "while I'm here". If the fix needs a refactor, do the refactor as a separate, behaviour-preserving step with the suite green in between.
  6. Regression test. The repro from step 2 becomes a permanent test named after the bug (it('does not <bug> when <condition>')). It must fail on the pre-fix code (verify by stashing the fix once) and pass after. (gate: build→test)
  7. Verify the whole, not the part. Run lint, typecheck, the full unit suite, affected integration/e2e, and build. Re-check every caller of the changed function (grep) for changed assumptions. (gate: test→verify)
  8. Fix in code, not data. If the bug produced bad rows, handle the scenario in code going forward and write a one-off, reviewed migration/backfill for the existing rows — never hand-edit data as the fix.
  9. Report with assets/fix-report.md; update docs/HANDOFF.md.

Output

ArtifactForm
Root cause statementone sentence, file:line, evidence
Diffminimal; 1–3 files typical
Regression testtests/**, named after the bug
Verificationcommand summary table
Fix reportassets/fix-report.md filled, in PR description

Self-check

  • [ ] Repro existed and failed before the change
  • [ ] Root cause stated with evidence (not "probably")
  • [ ] Diff touches only the failing path; no formatting/renames/unrelated edits
  • [ ] Regression test fails on old code, passes on new
  • [ ] Full suite green; callers of changed code re-checked
  • [ ] No data patched by hand; no any, no try/catch swallow, no test skipped or weakened
  • [ ] Rollback stated

References

  • references/safe-fix-method.md — reproduce → isolate → minimal diff → regression test → verify, with techniques
  • references/never-collateral.md — the guardrails (what a fix may never do)
  • references/common-bugs-stack.md — recurring causes in Next.js/Supabase/Vercel apps
  • assets/fix-report.md — report template
  • scripts/safefix.py — baseline / verify: snapshots the test suite before a fix and fails (exit 1) on any newly failing test

How to run (automation, when commands can run)

This skill is executable. Collect the inputs above, then run python3 scripts/run_skill.py build/safe-fix --input <name>=<value> … --out <dir> (see --explain build/safe-fix). Report the run.json results; do not hand-write the deliverables the scripts produce. Typical flow: run once before the fix (writes baseline.json), apply the fix, run again with --input baseline=<dir>/baseline.json; any newly failing test is collateral and the run exits 1.

In a conversation: write the plan now

  • The request names the feature (SPEC section, ticket, scope): answer in this reply with, in order: (1) the context read first — docs/SPEC.md (the named section), CLAUDE.md, docs/HANDOFF.md — and what each contributes, or To be baselined · owner to be named where their contents are not in the conversation; (2) at most 5 clarifying questions in one round, each with your default answer, then plan on the defaults; (3) the plan for docs/plans/<yyyy-mm-dd>-<slug>.md: file table (path → create/modify → why); ordered tasks, each with files, acceptance criterion, test(s), size S/M/L and rollback; a risk table (risk → mitigation → owner); a concrete rollback (revert tag, flag off, down-migration). Cross-cutting work the SPEC implies gets its own task — an audit-log write when the feature must be audited, an RLS negative test (another tenant's user gets nothing) when data is tenant-scoped, a security-review task when auth or RLS changes; (4) a closing line: no code is written until you reply "go". Never reply with only a request for the SPEC.
  • Too big for one thread (more than ~8 tasks, or several sub-systems such as plans, Stripe, invoices, dunning, admin UI): do not write one long plan. Split it into separate plans, one per thread; list them in build order with the dependency that sets the order, say which plan comes first and why, and give only that first plan's outline. Do not start building.
  • No feature named ("make a plan for the new feature"): ask once which feature or SPEC section, and stop; do not invent scope or tasks.
  • Asked to fill in tests or rollbacks a thin SPEC does not state: decline in one line (invented acceptance criteria are not the team's), still list the tasks, and mark their acceptance, tests and rollback To be baselined · owner: Tech lead.

Starting points

  • New — the SPEC section becomes a task-gated plan: tasks with acceptance, tests, rollback, files and size; anything the SPEC does not say is an owned TBD.
  • Existing — add repo: every file a task names is looked up and marked modify or create, a task that edits an applied migration or numbers a new one out of order is flagged in a "Repo check" section before approve.

When to use

  • "Plan this feature", "how should we build X", a ticket or SPEC section is handed over for implementation.
  • Any change touching >3 files, schema, auth, CI, or billing — the plan gate is mandatory.
  • NOT for: bugs (safe-fix), product definition (product-spec-prd), repo setup (project-bootstrap).

Procedure

  1. Read ../../../shared/token-efficiency.md, ../../../shared/stack-conventions.md, ../../../shared/quality-bar.md, then docs/SPEC.md, CLAUDE.md, docs/HANDOFF.md in the repo.

  8. Verify. All acceptance criteria checked, lint/typecheck/unit/build green, e2e for touched critical paths. Paste the command summary.

- **Too big for one thread** (more than ~8 tasks, or several sub-systems such as plans, Stripe, invoices, dunning, admin UI): do not write one long plan. Split it into separate plans, one per thread; list them in build order with the dependency that sets the order, say which plan comes first and why, and give only that first plan's outline. Do not start building.
- **No feature named** ("make a plan for the new feature"): ask once which feature or SPEC section, and stop; do not invent scope or tasks.
- **Asked to fill in tests or rollbacks a thin SPEC does not state**: decline in one line (invented acceptance criteria are not the team's), still list the tasks, and mark their acceptance, tests and rollback `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: Tech lead]`.

## Starting points
- **New** — the SPEC section becomes a task-gated plan: tasks with acceptance, tests, rollback, files and size; anything the SPEC does not say is an owned TBD.
- **Existing** — add `repo`: every file a task names is looked up and marked modify or create, a task that edits an applied migration or numbers a new one out of order is flagged in a "Repo check" section before approve.

## When to use
- "Plan this feature", "how should we build X", a ticket or SPEC section is handed over for implementation.
- Any change touching >3 files, schema, auth, CI, or billing — the plan gate is mandatory.
- NOT for: bugs (`safe-fix`), product definition (`product-spec-prd`), repo setup (`project-bootstrap`).

## Inputs required
| Input | Required | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Feature description or SPEC section / ticket | yes | user / `docs/SPEC.md` |
| Repo access (to read current structure) | yes | repo |
| Constraints (deadline, no-schema-change, flag-gated, etc.) | no | user |
| `docs/HANDOFF.md` state | yes if exists | repo |

Missing facts do not stop the plan: mark them `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]` and ask at the end. Only when no feature or SPEC section is named, ask once which one and stop.

## Procedure
1. Read `../../../shared/token-efficiency.md`, `../../../shared/stack-conventions.md`, `../../../shared/quality-bar.md`, then `docs/SPEC.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `docs/HANDOFF.md` in the repo.
2. **Clarify (brainstorm).** If the upstream skill `superpowers:brainstorming` is installed (see VENDORED.md), invoke it for this step; otherwise follow `references/brainstorm-fallback.md`. Output: ≤5 open questions, each with your default answer. Ask once. *(gate: plan inputs)*
3. **Map the change.** Read every file the change touches. Produce the file table: path → create/modify → why. Flag anything that violates `shared/stack-conventions.md`.
4. **Write the plan.** If `superpowers:writing-plans` is installed, invoke it and then apply the gates below; otherwise use `assets/plan-template.md` directly and follow `references/plan-method.md`. Every task has: files, acceptance criterion, test(s), estimate (S/M/L), rollback.
5. **Risk and rollback.** Fill the risk table (schema, auth, data migration, external API). Each risk: mitigation + owner. Rollback must be concrete (revert tag, disable flag, down-migration).
6. **Present and stop.** Post the plan summary (≤10 lines + link to `docs/plans/<slug>.md`). Wait for "go". *(gate: plan→approve)*
7. **Execute in task order** after approval. Per task: build → run its tests → run the full unit suite → mark done in the plan file. If `superpowers:executing-plans` is installed, invoke it for the loop. *(gates: build→test→verify)*
8. **Verify.** All acceptance criteria checked, lint/typecheck/unit/build green, e2e for touched critical paths. Paste the command summary.
9. Update `docs/HANDOFF.md` (changed files, open items, next-thread prompt).

## Output
| Artifact | Path |
|---|---|
| Plan | `docs/plans/<yyyy-mm-dd>-<slug>.md` (from `assets/plan-template.md`) |
| Plan summary | chat, ≤10 lines |
| Post-build verification | chat, command output summary |
| HANDOFF | `docs/HANDOFF.md` |

## Self-check
- [ ] Every task has files, acceptance criterion, test, rollback
- [ ] No code written before "go"
- [ ] File table came from reading the repo, not memory
- [ ] Schema changes route to `supabase-schema-rls`; auth/RLS changes get `security-review` as a task
- [ ] Plan fits one thread; if not, split and say so
- [ ] Unknowns marked `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]`

## References
- `references/plan-method.md` — task decomposition rules, sizing, gate definitions
- `references/brainstorm-fallback.md` — question method when superpowers is absent
- `assets/plan-template.md` — plan file template
- `scripts/plan.py` — SPEC section → plan.md (tasks, gates, rollback) + tasks.csv; unknown fields marked `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]`

## How to run (automation, when commands can run)
This skill is executable. Collect the inputs above, then run `python3 scripts/run_skill.py build/spec-to-plan --input <name>=<value> … --out <dir>` (see `--explain build/spec-to-plan`). Report the `run.json` results; do not hand-write the deliverables the scripts produce. Fields the SPEC does not state come out as `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]`; fill them (or the SPEC) before asking for the approve gate.

card: Root cause from a failure log
name: systematic-debugging-runner
description: Use when a test fails, a build breaks or an exception shows up and you want the evidence organised before anyone touches the code — "why is this test failing", "debug this stack trace", "did my change break this", "root-cause this error". Produces debug.json and debug-log.md (Symptom, Evidence, Hypotheses, Next experiment, Fix gate) by parsing a Python, JS/TS or Java failure log, finding the innermost in-repo frame, correlating frames with the lines a recent diff touched (regression-likely vs not) and ranking hypotheses that each carry a falsifying test; the fix gate stays closed until one is confirmed.
