bodyHtml:
systematic-debugging-runner

Wraps systematic-debugging from obra/superpowers (pinned in vendor/pins.json). The upstream skill is the method; this skill makes its first three phases (read the error, check recent changes, form testable hypotheses) a deterministic run, and passes the upstream instructions to the optional narrative step by path (../../../vendor/systematic-debugging/SKILL.md), never by copy.

In a conversation: organise the evidence now

  • The failure log is in the conversation: write the debug log in this reply in this order — Symptom (error type and message quoted from the log: the last Python exception, the deepest Java Caused by:), Evidence (stack frames innermost first with file:line and function; the innermost in-repo frame named; site-packages, node_modules, runtime and JDK/JUnit frames excluded), classification (regression-likely only when a frame's file and line fall inside a hunk the diff changed; no-diff when no diff was given), Hypotheses (a table ranked by evidence score — changed line in the stack 3, changed file or error-type signal at an in-repo frame 2, weak 1 — each with one falsifying test and status untested), Next experiment (establish a repro if none was given, then the top hypothesis's falsifying test), Fix gate: closed — it opens only when an experiment confirms a hypothesis and a failing test reproduces the defect. Missing repro steps are To be baselined · owner: Reporting engineer and become experiment 1.
  • The request says a log, diff or repro is here but its text is not in the conversation: still write all five sections now from what the request states (test framework, error type, whether a diff exists), with each value not given — error message, frames, innermost in-repo frame, overlapping hunk — shown as To be baselined · owner to be named naming the input it comes from. With a write-up request, also lay out the investigation per assets/investigation-template.md (Symptom, Evidence, Hypotheses, Next experiment, Open questions) following the upstream method. Never reply with only a request for the log.
  • No log at all ("my build is broken"): ask once for the failure output (and the diff since the last green build and repro steps if available). Do not guess the error.
  • Log with no exception, or asked to "just tell me the bug": say on line 1 that no parsable exception was found, so the run stops (exit 2) rather than inventing a symptom; name no bug and propose no fix. Ask for the output that contains the error or stack trace. No output ever proposes a fix while the gate is closed.

Starting points

  • Existing — the failure log (with the recent diff and repro steps when you have them) becomes an evidence-first debug log: symptom, evidence, ranked hypotheses, the next experiment, and a fix gate that stays closed until the root cause is proven.
  • Only for existing: debugging always starts from a failure in code that already runs; there is no from-scratch starting point.

When to use

  • A failing test, CI job or crash with a stack trace, before proposing any fix.
  • "Did my change break this?" — supply the diff and read the classification.
  • NOT for: applying or verifying the fix (safe-fix), security review of a diff (security-review), performance profiling, flaky-test statistics across many runs.

Inputs required

InputRequiredSource
logyesTest output or stack trace as text. Python tracebacks and pytest output, JS/TS (Node, Jest, Vitest), Java (incl. Caused by: chains).
diffnoUnified diff since the last green build. Without it the classification is no-diff.
repronoExact steps to reproduce (assets/repro-template.md). Missing → marked To be baselined · owner: Reporting engineer and made experiment 1.
narrativenotrue runs the LLM step that writes the investigation narrative.

Procedure

  1. Parse the log (scripts/debug_log.py): error type and message (the deepest Java Caused by:; the last Python exception), stack frames (file, line, function), stored innermost first.
  2. Find the innermost in-repo frame: skip site-packages, node_modules, runtime and JDK/JUnit frames (references/debug-method.md).
  3. Correlate with the diff: a frame overlaps by file (path-suffix or Java package path) and by line (inside a changed hunk). Any overlap → regression-likely.
  4. Rank hypotheses by evidence: changed line in the stack (3) > changed file or error-type signal at an in-repo frame (2) > weak (1). Each has one falsifying test and status untested.
  5. Next experiment: establish a repro if none was given, then run the top hypothesis's falsifying test.
  6. Fix gate: always written closed. It opens only when a hypothesis is confirmed by its experiment and a failing test reproduces the defect; after three failed fixes, stop and question the design.
  7. Optional: with narrative=true the LLM fills assets/investigation-template.md from the debug log and the upstream method.

Output

  • debug.json — symptom, frames (with in-repo and overlap flags), classification, ranked hypotheses, next experiments, gate. Checked by debug_log.py --validate (ranked, every hypothesis falsifiable, gate not open without confirmation).
  • debug-log.md — Symptom, Evidence, Hypotheses, Next experiment, Fix gate.
  • investigation.md (only with narrative=true) — narrative per assets/investigation-template.md.

Self-check

  • [ ] Error type and message are quoted from the log, never paraphrased into a different error
  • [ ] Every hypothesis has a falsifying test and the table is ranked by evidence score
  • [ ] Regression claims rest on a frame that the diff touches, not on timing alone
  • [ ] Missing repro is marked with an owner and is experiment 1
  • [ ] The fix gate says NO; no fix is proposed in any output

References

  • references/debug-method.md — parsing rules, in-repo heuristics, scoring and the gate
  • assets/repro-template.md — reproduction steps layout
  • assets/investigation-template.md — narrative template for the optional LLM step
  • scripts/debug_log.py — parser, correlator and contract validator (argparse; stdlib)
  • Upstream method: vendor/systematic-debugging/ (SKILL.md, root-cause-tracing.md)

How to run (automation, when commands can run)

This skill is executable. Collect the inputs below, then run python3 scripts/run_skill.py build/systematic-debugging-runner --input <name>=<value> … --out <dir> (see --explain build/systematic-debugging-runner). Report the run.json results; do not hand-write the deliverables the scripts produce. A log with no parsable exception stops the run (script exit 2) instead of inventing a symptom.

## In a conversation: organise the evidence now
- **The failure log is in the conversation**: write the debug log **in this reply** in this order — Symptom (error type and message quoted from the log: the last Python exception, the deepest Java `Caused by:`), Evidence (stack frames innermost first with file:line and function; the innermost in-repo frame named; site-packages, node_modules, runtime and JDK/JUnit frames excluded), classification (`regression-likely` only when a frame's file and line fall inside a hunk the diff changed; `no-diff` when no diff was given), Hypotheses (a table ranked by evidence score — changed line in the stack 3, changed file or error-type signal at an in-repo frame 2, weak 1 — each with one falsifying test and status `untested`), Next experiment (establish a repro if none was given, then the top hypothesis's falsifying test), Fix gate: **closed** — it opens only when an experiment confirms a hypothesis and a failing test reproduces the defect. Missing repro steps are `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: Reporting engineer]` and become experiment 1.
- **The request says a log, diff or repro is here but its text is not in the conversation**: still write all five sections now from what the request states (test framework, error type, whether a diff exists), with each value not given — error message, frames, innermost in-repo frame, overlapping hunk — shown as `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]` naming the input it comes from. With a write-up request, also lay out the investigation per `assets/investigation-template.md` (Symptom, Evidence, Hypotheses, Next experiment, Open questions) following the upstream method. Never reply with only a request for the log.
- **No log at all** ("my build is broken"): ask once for the failure output (and the diff since the last green build and repro steps if available). Do not guess the error.
- **Log with no exception, or asked to "just tell me the bug"**: say on line 1 that no parsable exception was found, so the run stops (exit 2) rather than inventing a symptom; name no bug and propose no fix. Ask for the output that contains the error or stack trace. No output ever proposes a fix while the gate is closed.

## Starting points
- **Existing** — the failure log (with the recent diff and repro steps when you have them) becomes an evidence-first debug log: symptom, evidence, ranked hypotheses, the next experiment, and a fix gate that stays closed until the root cause is proven.
- Only for existing: debugging always starts from a failure in code that already runs; there is no from-scratch starting point.

## When to use
- A failing test, CI job or crash with a stack trace, before proposing any fix.
- "Did my change break this?" — supply the diff and read the classification.
- NOT for: applying or verifying the fix (`safe-fix`), security review of a diff (`security-review`), performance profiling, flaky-test statistics across many runs.

## Inputs required
| Input | Required | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `log` | yes | Test output or stack trace as text. Python tracebacks and pytest output, JS/TS (Node, Jest, Vitest), Java (incl. `Caused by:` chains). |
| `diff` | no | Unified diff since the last green build. Without it the classification is `no-diff`. |
| `repro` | no | Exact steps to reproduce (assets/repro-template.md). Missing → marked `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: Reporting engineer]` and made experiment 1. |
| `narrative` | no | `true` runs the LLM step that writes the investigation narrative. |

## Procedure
1. **Parse the log** (`scripts/debug_log.py`): error type and message (the deepest Java `Caused by:`; the last Python exception), stack frames (file, line, function), stored innermost first.
2. **Find the innermost in-repo frame**: skip site-packages, node_modules, runtime and JDK/JUnit frames (`references/debug-method.md`).
3. **Correlate with the diff**: a frame overlaps by file (path-suffix or Java package path) and by line (inside a changed hunk). Any overlap → `regression-likely`.
4. **Rank hypotheses by evidence**: changed line in the stack (3) > changed file or error-type signal at an in-repo frame (2) > weak (1). Each has one falsifying test and status `untested`.
5. **Next experiment**: establish a repro if none was given, then run the top hypothesis's falsifying test.
6. **Fix gate**: always written closed. It opens only when a hypothesis is confirmed by its experiment and a failing test reproduces the defect; after three failed fixes, stop and question the design.
7. Optional: with `narrative=true` the LLM fills `assets/investigation-template.md` from the debug log and the upstream method.

## Output
- `debug.json` — symptom, frames (with in-repo and overlap flags), classification, ranked hypotheses, next experiments, gate. Checked by `debug_log.py --validate` (ranked, every hypothesis falsifiable, gate not open without confirmation).
- `debug-log.md` — Symptom, Evidence, Hypotheses, Next experiment, Fix gate.
- `investigation.md` (only with `narrative=true`) — narrative per `assets/investigation-template.md`.

## Self-check
- [ ] Error type and message are quoted from the log, never paraphrased into a different error
- [ ] Every hypothesis has a falsifying test and the table is ranked by evidence score
- [ ] Regression claims rest on a frame that the diff touches, not on timing alone
- [ ] Missing repro is marked with an owner and is experiment 1
- [ ] The fix gate says NO; no fix is proposed in any output

## References
- `references/debug-method.md` — parsing rules, in-repo heuristics, scoring and the gate
- `assets/repro-template.md` — reproduction steps layout
- `assets/investigation-template.md` — narrative template for the optional LLM step
- `scripts/debug_log.py` — parser, correlator and contract validator (argparse; stdlib)
- Upstream method: `vendor/systematic-debugging/` (SKILL.md, root-cause-tracing.md)

## How to run (automation, when commands can run)
This skill is executable. Collect the inputs below, then run `python3 scripts/run_skill.py build/systematic-debugging-runner --input <name>=<value> … --out <dir>` (see `--explain build/systematic-debugging-runner`). Report the `run.json` results; do not hand-write the deliverables the scripts produce. A log with no parsable exception stops the run (script exit 2) instead of inventing a symptom.

webapp-testing-runner

Wraps webapp-testing from anthropics/skills (pinned in vendor/pins.json). Upstream drives a live browser with native Python Playwright; the portal cannot launch one, so this skill turns the same method (headless Chromium, wait for networkidle, descriptive selectors) into a generator plus static checks, and passes the upstream instructions to the optional review step by path (../../../vendor/webapp-testing/SKILL.md), never by copy.

In a conversation: write the tests now

  • The flows are stated in the conversation (flows JSON or plain steps): write both outputs in this reply — test_flows.py with one test_<flow> per flow using the pytest-playwright page fixture, page.wait_for_load_state("networkidle") after every goto, role=/text=/label=/placeholder=/testid= mapped to get_by_role/get_by_text/get_by_label/get_by_placeholder/get_by_test_id, the base URL read from the BASE_URL environment variable, and GENERATED, NOT EXECUTED in the module docstring; then flows-report.md — Flows (coverage matrix: steps per action, assertions, selector kinds), Generated tests, Warnings (nth-child/nth-of-type, XPath, generated class names, long CSS chains, each with a better selector kind; flows not starting with goto or without an expect_* step), How to run (pip install pytest-playwright && playwright install chromium, then BASE_URL=… pytest test_flows.py). State plainly that the tests were generated and compile-checked, not executed; claim no pass/fail.
  • Validate first: known actions only (goto, click, fill, expect_text, expect_url — hover is not one), required fields per action, unique flow names, non-empty steps, base_url present. Any error: report every error, write no test file, and say the run failed.
  • Existing e2e tests supplied: match each flow to the existing test that covers it, list it with the covering test and do not regenerate it; generate only the gaps, and still report selector warnings for every flow.
  • The request says a flows file or test folder is here but its contents are not in the conversation: still write the skeleton now — one test function per flow the request names, the report sections above, and every selector, value or URL not given as To be baselined · owner to be named naming the flows file. With a review request, also lay out the test-plan review per assets/test-plan-review-template.md (Reconnaissance plan, Selector review, Gaps, How to run) per the upstream method. Never reply with only a request for files.
  • No flows at all ("write e2e tests for my app"): ask once for the flows JSON (assets/flows-template.json) — pages, selectors and URLs are never invented.

Starting points

  • New — every flow is validated and turned into a pytest-playwright test (generated and compile-checked, never executed here).
  • Existing — add your current e2e folder: its tests are read, flows they already cover are listed with the covering test and not generated again, and only the gaps are written.

When to use

  • Turning a list of user journeys into a Playwright suite the team can run locally or in CI.
  • Reviewing flow selectors for brittleness before the suite is written.
  • NOT for: executing tests or reporting pass/fail (needs a browser), unit/integration test scaffolding (test-strategy-tdd), visual or load testing.

Inputs required

InputRequiredSource
flowsyesJSON per assets/flows-template.json. Actions: goto(value), click(selector), fill(selector, value), expect_text(value[, selector]), expect_url(value).
narrativenotrue runs the LLM step that writes the test-plan review.

The base URL is never guessed: the generated file reads BASE_URL from the environment; a placeholder in the JSON makes tests skip until it is set.

Procedure

  1. Validate (scripts/gen_tests.py): base_url present, flows non-empty, unique names, known actions, required fields per action, string types. Any error → report with the errors, no test file, exit 1.
  2. Warn on selector style: nth-child/nth-of-type, XPath, generated class names, long CSS chains (warning); bare CSS (info); flows not starting with goto or with no expect_* step.
  3. Generate test_flows.py: one test_<flow> per flow using the pytest-playwright page fixture; goto is followed by wait_for_load_state("networkidle"); role=/text=/label=/placeholder=/testid= map to get_by_* locators.

  5. Report flows-report.md: coverage matrix (steps per action, assertions, selector kinds per flow), static-check result, warnings, how to run (incl. the upstream with_server.py helper).
  6. Optional: with narrative=true the LLM fills assets/test-plan-review-template.md.

Output

  • test_flows.py — runnable with BASE_URL=… pytest test_flows.py after pip install pytest-playwright && playwright install chromium.
  • flows-report.md — Flows, Generated tests, Warnings, How to run.

Self-check

  • [ ] Every flow became exactly one test function; names are unique
  • [ ] Every flow has at least one assertion, or a warning says it does not
  • [ ] Brittle selectors are listed under Warnings with a better alternative kind
  • [ ] The file compiles and says GENERATED, NOT EXECUTED; no pass/fail result is claimed anywhere
  • [ ] No URL or credential was invented; values come from the flows file

References

  • references/flow-format.md — flow JSON schema, selector mapping, warning rules
  • assets/flows-template.json — input layout
  • assets/test-plan-review-template.md — narrative template for the optional LLM step
  • scripts/gen_tests.py — validator, generator and compile check (argparse; stdlib)

- **The flows are stated in the conversation** (flows JSON or plain steps): write both outputs **in this reply** — `test_flows.py` with one `test_<flow>` per flow using the pytest-playwright `page` fixture, `page.wait_for_load_state("networkidle")` after every `goto`, `role=`/`text=`/`label=`/`placeholder=`/`testid=` mapped to `get_by_role`/`get_by_text`/`get_by_label`/`get_by_placeholder`/`get_by_test_id`, the base URL read from the `BASE_URL` environment variable, and `GENERATED, NOT EXECUTED` in the module docstring; then `flows-report.md` — Flows (coverage matrix: steps per action, assertions, selector kinds), Generated tests, Warnings (nth-child/nth-of-type, XPath, generated class names, long CSS chains, each with a better selector kind; flows not starting with `goto` or without an `expect_*` step), How to run (`pip install pytest-playwright && playwright install chromium`, then `BASE_URL=… pytest test_flows.py`). State plainly that the tests were generated and compile-checked, not executed; claim no pass/fail.
- **Validate first**: known actions only (`goto`, `click`, `fill`, `expect_text`, `expect_url` — `hover` is not one), required fields per action, unique flow names, non-empty steps, base_url present. Any error: report every error, write no test file, and say the run failed.
- **Existing e2e tests supplied**: match each flow to the existing test that covers it, list it with the covering test and do not regenerate it; generate only the gaps, and still report selector warnings for every flow.
- **The request says a flows file or test folder is here but its contents are not in the conversation**: still write the skeleton now — one test function per flow the request names, the report sections above, and every selector, value or URL not given as `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]` naming the flows file. With a review request, also lay out the test-plan review per `assets/test-plan-review-template.md` (Reconnaissance plan, Selector review, Gaps, How to run) per the upstream method. Never reply with only a request for files.
- **No flows at all** ("write e2e tests for my app"): ask once for the flows JSON (`assets/flows-template.json`) — pages, selectors and URLs are never invented.

## Starting points
- **New** — every flow is validated and turned into a pytest-playwright test (generated and compile-checked, never executed here).
- **Existing** — add your current e2e folder: its tests are read, flows they already cover are listed with the covering test and not generated again, and only the gaps are written.

## When to use
- Turning a list of user journeys into a Playwright suite the team can run locally or in CI.
- Reviewing flow selectors for brittleness before the suite is written.
- NOT for: executing tests or reporting pass/fail (needs a browser), unit/integration test scaffolding (`test-strategy-tdd`), visual or load testing.

## Inputs required
| Input | Required | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `flows` | yes | JSON per `assets/flows-template.json`. Actions: `goto`(value), `click`(selector), `fill`(selector, value), `expect_text`(value[, selector]), `expect_url`(value). |
| `narrative` | no | `true` runs the LLM step that writes the test-plan review. |

The base URL is never guessed: the generated file reads `BASE_URL` from the environment; a placeholder in the JSON makes tests skip until it is set.

## Procedure
1. **Validate** (`scripts/gen_tests.py`): base_url present, flows non-empty, unique names, known actions, required fields per action, string types. Any error → report with the errors, no test file, exit 1.
2. **Warn** on selector style: nth-child/nth-of-type, XPath, generated class names, long CSS chains (warning); bare CSS (info); flows not starting with `goto` or with no `expect_*` step.
3. **Generate** `test_flows.py`: one `test_<flow>` per flow using the pytest-playwright `page` fixture; `goto` is followed by `wait_for_load_state("networkidle")`; `role=`/`text=`/`label=`/`placeholder=`/`testid=` map to `get_by_*` locators.
4. **Verify** with `compile()` and stamp `GENERATED, NOT EXECUTED` in the module docstring.
5. **Report** `flows-report.md`: coverage matrix (steps per action, assertions, selector kinds per flow), static-check result, warnings, how to run (incl. the upstream `with_server.py` helper).
6. Optional: with `narrative=true` the LLM fills `assets/test-plan-review-template.md`.

## Output
- `test_flows.py` — runnable with `BASE_URL=… pytest test_flows.py` after `pip install pytest-playwright && playwright install chromium`.
- `flows-report.md` — Flows, Generated tests, Warnings, How to run.
- `test-plan-review.md` (only with `narrative=true`).

## Self-check
- [ ] Every flow became exactly one test function; names are unique
- [ ] Every flow has at least one assertion, or a warning says it does not
- [ ] Brittle selectors are listed under Warnings with a better alternative kind
- [ ] The file compiles and says GENERATED, NOT EXECUTED; no pass/fail result is claimed anywhere
- [ ] No URL or credential was invented; values come from the flows file

## References
- `references/flow-format.md` — flow JSON schema, selector mapping, warning rules
- `assets/flows-template.json` — input layout
- `assets/test-plan-review-template.md` — narrative template for the optional LLM step
- `scripts/gen_tests.py` — validator, generator and compile check (argparse; stdlib)
- Upstream method: `vendor/webapp-testing/SKILL.md` (and its server-lifecycle helper, vendor/webapp-testing/scripts/with_server.py)

bodyHtml:
Interview Prep (truth-locked)

In a conversation: prepare the candidate now

  • The request names the round, the interviewers and the JD / story bank (even if the files are "attached" and their contents are not in the conversation): build the prep pack in this reply, in this order: (1) traceability table — JD competency (C1–C10 from references/competency-map.md, ranked by JD emphasis) → story ID → fit STRONG / ADEQUATE / GAP; (2) STAR+R stories, each ≤120 words and citing [SB-nn] or [MR-Lnn]; (3) likely questions for this round type, each mapped to a story ID or GAP; (4) for hiring-manager, CIO/CEO or executive rounds, a 90-day plan on the Days 1–30 / 31–60 / 61–90 skeleton with an owner per item, built only from JD facts, unknowns To be baselined · owner to be named; (5) questions to ask, grouped by interviewer title (e.g., business VP, peer directors, principal architect; CIO-specific questions for a CIO round); (6) gaps and how to handle each honestly. Where story content is not visible, keep the user's SB ids and mark the content To be baselined · owner: user, source SB-nn; never invent it. Never reply with only a request for files. Chat reply ≤50 words outside the pack.
  • Asked to make up a story ("make up a SOX remediation story"): decline in one line, naming the TRUTH LOCK rule — every story must trace to the story bank or résumé, and an invented story fails the first follow-up question. Show the competency (SOX/audit → C7 Risk, security and compliance) as GAP in the traceability table, then offer (a) to interview the user for a true adjacent example, or (b) an honest "closest experience and how I would approach it" answer outline.
  • No story bank and no master résumé: ask once for the story bank (or the résumé, to build one by interviewing the user). Do not fill stories from memory and do not run a mock round on invented stories.

Starting points

  • New — the JD's competencies are mapped to your story bank (gaps stay gaps — nothing is invented), with the round's likely questions, questions to ask and a 90-day plan skeleton.
  • Existing — add your debrief from the last round: stories you already told are marked, competencies where every story is spent and JD competencies not shown yet are listed, and the questions already asked are kept for consistent follow-ups.

When to use

  • "I have a panel interview Thursday", "grill me for the CIO round", "map my stories to this JD", "draft my 90-day plan", "what should I ask them".
  • Mock-interview mode: user asks to be questioned and scored.
  • NOT for: résumé rewriting (resume-tailor), post-interview thank-you notes (outreach-and-followup), offer decisions (offer-evaluator).

Inputs required

InputRequiredSource
Story bank (STAR+R entries with stable IDs)yesuser file; format in assets/story-bank.example.md
Master résuméyes (if story bank is thin)user file; same format as resume-tailor
JD textyesuser paste
Round type and interviewers (titles)yesuser
Company context (public: strategy, recent news, tech stack)nouser or web search, each fact sourced
Interview date and format (virtual/onsite, length, case prompt)nouser

Story bank named but its contents not visible: build the pack anyway with the SB ids and To be baselined · owner to be named story content. No story bank and no résumé: ask once; offer to build it from the master résumé by interviewing the user (one question per bullet). Never fill it from memory.

TRUTH LOCK (hard rule)

  1. Every story, number, title and outcome traces to a story-bank ID [SB-nn] or résumé line [MR-Lnn].
  2. Allowed: reframe a story for a different competency, tighten, pick which details to lead with, add a Reflection sentence the user confirms.
  3. Not allowed: invent a story, add a metric, change the user's role in the story, upgrade "contributed" to "led".
  4. If the JD needs a competency with no story, say so and offer: (a) interview the user for a true example, or (b) prepare an honest "here is the closest experience and how I would approach it" answer.
  5. Output includes a traceability table: competency → story ID → fit (STRONG / ADEQUATE / GAP).

Procedure

  1. Read ../../../shared/quality-bar.md and ../../../shared/writing-style.md.
  2. Map JD responsibilities to the competencies in references/competency-map.md. Rank by JD emphasis.
  3. For each competency, select the best story from the story bank. Rewrite it in STAR+R per references/star-r-format.md (≤120 words spoken, ~90 seconds). Cite the ID.
  4. Pull the question bank for the round type from references/question-bank.md. Pair each likely question with a story ID or a GAP note.
  5. If the round is hiring manager, CIO/CEO or board-style: draft the 90-day plan from assets/90-day-plan.md using only JD facts and sourced company facts. Mark unknowns To be baselined · owner to be named.
  6. Select 6–8 questions to ask from references/questions-to-ask.md, tuned to interviewer title.
  7. Mock mode: ask one question at a time, score the answer against the STAR+R rubric (structure, specificity, scale, result, reflection; 1–5 each), give one fix, move on. Do not score stories not in the bank.
  8. Run the self-check. Reply ≤50 words outside the artifact.

Output

Markdown file prep-<company>-<round>.md:

  1. Competency → story traceability table
  2. STAR+R stories (ranked by JD emphasis)
  3. Likely questions for this round with story mapping
  4. 90-day plan draft (if applicable)
  5. Questions to ask (by interviewer)
  6. Gaps and how to handle them honestly

Self-check

  • [ ] Every story cites [SB-nn] or [MR-Lnn]; traceability table complete
  • [ ] No metric or role claim beyond the source; Reflection lines confirmed by user or marked [confirm]
  • [ ] Each story ≤120 words; Result contains a number where the source has one
  • [ ] Question bank matches the round type; interviewer titles respected
  • [ ] 90-day plan uses only JD and sourced facts; unknowns carry an owner
  • [ ] No author personal data pulled from memory

References

# Interview Prep (truth-locked)

## In a conversation: prepare the candidate now
- **The request names the round, the interviewers and the JD / story bank** (even if the files are "attached" and their contents are not in the conversation): build the prep pack in this reply, in this order: (1) traceability table — JD competency (C1–C10 from `references/competency-map.md`, ranked by JD emphasis) → story ID → fit STRONG / ADEQUATE / GAP; (2) STAR+R stories, each ≤120 words and citing `[SB-nn]` or `[MR-Lnn]`; (3) likely questions for this round type, each mapped to a story ID or GAP; (4) for hiring-manager, CIO/CEO or executive rounds, a 90-day plan on the Days 1–30 / 31–60 / 61–90 skeleton with an owner per item, built only from JD facts, unknowns `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]`; (5) questions to ask, grouped by interviewer title (e.g., business VP, peer directors, principal architect; CIO-specific questions for a CIO round); (6) gaps and how to handle each honestly. Where story content is not visible, keep the user's SB ids and mark the content `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: user, source SB-nn]`; never invent it. Never reply with only a request for files. Chat reply ≤50 words outside the pack.
- **Asked to make up a story** ("make up a SOX remediation story"): decline in one line, naming the **TRUTH LOCK** rule — every story must trace to the story bank or résumé, and an invented story fails the first follow-up question. Show the competency (SOX/audit → C7 Risk, security and compliance) as **GAP** in the traceability table, then offer (a) to interview the user for a true adjacent example, or (b) an honest "closest experience and how I would approach it" answer outline.
- **No story bank and no master résumé**: ask once for the story bank (or the résumé, to build one by interviewing the user). Do not fill stories from memory and do not run a mock round on invented stories.

## Starting points
- **New** — the JD's competencies are mapped to your story bank (gaps stay gaps — nothing is invented), with the round's likely questions, questions to ask and a 90-day plan skeleton.
- **Existing** — add your debrief from the last round: stories you already told are marked, competencies where every story is spent and JD competencies not shown yet are listed, and the questions already asked are kept for consistent follow-ups.

## When to use
- "I have a panel interview Thursday", "grill me for the CIO round", "map my stories to this JD", "draft my 90-day plan", "what should I ask them".
- Mock-interview mode: user asks to be questioned and scored.
- NOT for: résumé rewriting (`resume-tailor`), post-interview thank-you notes (`outreach-and-followup`), offer decisions (`offer-evaluator`).

## Inputs required
| Input | Required | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Story bank (STAR+R entries with stable IDs) | yes | user file; format in `assets/story-bank.example.md` |
| Master résumé | yes (if story bank is thin) | user file; same format as `resume-tailor` |
| JD text | yes | user paste |
| Round type and interviewers (titles) | yes | user |
| Company context (public: strategy, recent news, tech stack) | no | user or web search, each fact sourced |
| Interview date and format (virtual/onsite, length, case prompt) | no | user |

Story bank named but its contents not visible: build the pack anyway with the SB ids and `[TO BE BASELINED]` story content. No story bank and no résumé: ask once; offer to build it from the master résumé by interviewing the user (one question per bullet). Never fill it from memory.

## TRUTH LOCK (hard rule)
1. Every story, number, title and outcome traces to a story-bank ID `[SB-nn]` or résumé line `[MR-Lnn]`.
2. Allowed: reframe a story for a different competency, tighten, pick which details to lead with, add a Reflection sentence the user confirms.
3. Not allowed: invent a story, add a metric, change the user's role in the story, upgrade "contributed" to "led".
4. If the JD needs a competency with no story, say so and offer: (a) interview the user for a true example, or (b) prepare an honest "here is the closest experience and how I would approach it" answer.
5. Output includes a traceability table: competency → story ID → fit (STRONG / ADEQUATE / GAP).

## Procedure
1. Read `../../../shared/quality-bar.md` and `../../../shared/writing-style.md`.
2. Map JD responsibilities to the competencies in `references/competency-map.md`. Rank by JD emphasis.
3. For each competency, select the best story from the story bank. Rewrite it in STAR+R per `references/star-r-format.md` (≤120 words spoken, ~90 seconds). Cite the ID.
4. Pull the question bank for the round type from `references/question-bank.md`. Pair each likely question with a story ID or a GAP note.
5. If the round is hiring manager, CIO/CEO or board-style: draft the 90-day plan from `assets/90-day-plan.md` using only JD facts and sourced company facts. Mark unknowns `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]`.
6. Select 6–8 questions to ask from `references/questions-to-ask.md`, tuned to interviewer title.
7. Mock mode: ask one question at a time, score the answer against the STAR+R rubric (structure, specificity, scale, result, reflection; 1–5 each), give one fix, move on. Do not score stories not in the bank.
8. Run the self-check. Reply ≤50 words outside the artifact.

## Output
Markdown file `prep-<company>-<round>.md`:
1. Competency → story traceability table
2. STAR+R stories (ranked by JD emphasis)
3. Likely questions for this round with story mapping
4. 90-day plan draft (if applicable)
5. Questions to ask (by interviewer)
6. Gaps and how to handle them honestly

## Self-check
- [ ] Every story cites `[SB-nn]` or `[MR-Lnn]`; traceability table complete
- [ ] No metric or role claim beyond the source; Reflection lines confirmed by user or marked `[confirm]`
- [ ] Each story ≤120 words; Result contains a number where the source has one
- [ ] Question bank matches the round type; interviewer titles respected
- [ ] 90-day plan uses only JD and sourced facts; unknowns carry an owner
- [ ] No author personal data pulled from memory

## References
- `scripts/prep.py` — JD competencies → story map (GAP when no story), prep pack by round type, questions to ask, 90-day plan skeleton (stdlib, offline)
- `references/competency-map.md` — exec IT competencies, behavioral indicators, JD phrases
- `references/star-r-format.md` — STAR+R structure, timing, scoring rubric
- `references/question-bank.md` — questions by round type
- `references/questions-to-ask.md` — questions to ask by interviewer
- `assets/story-bank.example.md` — EXAMPLE story bank (fictional)
- `assets/90-day-plan.md` — plan skeleton

bodyHtml:
account-plan

In a conversation: write the plan now

The reply is the plan: its first line is Posture: <Grow / Defend / Harvest / Enter> — <the facts that drove it>, never a question or a request for files. Questions for missing facts go at the end.

  • The request carries account facts (engagements, end dates, pipeline, stakeholders, events such as a sponsor leaving), or says the CRM export, stakeholder list, catalog or prior plan are attached but their contents are not in the conversation: write the full account plan in this reply from the stated facts. Never reply with only a request for files. In this order, page 1 standing alone:
    1. Posture on line 1 (Grow / Defend / Harvest / Enter) with the two or three facts that drove it (e.g. sponsor departure, nearest engagement end date).
    2. Snapshot — revenue, active engagements with end dates, contract vehicles; each cell sourced ("CRM export, <date>") or To be baselined · owner to be named. Weighted pipeline only when the CRM supplies probabilities, and say so.
    3. Top risks and 90-day plays (3–6), each with owner, date and success measure: at least one coverage play (e.g. the successor to a departing sponsor) and one renewal/defense play for the nearest engagement end.
    4. Detail: stakeholder map (role, influence, disposition — unknown stays unknown —, our owner, last contact) with departures flagged as exposure and coverage gaps computed; white-space matrix (our services × their units) using current / qualified / hypothesis / no fit / unknown, each hypothesis citing its signal and confirming action; pipeline table; risk register; change log vs the prior plan on a refresh (achieved, carried, dropped and why). Mark every value the request does not give To be baselined · owner to be named naming the source it will come from, and end with the few questions that close those gaps.
  • No account facts at all ("write an account plan for X"): ask once, in one list, for account facts (engagements, revenue, stakeholders, pipeline), our service catalog and the quarter. Do not estimate current spend, wallet share or stakeholder dispositions. Offer the Enter posture template with every cell marked To be baselined · owner to be named if the account is a target with no history.
  • Asked to invent win probabilities or a target ("assign 60% / 30%", "put the target at what we usually aim for"): say in one line that probabilities and targets are not invented, because leadership will treat them as forecast. Show the unweighted pipeline only; offer to add probabilities if the user records them in the CRM as their own sales judgment, labelled as such. Show the target as To be baselined · owner to be named until the user confirms the official target and its source, and report gap-to-target as a marker until target and weighting are confirmed. Never print the requested percentages or target figure as plan values.

Starting points

  • New — stakeholders, pipeline and service coverage become a 90-day plan: stakeholder map, white space, pipeline, risks and plays with owned TBDs.
  • Existing — add last quarter's plays and pipeline: the refresh says which plays were done, carried over (with last quarter's owner to confirm), dropped or closed by events, which plays are new, and how each opportunity moved since the last plan.

When to use

  • "Build the Q<n> account plan for <client>."
  • "Refresh the account strategy — we just lost the renewal / won the assessment."
  • "Prepare the quarterly account review for leadership."
  • NOT for: new-logo research (client-research-brief), one pursuit (competitive-positioning, proposal-writer).

Inputs required

InputRequiredSource
Account facts: current engagements (scope, value, end dates), revenue history, contract vehicles, team on the accountyesuser / CRM export / prior plan
Stakeholder list with titles, our relationship owner, last contactyes (any subset; rest TBD)user / CRM
Client business context: strategy, initiatives, org changes, budget cycle (from client-research-brief or user)nobrief / user
Pipeline: opportunities, stage, value, close date, next stepyes or "none"CRM / user
Our service catalog (for white space)yesfile / user
Prior plan (for refresh)nofile
Quarter and planning horizonyesuser

If the request carries no account facts at all, ask once. Individual facts missing from a request that has some (catalog, revenue, a stakeholder's last contact) do not stop the draft: they are marked To be baselined · owner to be named. Never estimate the client's spend with us or wallet share from memory.

Procedure

Read ../../../shared/quality-bar.md and ../../../shared/writing-style.md first.

  1. Snapshot: fill the account snapshot table (assets/account-plan-template.md §1) from inputs only: revenue by period, active engagements with end dates, contract vehicles, NPS/health signals if provided. Each cell sourced (CRM export date, prior plan version, user statement) or marked.
  2. Stakeholder map per references/account-planning-method.md §2: for each stakeholder — role, influence (decision / influencer / gatekeeper / user), disposition toward us (advocate / neutral / skeptic / unknown), our relationship owner, last meaningful contact, next contact plan. Compute coverage gaps: decision-makers with no owner or no contact in 90 days; business units with no relationship. Unknown disposition is unknown, never assumed neutral.
  3. White-space map (§3): matrix of our service lines × the client's business units or platforms. Cells: current (sourced engagement), qualified (pipeline), hypothesis (signal from brief or discovery with the signal cited), no fit (reason), unknown. Hypotheses carry the confirming action. Count the cells; the plan's growth plays come from hypothesis cells with the strongest signals.
  4. Pipeline table: each opportunity with stage (use the user's stage names), value (from CRM or marked), close date, win probability only if the user's CRM supplies it (no invented probabilities), next step with owner and date, and the blocker if any. Reconcile the sum with the snapshot.
  5. Decision point — account posture. Per §4: Grow / Defend / Harvest / Enter, from the facts (renewal exposure, relationship coverage, competitive threat, white-space signal strength). State the posture on line 1 and the two or three facts that drove it.
  6. Risks to the account (§5): renewal risk, stakeholder departure, competitive entry, delivery issues, budget cut, concentration risk; each with likelihood, impact, early signal, mitigation, owner.
  7. 90-day plays: 3–6 plays, each with objective, actions, owner, date, success measure, and which white-space cell or risk it addresses. Plays without an owner are not plays. Include at least one relationship play (coverage gap) and one delivery-quality play if any engagement is active.
  8. Targets only from the user: if a revenue target exists, show gap-to-target = target − (booked + weighted pipeline, if probabilities are supplied) and the plays that close it. If no target, To be baselined · owner to be named.
  9. One-page view first, detail behind. Refresh mode: diff against the prior plan (what changed, what was achieved, what was dropped and why).
  10. Run the self-check.

Output

  • File: account-plan-<client>-<quarter>.md per assets/account-plan-template.md
  • Page 1: posture and bottom line · snapshot · top risks · 90-day plays. Following pages: stakeholder map and gaps · white-space matrix · pipeline · risk register · change log (refresh)

Self-check

  • [ ] Posture stated on line 1 with the driving facts
  • [ ] Every revenue, pipeline, and target figure sourced or To be baselined · owner to be named
  • [ ] No invented win probabilities; weighted pipeline only if the CRM supplies probabilities
  • [ ] Stakeholder dispositions sourced; unknowns marked unknown
  • [ ] Coverage gaps computed and addressed by at least one play
  • [ ] White-space hypotheses cite a signal and a confirming action
  • [ ] Every play has owner, date, success measure
  • [ ] Risks have likelihood, impact, early signal, mitigation, owner
  • [ ] Internal document; no content copied into client-facing material without review

References

  • references/account-planning-method.md — snapshot, stakeholder mapping, white-space logic, posture decision, risk patterns, play design, review cadence
  • assets/account-plan-template.md — plan template (one page first)

How to run (automation, when commands can run)

# account-plan

## In a conversation: write the plan now
The reply **is the plan**: its first line is `Posture: <Grow / Defend / Harvest / Enter> — <the facts that drove it>`, never a question or a request for files. Questions for missing facts go at the end.
- **The request carries account facts** (engagements, end dates, pipeline, stakeholders, events such as a sponsor leaving), or says the CRM export, stakeholder list, catalog or prior plan are attached but their contents are not in the conversation: write the full account plan **in this reply** from the stated facts. Never reply with only a request for files. In this order, page 1 standing alone:
  1. **Posture on line 1** (Grow / Defend / Harvest / Enter) with the two or three facts that drove it (e.g. sponsor departure, nearest engagement end date).
  2. **Snapshot** — revenue, active engagements with end dates, contract vehicles; each cell sourced ("CRM export, <date>") or `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]`. Weighted pipeline only when the CRM supplies probabilities, and say so.
  3. **Top risks** and **90-day plays** (3–6), each with owner, date and success measure: at least one coverage play (e.g. the successor to a departing sponsor) and one renewal/defense play for the nearest engagement end.
  4. Detail: **stakeholder map** (role, influence, disposition — unknown stays `unknown` —, our owner, last contact) with departures flagged as exposure and **coverage gaps** computed; **white-space matrix** (our services × their units) using `current / qualified / hypothesis / no fit / unknown`, each hypothesis citing its signal and confirming action; **pipeline table**; **risk register**; **change log vs the prior plan** on a refresh (achieved, carried, dropped and why).
  Mark every value the request does not give `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]` naming the source it will come from, and end with the few questions that close those gaps.
- **No account facts at all** ("write an account plan for X"): ask once, in one list, for account facts (engagements, revenue, stakeholders, pipeline), our service catalog and the quarter. Do not estimate current spend, wallet share or stakeholder dispositions. Offer the **Enter** posture template with every cell marked `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]` if the account is a target with no history.
- **Asked to invent win probabilities or a target** ("assign 60% / 30%", "put the target at what we usually aim for"): say in one line that probabilities and targets are not invented, because leadership will treat them as forecast. Show the **unweighted** pipeline only; offer to add probabilities if the user records them in the CRM as their own sales judgment, labelled as such. Show the target as `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]` until the user confirms the official target and its source, and report gap-to-target as a marker until target and weighting are confirmed. Never print the requested percentages or target figure as plan values.

## Starting points
- **New** — stakeholders, pipeline and service coverage become a 90-day plan: stakeholder map, white space, pipeline, risks and plays with owned TBDs.
- **Existing** — add last quarter's plays and pipeline: the refresh says which plays were done, carried over (with last quarter's owner to confirm), dropped or closed by events, which plays are new, and how each opportunity moved since the last plan.

## When to use
- "Build the Q<n> account plan for <client>."
- "Refresh the account strategy — we just lost the renewal / won the assessment."
- "Prepare the quarterly account review for leadership."
- NOT for: new-logo research (`client-research-brief`), one pursuit (`competitive-positioning`, `proposal-writer`).

## Inputs required
| Input | Required | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Account facts: current engagements (scope, value, end dates), revenue history, contract vehicles, team on the account | yes | user / CRM export / prior plan |
| Stakeholder list with titles, our relationship owner, last contact | yes (any subset; rest TBD) | user / CRM |
| Client business context: strategy, initiatives, org changes, budget cycle (from `client-research-brief` or user) | no | brief / user |
| Pipeline: opportunities, stage, value, close date, next step | yes or "none" | CRM / user |
| Our service catalog (for white space) | yes | file / user |
| Prior plan (for refresh) | no | file |
| Quarter and planning horizon | yes | user |

If the request carries no account facts at all, ask once. Individual facts missing from a request that has some (catalog, revenue, a stakeholder's last contact) do not stop the draft: they are marked `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]`. Never estimate the client's spend with us or wallet share from memory.

## Procedure
Read `../../../shared/quality-bar.md` and `../../../shared/writing-style.md` first.

1. **Snapshot**: fill the account snapshot table (`assets/account-plan-template.md` §1) from inputs only: revenue by period, active engagements with end dates, contract vehicles, NPS/health signals if provided. Each cell sourced (CRM export date, prior plan version, user statement) or marked.
2. **Stakeholder map** per `references/account-planning-method.md` §2: for each stakeholder — role, influence (decision / influencer / gatekeeper / user), disposition toward us (advocate / neutral / skeptic / unknown), our relationship owner, last meaningful contact, next contact plan. Compute coverage gaps: decision-makers with no owner or no contact in 90 days; business units with no relationship. Unknown disposition is `unknown`, never assumed neutral.
3. **White-space map** (§3): matrix of our service lines × the client's business units or platforms. Cells: `current` (sourced engagement), `qualified` (pipeline), `hypothesis` (signal from brief or discovery with the signal cited), `no fit` (reason), `unknown`. Hypotheses carry the confirming action. Count the cells; the plan's growth plays come from `hypothesis` cells with the strongest signals.
4. **Pipeline table**: each opportunity with stage (use the user's stage names), value (from CRM or marked), close date, win probability only if the user's CRM supplies it (no invented probabilities), next step with owner and date, and the blocker if any. Reconcile the sum with the snapshot.
5. **Decision point — account posture.** Per §4: Grow / Defend / Harvest / Enter, from the facts (renewal exposure, relationship coverage, competitive threat, white-space signal strength). State the posture on line 1 and the two or three facts that drove it.
6. **Risks to the account** (§5): renewal risk, stakeholder departure, competitive entry, delivery issues, budget cut, concentration risk; each with likelihood, impact, early signal, mitigation, owner.
7. **90-day plays**: 3–6 plays, each with objective, actions, owner, date, success measure, and which white-space cell or risk it addresses. Plays without an owner are not plays. Include at least one relationship play (coverage gap) and one delivery-quality play if any engagement is active.
8. **Targets** only from the user: if a revenue target exists, show gap-to-target = target − (booked + weighted pipeline, if probabilities are supplied) and the plays that close it. If no target, `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]`.
9. **One-page view first**, detail behind. Refresh mode: diff against the prior plan (what changed, what was achieved, what was dropped and why).
10. Run the self-check.

## Output
- File: `account-plan-<client>-<quarter>.md` per `assets/account-plan-template.md`
- Page 1: posture and bottom line · snapshot · top risks · 90-day plays. Following pages: stakeholder map and gaps · white-space matrix · pipeline · risk register · change log (refresh)

## Self-check
- [ ] Posture stated on line 1 with the driving facts
- [ ] Every revenue, pipeline, and target figure sourced or `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]`
- [ ] No invented win probabilities; weighted pipeline only if the CRM supplies probabilities
- [ ] Stakeholder dispositions sourced; unknowns marked unknown
- [ ] Coverage gaps computed and addressed by at least one play
- [ ] White-space hypotheses cite a signal and a confirming action
- [ ] Every play has owner, date, success measure
- [ ] Risks have likelihood, impact, early signal, mitigation, owner
- [ ] Internal document; no content copied into client-facing material without review

## References
- `references/account-planning-method.md` — snapshot, stakeholder mapping, white-space logic, posture decision, risk patterns, play design, review cadence
- `assets/account-plan-template.md` — plan template (one page first)

## How to run (automation, when commands can run)
This skill is executable. Collect the inputs below, then run `python3 scripts/run_skill.py presales/account-plan --input <name>=<value> … --out <dir>` (see `--explain presales/account-plan`). Report the `run.json` results; do not hand-write the deliverables the scripts produce.

discovery-interview

In a conversation: produce the pack now

  • The request names the vertical and the call (who attends, how long, the trigger): write the prep pack in this reply — do not ask for files first. 3–5 hypotheses in a table (each with what would confirm or kill it and the questions that test it); 12–18 questions from the vertical's question bank ordered situation → pain → impact → urgency → decision → constraints, each tagged with persona and hypothesis ID; the five closes (decision owner, budget state, timeline driver, incumbents, success measure); a time budget that leaves about 20% to the client's questions. No question opens with a technology or vendor comparison.
  • The request gives call notes: synthesize them now. Line 1 is the qualification call. Pains scored with verbatim evidence; impact without a stated figure scores 2 or lower and shows To be baselined · owner to be named; a gaps list names who at the client likely holds each missing fact and our owner; forcing events are named without inventing dates.
  • The request lacks the vertical or the mode (prep vs synthesize): ask once for mode, vertical and opportunity context, and stop — no question list before the vertical; never invent attendees, triggers or pains.
  • Asked to fill numbers, budgets or decision owners "from what clients usually do": say in one line that it was not in the notes and must be baselined; mark it To be baselined · owner to be named.

Starting points

  • New — before the call: a timed question plan for the attendees' personas from the vertical's question bank, with the five closes all open and an empty pain matrix.
  • Existing — after the call: your notes or transcript are synthesised into the pain matrix and the five closes; anything the notes do not say stays an owned TBD.

When to use

  • "Prep me for the discovery call with <client> on <topic>."
  • "Here are my notes from the workshop — synthesize them."
  • "What should I ask a <vertical> CIO about <platform/initiative>?"
  • NOT for: company background before a pitch (client-research-brief), RFP question lists (rfp-compliance-matrix), or pitch rehearsal (orals-prep).

Inputs required

InputRequiredSource
Client name, vertical (EdTech / Retail / Manufacturing / Travel / other)yesuser
Opportunity context: initiative, platform(s), trigger eventyesuser / brief
Attendee list with titles (or "unknown")nouser
Mode: prep (before call) or synthesize (after call)yesuser
Raw notes / transcript (synthesize mode only)yes in synthesizefile
Time available for the call (minutes)no — default 45user

If a required input is missing, ask once. Do not invent the vertical, attendees, or the client's pain.

Procedure

Read ../../../shared/quality-bar.md and ../../../shared/writing-style.md first. Both apply to every output here.

Mode A — prep

  1. Classify the opportunity: vertical, buyer persona (CIO / CDO / VP Apps / COO / Head of Supply Chain / Provost / CFO), and initiative type (modernization, migration, AI, integration, cost-out, compliance). If the vertical is outside the four banks, use references/question-banks/retail.md as the structural base and say so.
  2. Write 3–5 hypotheses before writing questions (references/hypothesis-and-synthesis.md §1). Each hypothesis states a suspected pain, who owns it, and what evidence would confirm or kill it. Questions exist to test hypotheses, not to fill time.
  3. Load the vertical bank from references/question-banks/<vertical>.md. Select 12–18 questions using the time budget rule: ~3 minutes per open question, reserve 20% for their questions. Tag each selected question with the hypothesis it tests (H1…H5) and the persona it is aimed at.
  4. Order questions using the funnel in references/discovery-method.md §2: situation → pain → impact → urgency → decision process → constraints. Never open with a technology question.
  5. Add the five non-negotiable closes from references/discovery-method.md §4 (decision owner, budget state, timeline driver, incumbents, success measure). These are asked on every call.
  6. Produce the prep pack (see Output). Include an "If they say X, go to Y" branch table for the 3 most likely pivots.

Mode B — synthesize

  1. Read the notes once end-to-end before extracting anything. Note what was not said (no numbers, no owner named, no timeline).
  2. Extract every pain statement verbatim into the pain/impact/urgency matrix using the scoring rubric in references/discovery-method.md §3. A pain with no stated impact scores Impact = To be baselined · owner to be named, never a guessed number.
  3. Update the hypothesis register: confirmed / killed / untested, with the quote that decides it.
  4. Build the gaps list: every fact the proposal or estimate will need that the call did not produce (volumes, counts, contract dates, team size, budget range). Assign an owner on our side to chase each gap and the client-side person who likely holds it.
  5. Decision point — qualify: apply the qualification gate in references/discovery-method.md §5. Output one of PURSUE / PURSUE-WITH-CONDITIONS / PARK with the two or three facts that drove it. Do not soften a PARK.
  6. Draft the follow-up note (≤120 words, client-facing): what we heard, what we will bring next, the two or three things we need from them, by when.

Both modes

  1. Run the self-check. Strip anything that looks like a figure you did not hear or read.

- **The request lacks the vertical or the mode (prep vs synthesize)**: ask once for mode, vertical and opportunity context, and stop — no question list before the vertical; never invent attendees, triggers or pains.
- **Asked to fill numbers, budgets or decision owners "from what clients usually do"**: say in one line that it was not in the notes and must be baselined; mark it `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]`.

## Starting points
- **New** — before the call: a timed question plan for the attendees' personas from the vertical's question bank, with the five closes all open and an empty pain matrix.
- **Existing** — after the call: your notes or transcript are synthesised into the pain matrix and the five closes; anything the notes do not say stays an owned TBD.

## When to use
- "Prep me for the discovery call with <client> on <topic>."
- "Here are my notes from the workshop — synthesize them."
- "What should I ask a <vertical> CIO about <platform/initiative>?"
- NOT for: company background before a pitch (`client-research-brief`), RFP question lists (`rfp-compliance-matrix`), or pitch rehearsal (`orals-prep`).

## Inputs required
| Input | Required | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Client name, vertical (EdTech / Retail / Manufacturing / Travel / other) | yes | user |
| Opportunity context: initiative, platform(s), trigger event | yes | user / brief |
| Attendee list with titles (or "unknown") | no | user |
| Mode: `prep` (before call) or `synthesize` (after call) | yes | user |
| Raw notes / transcript (synthesize mode only) | yes in synthesize | file |
| Time available for the call (minutes) | no — default 45 | user |

If a required input is missing, ask once. Do not invent the vertical, attendees, or the client's pain.

## Procedure
Read `../../../shared/quality-bar.md` and `../../../shared/writing-style.md` first. Both apply to every output here.

### Mode A — prep
1. Classify the opportunity: vertical, buyer persona (CIO / CDO / VP Apps / COO / Head of Supply Chain / Provost / CFO), and initiative type (modernization, migration, AI, integration, cost-out, compliance). If the vertical is outside the four banks, use `references/question-banks/retail.md` as the structural base and say so.
2. Write 3–5 **hypotheses** before writing questions (`references/hypothesis-and-synthesis.md` §1). Each hypothesis states a suspected pain, who owns it, and what evidence would confirm or kill it. Questions exist to test hypotheses, not to fill time.
3. Load the vertical bank from `references/question-banks/<vertical>.md`. Select 12–18 questions using the time budget rule: ~3 minutes per open question, reserve 20% for their questions. Tag each selected question with the hypothesis it tests (H1…H5) and the persona it is aimed at.
4. Order questions using the funnel in `references/discovery-method.md` §2: situation → pain → impact → urgency → decision process → constraints. Never open with a technology question.
5. Add the five **non-negotiable closes** from `references/discovery-method.md` §4 (decision owner, budget state, timeline driver, incumbents, success measure). These are asked on every call.
6. Produce the prep pack (see Output). Include an "If they say X, go to Y" branch table for the 3 most likely pivots.

### Mode B — synthesize
1. Read the notes once end-to-end before extracting anything. Note what was *not* said (no numbers, no owner named, no timeline).
2. Extract every pain statement verbatim into the pain/impact/urgency matrix using the scoring rubric in `references/discovery-method.md` §3. A pain with no stated impact scores Impact = `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]`, never a guessed number.
3. Update the hypothesis register: confirmed / killed / untested, with the quote that decides it.
4. Build the **gaps list**: every fact the proposal or estimate will need that the call did not produce (volumes, counts, contract dates, team size, budget range). Assign an owner on our side to chase each gap and the client-side person who likely holds it.
5. Decision point — qualify: apply the qualification gate in `references/discovery-method.md` §5. Output one of `PURSUE / PURSUE-WITH-CONDITIONS / PARK` with the two or three facts that drove it. Do not soften a PARK.
6. Draft the follow-up note (≤120 words, client-facing): what we heard, what we will bring next, the two or three things we need from them, by when.

### Both modes
7. Run the self-check. Strip anything that looks like a figure you did not hear or read.

| prep | `discovery-prep-<client>-<yyyy-mm-dd>.md` | Sections: Hypotheses (table) · Question plan (table: #, question, persona, hypothesis, time) · Branches · Closes · Pre-reads to send |
| synthesize | `discovery-synthesis-<client>-<yyyy-mm-dd>.md` | Sections: Bottom line (qualification call) · Pain/Impact/Urgency matrix · Hypothesis register · Gaps list (table with owners) · Follow-up note · Parked items |

Template: `assets/discovery-pack-template.md`.

- [ ] Gaps list has an owner for every row
- [ ] Follow-up note contains no internal commentary and no other-client references
- [ ] Tables for questions, matrix, hypotheses, gaps

bodyHtml:
integration-migration-assessor

In a conversation: assess now

  • The request carries the inventory (or its contents): produce the readout in this reply. Report the share of unknown factors and whether the assessment is provisional; list retirement candidates with owners to confirm before effort is discussed; a band distribution table with outliers explained; a wave plan (wave 0 foundation, a representative wave 1, balanced middle waves, dependencies enforced, cutovers outside the client's freeze windows, entry/exit criteria); TCO lines that cite the client's contract for licence cost, with migration cost To be baselined · owner to be named until the effort estimate exists; handoffs to effort-estimator and solution-architecture-doc.
  • No inventory, only a count: ask once for the inventory and offer the collection template (assets/inventory-columns.md) and the minimum viable column set for a provisional assessment. Never synthesize an inventory or a band distribution from a count.
  • Asked to use list prices, treat blanks as simple, or give a ballpark savings figure: say in one line why not (blank factors scored simple are the main cause of overrun; vendor list prices from memory are not the client's contract). Score blanks as unknown (mid-band, flagged); show licence cost and savings as To be baselined · owner to be named naming the client contract as the source; state the TCO direction qualitatively at most; give next steps with owners.

Starting points

  • Existing — the inventory of your current estate is scored, banded and planned into waves, the TCO is built only from the rate inputs you supply, and the readout is written by the model step or, with draft_only, assembled from the two summaries with every figure copied verbatim.
  • Only for existing: an assessment always scores an integration estate that already runs; there is nothing to assess from scratch.

When to use

  • "Assess <client>'s MuleSoft/Boomi/ESB/Informatica estate for migration to <target>."
  • "Score this interface inventory and give me waves."
  • "Build the TCO comparison for staying vs migrating."
  • NOT for: drawing the target architecture (solution-architecture-doc), P50/P80 effort (effort-estimator), full business case with non-platform benefits (value-case-builder).

Inputs required

InputRequiredSource
Interface inventory CSV (one row per interface/API/flow; columns per assets/inventory-columns.md)yesclient export / discovery / platform admin console export
Source and target platforms (or "target to be selected")yesuser
Current platform cost facts: licence, infrastructure, support/run team, contract endno — TCO is To be baselined · owner to be named without themclient / user
Constraints: freeze windows, contract end dates, dependent programs (ERP upgrade), compliancenodiscovery
Prior migration actuals (unit effort per band) if anynouser

If the inventory is missing, ask once; offer assets/inventory-columns.md as the collection template. Never synthesize an inventory.

Procedure

Read ../../../shared/quality-bar.md and ../../../shared/writing-style.md first.

  1. Validate the inventory: run python3 -I scripts/score_inventory.py inventory.csv --validate. It reports missing columns, blank factor cells, and duplicates. Blank factor cells score as "unknown" (mid-band with a flag), never as "simple". Report the unknown share; above 25% the assessment is provisional and says so.
  2. Score complexity with python3 -I scripts/score_inventory.py inventory.csv --out scored.csv --waves 4. Factors and weights per references/complexity-scoring.md (pattern, transformation logic, protocol/connector availability on target, endpoints, data volume, error handling and orchestration, security, test coverage, documentation, business criticality). Review the band distribution (Simple / Medium / Complex / Very complex) against what discovery said; investigate outliers.
  3. Decision point — migration approach per band. Apply references/migration-factory-method.md §2: Simple → automated/tool-assisted conversion with templated tests; Medium → factory with pattern templates; Complex → design-led with refactor; Very complex → candidates for redesign, retirement, or re-platform outside the factory. Retirement candidates (unused, duplicate, superseded) are identified first; they are the cheapest migration.
  4. Assign waves (script output, then adjust): wave 0 foundation; wave 1 representative simples; middle waves balance complexity and resolve dependencies; final wave long-tail and decommission. Respect freeze windows and dependent programs from constraints. Each wave gets entry/exit criteria and a rollback approach from §4 of the method.
  5. Build the TCO/ROI layout on assets/tco-model-spec.md (CSV layout spec) and assets/tco-model.md (markdown table layout): current run-rate (licence, infra, people, support, incidents) vs target run-rate, one-time migration cost (from effort-estimator, or To be baselined · owner to be named), timing of savings (only after decommission), 3–5-year view, payback, sensitivity on the two biggest drivers. Every figure sourced to a client document or marked. Licence savings are not realized until the source platform is decommissioned; model that date explicitly.
  6. Risk register for the migration: dual-run cost, connector gaps on target, skills, endpoint changes during migration, data drift, cutover windows, vendor cooperation; each with likelihood, impact, mitigation, owner.
  7. Write the assessment readout on assets/assessment-readout-template.md: bottom line (inventory size, band mix, approach, waves, TCO direction with confidence, decision asked), evidence, scoring results, wave plan, TCO layout, risks, next steps. Feed interface counts and bands to effort-estimator and the wave plan to solution-architecture-doc.
  8. Run the self-check.

  • [ ] Band distribution reviewed against discovery; outliers explained
  • [ ] Retirement candidates identified before scoring effort
  • [ ] Waves have entry/exit criteria, rollback, and respect constraints
  • [ ] TCO: every figure sourced or To be baselined · owner to be named; savings timed after decommission
  • [ ] Sensitivity on the two largest drivers shown

bodyMd:
# integration-migration-assessor

## In a conversation: assess now
- **The request carries the inventory** (or its contents): produce the readout **in this reply**. Report the share of unknown factors and whether the assessment is provisional; list retirement candidates with owners to confirm before effort is discussed; a band distribution table with outliers explained; a wave plan (wave 0 foundation, a representative wave 1, balanced middle waves, dependencies enforced, cutovers outside the client's freeze windows, entry/exit criteria); TCO lines that cite the client's contract for licence cost, with migration cost `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]` until the effort estimate exists; handoffs to effort-estimator and solution-architecture-doc.
- **No inventory, only a count**: ask once for the inventory and offer the collection template (`assets/inventory-columns.md`) and the minimum viable column set for a provisional assessment. Never synthesize an inventory or a band distribution from a count.
- **Asked to use list prices, treat blanks as simple, or give a ballpark savings figure**: say in one line why not (blank factors scored simple are the main cause of overrun; vendor list prices from memory are not the client's contract). Score blanks as unknown (mid-band, flagged); show licence cost and savings as `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]` naming the client contract as the source; state the TCO direction qualitatively at most; give next steps with owners.

## Starting points
- **Existing** — the inventory of your current estate is scored, banded and planned into waves, the TCO is built only from the rate inputs you supply, and the readout is written by the model step or, with `draft_only`, assembled from the two summaries with every figure copied verbatim.
- Only for existing: an assessment always scores an integration estate that already runs; there is nothing to assess from scratch.

## When to use
- "Assess <client>'s MuleSoft/Boomi/ESB/Informatica estate for migration to <target>."
- "Score this interface inventory and give me waves."
- "Build the TCO comparison for staying vs migrating."
- NOT for: drawing the target architecture (`solution-architecture-doc`), P50/P80 effort (`effort-estimator`), full business case with non-platform benefits (`value-case-builder`).

## Inputs required
| Input | Required | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Interface inventory CSV (one row per interface/API/flow; columns per `assets/inventory-columns.md`) | yes | client export / discovery / platform admin console export |
| Source and target platforms (or "target to be selected") | yes | user |
| Current platform cost facts: licence, infrastructure, support/run team, contract end | no — TCO is `[TO BE BASELINED]` without them | client / user |
| Constraints: freeze windows, contract end dates, dependent programs (ERP upgrade), compliance | no | discovery |
| Prior migration actuals (unit effort per band) if any | no | user |

If the inventory is missing, ask once; offer `assets/inventory-columns.md` as the collection template. Never synthesize an inventory.

## Procedure
Read `../../../shared/quality-bar.md` and `../../../shared/writing-style.md` first.

1. **Validate the inventory**: run `python3 -I scripts/score_inventory.py inventory.csv --validate`. It reports missing columns, blank factor cells, and duplicates. Blank factor cells score as "unknown" (mid-band with a flag), never as "simple". Report the unknown share; above 25% the assessment is provisional and says so.
2. **Score complexity** with `python3 -I scripts/score_inventory.py inventory.csv --out scored.csv --waves 4`. Factors and weights per `references/complexity-scoring.md` (pattern, transformation logic, protocol/connector availability on target, endpoints, data volume, error handling and orchestration, security, test coverage, documentation, business criticality). Review the band distribution (Simple / Medium / Complex / Very complex) against what discovery said; investigate outliers.
3. **Decision point — migration approach per band.** Apply `references/migration-factory-method.md` §2: Simple → automated/tool-assisted conversion with templated tests; Medium → factory with pattern templates; Complex → design-led with refactor; Very complex → candidates for redesign, retirement, or re-platform outside the factory. Retirement candidates (unused, duplicate, superseded) are identified first; they are the cheapest migration.
4. **Assign waves** (script output, then adjust): wave 0 foundation; wave 1 representative simples; middle waves balance complexity and resolve dependencies; final wave long-tail and decommission. Respect freeze windows and dependent programs from constraints. Each wave gets entry/exit criteria and a rollback approach from §4 of the method.
5. **Build the TCO/ROI layout** on `assets/tco-model-spec.md` (CSV layout spec) and `assets/tco-model.md` (markdown table layout): current run-rate (licence, infra, people, support, incidents) vs target run-rate, one-time migration cost (from `effort-estimator`, or `[TO BE BASELINED]`), timing of savings (only after decommission), 3–5-year view, payback, sensitivity on the two biggest drivers. Every figure sourced to a client document or marked. Licence savings are not realized until the source platform is decommissioned; model that date explicitly.
6. **Risk register for the migration**: dual-run cost, connector gaps on target, skills, endpoint changes during migration, data drift, cutover windows, vendor cooperation; each with likelihood, impact, mitigation, owner.
7. **Write the assessment readout** on `assets/assessment-readout-template.md`: bottom line (inventory size, band mix, approach, waves, TCO direction with confidence, decision asked), evidence, scoring results, wave plan, TCO layout, risks, next steps. Feed interface counts and bands to `effort-estimator` and the wave plan to `solution-architecture-doc`.
8. Run the self-check.

## Output
| Artifact | File |
|---|---|
| Scored inventory | `inventory-scored-<client>.csv` (script) |
| Wave plan | within readout; CSV wave column in scored inventory |
| TCO model layout | `tco-<client>.csv` per `assets/tco-model-spec.md` + markdown table in readout |
| Assessment readout | `migration-assessment-<client>-<yyyy-mm-dd>.md` |

## Self-check
- [ ] Inventory validated; unknown-factor share reported; provisional flag if >25%
- [ ] Band distribution reviewed against discovery; outliers explained
- [ ] Retirement candidates identified before scoring effort
- [ ] Waves have entry/exit criteria, rollback, and respect constraints
- [ ] TCO: every figure sourced or `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]`; savings timed after decommission
- [ ] Sensitivity on the two largest drivers shown
- [ ] No vendor pricing quoted from memory; licence figures from client contracts or marked
- [ ] No other-client specifics; no author history

## References
- `references/complexity-scoring.md` — factors, weights, bands, unknown handling, calibration
- `references/migration-factory-method.md` — approach per band, factory operating model, wave rules, cutover and rollback, decommission
- `assets/inventory-columns.md` — inventory CSV column spec (collection template)
- `assets/tco-model-spec.md` — TCO/ROI CSV layout spec
- `assets/tco-model.md` — TCO markdown table layout
- `assets/assessment-readout-template.md` — readout template
- `scripts/score_inventory.py` — validate, score, band, assign waves

## How to run (automation, when commands can run)
This skill is executable. Collect the inputs below, then run `python3 scripts/run_skill.py presales/integration-migration-assessor --input <name>=<value> … --out <dir>` (see `--explain presales/integration-migration-assessor`). Report the `run.json` results; do not hand-write the deliverables the scripts produce.
