In a conversation: prepare the team now

  • The request carries the format and the team (duration, presentation vs Q&A split, evaluators, presenters) — including when the proposal, deck, compliance matrix or battle card are said to be attached but their contents are not in the conversation: write the orals pack in this reply from the stated facts. Never reply with only a request for files. In this order:
    1. Evaluation map — each stated criterion (or, if criteria are unknown, the proposal's structure) → slide(s) → speaker.
    2. Timed script fitting the presentation slot — segments with start/end minute, speaker, slide, point, proof (number with source or To be baselined · owner to be named), transition; opening ≤90 s and close ≤60 s written verbatim; scripted handoffs; airtime check (every speaker ≥1 segment, none >40%).
    3. Likely-questions bank (table) — one question per compliance partial (e.g. each security partial), per [TBD], per estimate assumption, plus the battle card's objections and the standard evaluator set; each answer ≤75 words with the answerer, evidence pointer and "do not say" line.
    4. The hard three (typically price, the known gaps, incumbent continuity) with honest answers that state the gap and the mitigation.
    5. Red-team protocol and rehearsal plan — three dry runs (content and timing, Q&A only, full with red team), each with a date or To be baselined · owner to be named and the rubric (assets/orals-rubric.md).
    6. Number sheet — every figure the team may say, with its proposal page · Logistics and risks · Open items with owners. No competitor is named in any answer.
  • No format or team ("help us get ready for the pitch"): ask once, in one list, for the format (duration, presentation/Q&A split, attendees, evaluation criteria), the presenting team and the proposal and deck. Do not produce a timed script without the duration and the team. If the proposal is available, offer to generate the question bank from it as a parallel first step.
  • Asked to script new numbers, uncleared client claims or a competitor attack ("say we are 30% faster", "our last clients saw 40% savings", "name the incumbent's failed upgrade"): say in one line that new numbers and competitor naming in orals create credibility and compliance risk. Rewrite the answer around the proposal's basis of estimate, P80 contingency and a like-for-like comparison; use cleared references only, in their cleared form, or omit them; replace the competitor mention with a ghost line in consequence language (the risk the client should weigh, and how we remove it). Never print the requested percentages in the answer, unless the user shows they are in the proposal with a source.

Starting points

  • New — from the submitted proposal: a timed script skeleton with speakers, an airtime check, a number sheet every presenter keeps in front of them, and likely evaluator questions.
  • Existing — add your team's current talk track: every figure it says that the proposal does not contain is flagged, each speaker's spoken length is compared with their slot, and people with lines but no slot are listed (talk-track-check.md).

When to use

  • "We are shortlisted; orals are Thursday — prepare us."
  • "Run a red-team on our pitch."
  • "Build the Q&A bank for the steering-committee readout."
  • NOT for: fixing the slides (exec-deck-redline), building the battle card (competitive-positioning), writing the proposal (proposal-writer).

Inputs required

InputRequiredSource
The proposal or readout document (final)yesfile
The deck to be presented (final or near-final)yesfile
Format rules: duration, presentation vs Q&A split, attendees (names/roles if known), evaluation criteria, allowed presentersyesRFP / client / user
Our presenting team (names, roles on the engagement)yesuser
Battle card (if a competitive pursuit)nocompetitive-positioning output
Compliance matrix and clarification answers (RFP pursuits)norfp-compliance-matrix output

If format rules or the team are missing, ask once; a script cannot be timed or assigned without them. Missing files (proposal, deck, compliance matrix, battle card) or unknown evaluation criteria do not stop the pack when the format and team are stated: the gaps are marked To be baselined · owner to be named.

Procedure

Read ../../../shared/quality-bar.md and ../../../shared/writing-style.md first.

  1. Decode the evaluation: from the format rules, list what is scored and by whom. If the evaluation criteria are unknown, mark To be baselined · owner to be named and assume the proposal's structure is the scoring frame. Map each scored criterion to the slide(s) and speaker that will prove it (references/orals-method.md §1).
  2. Build the timed script on assets/script-template.md: segments with start/end minute, speaker, slide, the point (one sentence), the proof (number with source), the transition line. Reserve ≥35% of total time for Q&A unless the format fixes it. Opening ≤90 seconds: their situation, the outcome, what they will hear. Close ≤60 seconds: the ask and the next step.
  3. Assign speakers by credibility, not seniority: the person who will do the work speaks to the approach; the engagement lead to governance and commitments; the executive sponsor opens and closes. Every speaker has ≥1 segment and ≤40% of airtime. Note handoffs explicitly.
  4. Generate the likely-questions bank (references/question-bank-and-red-team.md §1): from the proposal's weak spots (every P/N in the compliance matrix, every [TBD], every assumption), from the evaluation criteria, from the battle card's objections, and from the standard evaluator set. For each: question, who answers, the answer (≤75 words, number + source, no new claims), the evidence slide/page, and the "do not say" line.
  5. Decision point — the hard three. Identify the three questions the team most fears (price, a gap, a credibility challenge). Write the answers with the engagement lead; rehearse these first and most. If an honest answer exposes a real gap, the answer states the gap and the mitigation; it does not spin.
  6. Red-team (§2): assign one person to play the skeptical evaluator and one the incumbent-friendly evaluator; run the objections in the bank plus three unscripted; score with assets/orals-rubric.md; log every answer that exceeded 90 seconds, invented a number, or contradicted the proposal.
  7. Rehearsal plan: dry run 1 (content and timing), dry run 2 (Q&A only), dry run 3 (full, with red team), each with a date and the rubric scores. Fix list after each.
  8. Logistics and risk: room/virtual setup, backups (PDF of deck, offline), who speaks if someone drops, name pronunciation for attendees, prohibited content (other clients' names without clearance, pricing details if sealed).
  9. Run the self-check.

Output

  • File: orals-prep-<client>-<yyyy-mm-dd>.md
  • Sections: Evaluation map (criterion → slide → speaker) · Timed script · Speaker assignments and handoffs · Likely questions bank (table) · The hard three · Red-team log · Rehearsal plan · Logistics and risks · Open items
  • Companion: assets/orals-rubric.md scored per dry run

  • [ ] Every scored criterion mapped to a slide and a speaker
  • [ ] Script timed to the format; Q&A ≥35% unless fixed by the client
  • [ ] Every number in the script and answers traces to the proposal/sources; none new
  • [ ] Hard three identified with honest answers that state gaps and mitigations
  • [ ] Each answer ≤75 words with a named answerer and evidence pointer
  • [ ] No competitor named in any answer; no uncleared client references
  • [ ] Rehearsal plan has dates and rubric scores recorded
  • [ ] Logistics and backups listed

  • assets/script-template.md — timed script layout

5. **Decision point — the hard three.** Identify the three questions the team most fears (price, a gap, a credibility challenge). Write the answers with the engagement lead; rehearse these first and most. If an honest answer exposes a real gap, the answer states the gap and the mitigation; it does not spin.
6. **Red-team** (§2): assign one person to play the skeptical evaluator and one the incumbent-friendly evaluator; run the objections in the bank plus three unscripted; score with `assets/orals-rubric.md`; log every answer that exceeded 90 seconds, invented a number, or contradicted the proposal.
7. **Rehearsal plan**: dry run 1 (content and timing), dry run 2 (Q&A only), dry run 3 (full, with red team), each with a date and the rubric scores. Fix list after each.
8. **Logistics and risk**: room/virtual setup, backups (PDF of deck, offline), who speaks if someone drops, name pronunciation for attendees, prohibited content (other clients' names without clearance, pricing details if sealed).
9. Run the self-check.

## Output
- File: `orals-prep-<client>-<yyyy-mm-dd>.md`
- Sections: Evaluation map (criterion → slide → speaker) · Timed script · Speaker assignments and handoffs · Likely questions bank (table) · The hard three · Red-team log · Rehearsal plan · Logistics and risks · Open items
- Companion: `assets/orals-rubric.md` scored per dry run

## Self-check
- [ ] Every scored criterion mapped to a slide and a speaker
- [ ] Script timed to the format; Q&A ≥35% unless fixed by the client
- [ ] Every number in the script and answers traces to the proposal/sources; none new
- [ ] Hard three identified with honest answers that state gaps and mitigations
- [ ] Each answer ≤75 words with a named answerer and evidence pointer
- [ ] No competitor named in any answer; no uncleared client references
- [ ] Rehearsal plan has dates and rubric scores recorded

bodyHtml:
rfp-compliance-matrix

In a conversation: build the matrix now

  • The request carries the RFP and the capability source — including when the RFP PDF and catalog are said to be attached but their contents are not in the conversation: produce the bid review in this reply from the stated facts. Never reply with only a request for files. In this order:
    1. Bid call on line 1 — BID / BID-WITH-CONDITIONS / NO-BID (provisional where the gate tests are open) with its three drivers.
    2. Requirement inventory — apply scripts/extract_requirements.py's rules by hand: numbered clauses and shall/must/required sentences, wrapped lines merged, boilerplate moved to Administrative, items from tables and appendices added, client IDs kept with our REQ-nnn alongside.
    3. Classification — every requirement by category (FUN TEC SEC COM DEL ADM) and M/D/O per references/requirement-taxonomy.md; hidden mandatories flagged.
    4. Compliance matrix in the column order of assets/compliance-matrix-columns.md (req_id, client_id, section, page, text, category, mdo, weight, flags, compliance, evidence, gap_condition, mitigation, owner, response_section, status, clarification_id). No C without an evidence citation from the capability catalog; no evidence → P or Q.
    5. Gaps and risks — every P/N with mitigation, risk if unmitigated and owner.
    6. Clarification questions — one per item, neutral, citing the clause ID, revealing no gap.
    7. Deadlines (Q&A, submission) with the RFP page, or page To be baselined · owner to be named · Response plan (section, owner, due). Rows the request cannot fill show To be baselined · owner to be named; end with the few questions that close them.
  • No RFP at all: ask once for the document. No capability source: ask once for the capability statement or service catalog, and still produce the requirement inventory and taxonomy classification now; if the user declines, mark every compliance cell Q with owner: ___ rather than guessing C.
  • Asked to mark items Comply without evidence ("we are basically SOC 2 ready, ISO 27001 next quarter", "no partials in front of the client"): say in one line that C requires current, in-scope certification evidence. Score those requirements P with mitigation roadmap and the expected date To be baselined · owner to be named (never the hoped-for date); flag the mandatory items in gaps-and-risks with an owner; offer client-facing wording that presents the roadmap commitment without misrepresenting current status.

Starting points

  • New — the RFP is split into requirements, each scored against your capability inventory (C/P/Q with evidence and owner), with mandatory gaps, clarification questions and a provisional bid gate.
  • Existing — add previous (your reviewed matrix from the last round): unchanged clauses keep their reviewed answer, changed clauses are re-scored and flagged for re-review, new clauses are flagged, and withdrawn ones are listed to drop from the response.

When to use

  • "We received an RFP from <client>; break it down."
  • "Build the compliance matrix for this RFI."
  • "Should we bid on this?"
  • "What clarification questions do we send before the deadline?"
  • NOT for: proposal prose (proposal-writer), pricing (effort-estimator), SOW (sow-drafter).

Inputs required

InputRequiredSource
RFP document(s): .pdf / .docx / .md / .txt, including appendicesyesfile
Submission deadline, Q&A deadline, format rules (page limits, forms)yes (extract or ask)document / user
Our capability statement or service catalog (what we can claim)yesfile / user
Named owners for response sections (or "assign later")nouser
Known incumbent / competitive contextnouser

If the RFP file is missing, ask once. If the capability source is missing, ask once and still produce the inventory and classification; if it stays missing, mark every compliance cell Q (Clarify) with owner: ___ rather than guessing what we comply with. Missing deadlines or owners do not stop the matrix: they are marked To be baselined · owner to be named.

Procedure

Read ../../../shared/quality-bar.md and ../../../shared/writing-style.md first.

  1. Extract the requirement inventory. Run python3 -I scripts/extract_requirements.py <rfp-file> --out requirements.csv. The script captures numbered clauses (1.2.3, (a), R-014), and sentences with shall / must / required / will provide, with section context and page. Review the CSV: merge split sentences, drop boilerplate (definitions, instructions to bidders go in a separate "Administrative" category), and add any requirements the script missed from tables and appendices. Never renumber the client's IDs; add our REQ-nnn alongside.
  2. Classify every requirement using references/requirement-taxonomy.md: Category (Functional / Technical / Security-Compliance / Commercial / Delivery-PM / Administrative), Mandatory vs Desirable (per RFP wording), and Evaluation weight if the RFP states scoring. Flag "hidden mandatories" — requirements phrased softly but located in pass/fail sections.
  3. Score compliance per references/compliance-scoring.md: C Comply · P Partial · N Non-comply · Q Clarify. The rule: C requires evidence we can cite (project, certification, product feature, named capability in our catalog). No evidence → P or Q, never C. Each row gets an owner and the proposal section that will carry the response.
  4. Decision point — bid/no-bid. Apply the gate in references/compliance-scoring.md §3: any N on a mandatory is a hard stop unless a clarification can convert it; compute C share on mandatories; check deadline feasibility against the response effort (count of sections × owners available). Output BID / BID-WITH-CONDITIONS / NO-BID with the three facts that drove it. Do not soften a NO-BID.
  5. Draft clarification questions for every Q, ambiguous mandatory, and scoring-rule gap. Use the question format in references/compliance-scoring.md §4: neutral wording, no capability reveal, one question per item, reference the clause ID. Group by theme; cap at the count the RFP allows.
  6. Build the gaps-and-risks list: every P and N with the mitigation (partner, roadmap commitment, alternative approach, exception request) and the risk if unmitigated.
  7. Assemble the matrix on assets/compliance-matrix-columns.md (column spec) — export as CSV/XLSX for the response team, plus a Markdown summary for the bid review. Totals by category and by compliance level must reconcile with the inventory count.
  8. Run the self-check.

Self-check

  • [ ] Inventory count = matrix row count; totals by category reconcile
  • [ ] No C without a cited evidence item
  • [ ] Every mandatory N or P appears in gaps-and-risks with a mitigation and owner
  • [ ] Clarification questions reference clause IDs and reveal no capability gaps
  • [ ] Bid/no-bid call on line 1 of the summary with its three drivers
  • [ ] Deadlines (Q&A, submission) stated with source page
  • [ ] No other-client names or internal rate information in any artifact that could ship

bodyMd:
# rfp-compliance-matrix

## In a conversation: build the matrix now
- **The request carries the RFP and the capability source** — including when the RFP PDF and catalog are said to be attached but their contents are not in the conversation: produce the bid review **in this reply** from the stated facts. Never reply with only a request for files. In this order:
  1. **Bid call on line 1** — `BID / BID-WITH-CONDITIONS / NO-BID` (provisional where the gate tests are open) with its three drivers.
  2. **Requirement inventory** — apply `scripts/extract_requirements.py`'s rules by hand: numbered clauses and shall/must/required sentences, wrapped lines merged, boilerplate moved to Administrative, items from tables and appendices added, client IDs kept with our `REQ-nnn` alongside.
  3. **Classification** — every requirement by category (`FUN TEC SEC COM DEL ADM`) and `M/D/O` per `references/requirement-taxonomy.md`; hidden mandatories flagged.
  4. **Compliance matrix** in the column order of `assets/compliance-matrix-columns.md` (`req_id, client_id, section, page, text, category, mdo, weight, flags, compliance, evidence, gap_condition, mitigation, owner, response_section, status, clarification_id`). No `C` without an evidence citation from the capability catalog; no evidence → `P` or `Q`.
  5. **Gaps and risks** — every `P`/`N` with mitigation, risk if unmitigated and owner.
  6. **Clarification questions** — one per item, neutral, citing the clause ID, revealing no gap.
  7. **Deadlines** (Q&A, submission) with the RFP page, or page `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]` · **Response plan** (section, owner, due).
  Rows the request cannot fill show `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]`; end with the few questions that close them.
- **No RFP at all**: ask once for the document. **No capability source**: ask once for the capability statement or service catalog, and still produce the requirement inventory and taxonomy classification now; if the user declines, mark every compliance cell `Q` with `owner: ___` rather than guessing `C`.
- **Asked to mark items Comply without evidence** ("we are basically SOC 2 ready, ISO 27001 next quarter", "no partials in front of the client"): say in one line that `C` requires current, in-scope certification evidence. Score those requirements `P` with mitigation `roadmap` and the expected date `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]` (never the hoped-for date); flag the mandatory items in gaps-and-risks with an owner; offer client-facing wording that presents the roadmap commitment without misrepresenting current status.

## Starting points
- **New** — the RFP is split into requirements, each scored against your capability inventory (C/P/Q with evidence and owner), with mandatory gaps, clarification questions and a provisional bid gate.
- **Existing** — add `previous` (your reviewed matrix from the last round): unchanged clauses keep their reviewed answer, changed clauses are re-scored and flagged for re-review, new clauses are flagged, and withdrawn ones are listed to drop from the response.

## When to use
- "We received an RFP from <client>; break it down."
- "Build the compliance matrix for this RFI."
- "Should we bid on this?"
- "What clarification questions do we send before the deadline?"
- NOT for: proposal prose (`proposal-writer`), pricing (`effort-estimator`), SOW (`sow-drafter`).

## Inputs required
| Input | Required | Source |
|---|---|---|
| RFP document(s): .pdf / .docx / .md / .txt, including appendices | yes | file |
| Submission deadline, Q&A deadline, format rules (page limits, forms) | yes (extract or ask) | document / user |
| Our capability statement or service catalog (what we can claim) | yes | file / user |
| Named owners for response sections (or "assign later") | no | user |
| Known incumbent / competitive context | no | user |

If the RFP file is missing, ask once. If the capability source is missing, ask once and still produce the inventory and classification; if it stays missing, mark every compliance cell `Q` (Clarify) with `owner: ___` rather than guessing what we comply with. Missing deadlines or owners do not stop the matrix: they are marked `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]`.

## Procedure
Read `../../../shared/quality-bar.md` and `../../../shared/writing-style.md` first.

1. **Extract the requirement inventory.** Run `python3 -I scripts/extract_requirements.py <rfp-file> --out requirements.csv`. The script captures numbered clauses (1.2.3, (a), R-014), and sentences with shall / must / required / will provide, with section context and page. Review the CSV: merge split sentences, drop boilerplate (definitions, instructions to bidders go in a separate "Administrative" category), and add any requirements the script missed from tables and appendices. Never renumber the client's IDs; add our `REQ-nnn` alongside.
2. **Classify every requirement** using `references/requirement-taxonomy.md`: Category (Functional / Technical / Security-Compliance / Commercial / Delivery-PM / Administrative), Mandatory vs Desirable (per RFP wording), and Evaluation weight if the RFP states scoring. Flag "hidden mandatories" — requirements phrased softly but located in pass/fail sections.
3. **Score compliance** per `references/compliance-scoring.md`: `C` Comply · `P` Partial · `N` Non-comply · `Q` Clarify. The rule: `C` requires evidence we can cite (project, certification, product feature, named capability in our catalog). No evidence → `P` or `Q`, never `C`. Each row gets an owner and the proposal section that will carry the response.
4. **Decision point — bid/no-bid.** Apply the gate in `references/compliance-scoring.md` §3: any `N` on a mandatory is a hard stop unless a clarification can convert it; compute `C` share on mandatories; check deadline feasibility against the response effort (count of sections × owners available). Output `BID / BID-WITH-CONDITIONS / NO-BID` with the three facts that drove it. Do not soften a NO-BID.
5. **Draft clarification questions** for every `Q`, ambiguous mandatory, and scoring-rule gap. Use the question format in `references/compliance-scoring.md` §4: neutral wording, no capability reveal, one question per item, reference the clause ID. Group by theme; cap at the count the RFP allows.
6. **Build the gaps-and-risks list**: every `P` and `N` with the mitigation (partner, roadmap commitment, alternative approach, exception request) and the risk if unmitigated.
7. **Assemble the matrix** on `assets/compliance-matrix-columns.md` (column spec) — export as CSV/XLSX for the response team, plus a Markdown summary for the bid review. Totals by category and by compliance level must reconcile with the inventory count.
8. Run the self-check.

## Output
| Artifact | File | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Requirement inventory | `rfp-<client>-requirements.csv` | Script output, reviewed |
| Compliance matrix | `rfp-<client>-compliance-matrix.csv` (or `.xlsx` if openpyxl available) | Columns per `assets/compliance-matrix-columns.md` |
| Bid review summary | `rfp-<client>-bid-review.md` | Bottom line (BID call) · Totals table · Mandatory non-compliances · Gaps and risks · Clarification questions · Response plan (section, owner, due) · Administrative checklist |

## Self-check
- [ ] Inventory count = matrix row count; totals by category reconcile
- [ ] No `C` without a cited evidence item
- [ ] Every mandatory `N` or `P` appears in gaps-and-risks with a mitigation and owner
- [ ] Clarification questions reference clause IDs and reveal no capability gaps
- [ ] Bid/no-bid call on line 1 of the summary with its three drivers
- [ ] Deadlines (Q&A, submission) stated with source page
- [ ] No other-client names or internal rate information in any artifact that could ship

## References
- `references/requirement-taxonomy.md` — categories, mandatory detection, hidden-mandatory patterns, evaluation weighting
- `references/compliance-scoring.md` — C/P/N/Q rules, evidence standard, bid/no-bid gate, clarification-question format
- `assets/compliance-matrix-columns.md` — column specification for CSV/XLSX
- `scripts/extract_requirements.py` — .txt/.md/.docx/.pdf → requirements CSV

## How to run (automation, when commands can run)
This skill is executable. Collect the inputs below, then run `python3 scripts/run_skill.py presales/rfp-compliance-matrix --input <name>=<value> … --out <dir>` (see `--explain presales/rfp-compliance-matrix`). Report the `run.json` results; do not hand-write the deliverables the scripts produce.

solution-architecture-doc

In a conversation: write the document now

  • The request carries facts (systems, interfaces, constraints, NFRs, dates, audience): write the architecture document in this reply. Do not ask for a file or JSON first, and never answer with only questions. Use what is given; mark each missing fact To be baselined · owner: <role>; end with the few questions that would close those gaps.
  • The request carries no client facts at all: ask once, in one list, for current-state facts, drivers and constraints, NFR expectations and the audience. Do not draw a current state from assumptions. You may offer a generic pattern catalogue, labelled "not client-specific".
  • Asked to invent NFR numbers or to "just pick" products: say in one line why not (unsourced targets and undecided products become contractual and credibility risk). Show each target as To be baselined · owner to be named with its measurement method and the discovery question that would set it; show products as role placeholders with proposed ADRs naming the client decision owner; offer the scored options table as the way to decide.

The document, in this order (CIO depth: 6–10 pages, the bottom line stands alone; ARB depth adds component, deployment and security views):

  1. Bottom line — the target state in one paragraph, the top 3 decisions, the waves, the biggest risk, what is still open.
  2. Drivers and constraints — each with its source.
  3. Current state (context + container, Mermaid) from evidence only; every box source-tagged; unknown integrations dashed and listed as gaps.
  4. Options and recommendation — at least two options scored on weighted criteria (show the arithmetic); the choice is ADR-001.
  5. Target state (context + container, Mermaid C4) — undecided products as placeholders.
  6. Integration map — interfaces grouped by pattern, with protocol, data, volume/SLA (sourced or marked) and wave.
  7. NFRs — target, measurement method, source, design response; constraints such as data residency become NFRs.
  8. Security and data, operability and environments.
  9. Migration waves — goal, scope, entry and exit criteria, rollback, aligned to the stated dates.
  10. Decision log (ADRs with owner and status), risks (likelihood × impact, owner, mitigation), open items with owners, sources.

Starting points

  • New — the target design becomes a decision-ready architecture document: bottom line, drivers, C4 context, container and deployment diagrams, integration map, migration waves (entry, exit, rollback), NFRs, security, scored options with ADRs, risks, decision log, open items and sources.
  • Existing — add current (the estate as it runs today, same layout): the document gains a change view — containers kept, added, retired or re-platformed, integrations added, retired or re-patterned — and a decision-log row for every retirement and re-platform.

When to use

  • "Produce the target architecture for <client>'s <initiative>."
  • "Draw the C4 context and container views for the proposal."
  • "Write the NFRs and decision log for this design."
  • "Review this architecture document before it goes to the client."
  • NOT for: effort (effort-estimator), interface scoring and TCO (integration-migration-assessor), proposal prose (proposal-writer).

Inputs required

InputRequiredSource
Current-state facts: systems, platforms, integration inventory, environments, hostingyesdiscovery synthesis / assessor output / client docs
Drivers and constraints: objectives, compliance regimes, vendor decisions already made, budget shape, datesyesdiscovery synthesis / RFP
Stated NFR expectations (volumes, latency, availability, RPO/RTO, security) or "none stated"yesclient docs / user
Audience: CIO deck-level vs architecture-review-board levelyesuser
Existing draft (review mode)yes in reviewfile

Missing facts never stop the draft: write what is evidenced, mark the rest To be baselined · owner to be named, and ask for it at the end. Never draw a current-state diagram from assumptions.

Procedure

Read ../../../shared/quality-bar.md and ../../../shared/writing-style.md first.

  1. Fix the audience and depth per references/architecture-method.md §1. CIO-level: context view + container view + decisions + waves, 6–10 pages. ARB-level: add component views for the critical containers, full NFR table, deployment view, security view.
  2. Draw the current state first (context + container) from evidence only. Every box carries a source tag (document, slide, interview). Unknown integrations are drawn dashed with a ? label and listed as gaps. This diagram is the baseline the client will correct; invite correction explicitly.
  3. Decision point — architecture options. Identify the 2–3 options that the drivers permit (e.g., strangler migration vs big-bang; single API gateway vs federated; event backbone vs point-to-point API). Score each against the weighted criteria in §3 of the method (fit to drivers, risk, cost shape, time to value, operability, lock-in). Record the chosen option as ADR-001 using assets/adr-template.md; the others become the "alternatives considered" section. Never present a single option as inevitable.
  4. Draw the target state (context, container; component for critical containers at ARB depth) with the Mermaid C4 templates in assets/mermaid-c4-templates.md. Name every container with technology placeholders only where a product decision is still open; mark those To be baselined · owner to be named.
  5. Build the integration map: table of interfaces (source, target, pattern, protocol, data, volume, SLA, owner, wave) from the assessor output or the inventory; group by pattern (sync API, async event, batch file, managed-file transfer). Volumes and SLAs come from sources or are marked.
  6. Write the NFRs with assets/nfr-checklist.md: every applicable NFR gets a measurable target, a measurement method, a source for the target (client statement, regulation, SLA), and a design response. "High availability" is not an NFR; "99.9% monthly, measured at the gateway, excluding planned windows ≤4h/month" is.
  7. Log every significant decision as an ADR (context, options, decision, consequences, status, owner, date). Significant = changes cost, risk, vendor lock-in, or operating model. Decisions the client must make are ADRs in proposed status with the client owner named.
  8. Plan migration waves per §5 of the method: wave criteria (risk, dependency, business value, freeze windows), per-wave scope, entry/exit criteria, rollback approach, parallel-run strategy. Wave membership for interfaces comes from the assessor's wave assignment when it exists.
  9. Security, data, and operability views at the depth the audience needs: identity and access model, data classification and residency, secrets, observability, environments and promotion path, DR.
  10. Review mode: read the draft fully; check each section against the review rubric in references/architecture-review-rubric.md; produce [KEEP] [SHARPEN] [CUT] [ADD] [TBD] findings with rewritten content; deliver the clean version.
  11. Run the self-check.

Output

  • architecture.md (Mermaid blocks inline, for Git and Confluence) and architecture.html (the same document, printable, diagrams inline; Print → Save as PDF)
  • diagrams/context.svg, diagrams/container.svg, diagrams/deployment.svg (C4 pictures for slides) and architecture.drawio (every view, editable in diagrams.net / Confluence)
  • adr/ADR-nnn-<slug>.md per decision, with the weighted option scores; nfr.csv
  • Sections: Bottom line (target state in one paragraph + top 3 decisions) · Drivers and constraints · Current state (diagrams + gaps) · Options and recommendation (scored table) · Target state (diagrams) · Integration map · NFRs · Security and data · Operability and environments · Migration waves · Decision log (ADR index) · Risks · Open items with owners
  • Appendices: adr/ADR-nnn-<slug>.md per decision (template assets/adr-template.md)

Self-check

  • [ ] Current-state boxes each carry a source; unknowns dashed and listed as gaps
  • [ ] ≥2 options scored on stated criteria before the recommendation
  • [ ] Every NFR has target, measurement method, source, design response
  • [ ] Every significant decision has an ADR with owner and status
  • [ ] Every volume, SLA, count sourced or To be baselined · owner to be named
  • [ ] Waves have entry/exit criteria and rollback
  • [ ] Product names appear only where decided; otherwise placeholders marked
  • [ ] Diagrams render (valid Mermaid); each has a one-line caption stating what it shows
  • [ ] No other-client architecture details, no author history

References

  • references/architecture-method.md — depth by audience, current-state evidence rules, option scoring, wave planning, views
  • references/architecture-review-rubric.md — review criteria and scoring for existing documents
  • assets/mermaid-c4-templates.md — Mermaid C4 context/container/component/deployment templates
  • assets/nfr-checklist.md — NFR categories with target patterns and measurement methods
  • assets/adr-template.md — ADR template

When you can run commands, put the facts into components.json (layout: evals/fixtures/northwind-order-hub.json) and run python3 scripts/run_skill.py presales/solution-architecture-doc --input components=<file> --input client=<name> --out <dir>; report run.json and hand over the deliverables it writes (below) instead of re-typing them. When you cannot run commands, write the document yourself following the Procedure — never answer a request that already carries facts with only a question. | Input | Required | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Current-state facts: systems, platforms, integration inventory, environments, hosting | yes | discovery synthesis / assessor output / client docs |
| Drivers and constraints: objectives, compliance regimes, vendor decisions already made, budget shape, dates | yes | discovery synthesis / RFP |
| Stated NFR expectations (volumes, latency, availability, RPO/RTO, security) or "none stated" | yes | client docs / user |
| Audience: CIO deck-level vs architecture-review-board level | yes | user |
| Existing draft (review mode) | yes in review | file |

Missing facts never stop the draft: write what is evidenced, mark the rest `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]`, and ask for it at the end. Never draw a current-state diagram from assumptions.

## Procedure
Read `../../../shared/quality-bar.md` and `../../../shared/writing-style.md` first.

1. **Fix the audience and depth** per `references/architecture-method.md` §1. CIO-level: context view + container view + decisions + waves, 6–10 pages. ARB-level: add component views for the critical containers, full NFR table, deployment view, security view.
2. **Draw the current state first** (context + container) from evidence only. Every box carries a source tag (document, slide, interview). Unknown integrations are drawn dashed with a `?` label and listed as gaps. This diagram is the baseline the client will correct; invite correction explicitly.
3. **Decision point — architecture options.** Identify the 2–3 options that the drivers permit (e.g., strangler migration vs big-bang; single API gateway vs federated; event backbone vs point-to-point API). Score each against the weighted criteria in §3 of the method (fit to drivers, risk, cost shape, time to value, operability, lock-in). Record the chosen option as ADR-001 using `assets/adr-template.md`; the others become the "alternatives considered" section. Never present a single option as inevitable.
4. **Draw the target state** (context, container; component for critical containers at ARB depth) with the Mermaid C4 templates in `assets/mermaid-c4-templates.md`. Name every container with technology placeholders only where a product decision is still open; mark those `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]`.
5. **Build the integration map**: table of interfaces (source, target, pattern, protocol, data, volume, SLA, owner, wave) from the assessor output or the inventory; group by pattern (sync API, async event, batch file, managed-file transfer). Volumes and SLAs come from sources or are marked.
6. **Write the NFRs** with `assets/nfr-checklist.md`: every applicable NFR gets a measurable target, a measurement method, a source for the target (client statement, regulation, SLA), and a design response. "High availability" is not an NFR; "99.9% monthly, measured at the gateway, excluding planned windows ≤4h/month" is.
7. **Log every significant decision** as an ADR (context, options, decision, consequences, status, owner, date). Significant = changes cost, risk, vendor lock-in, or operating model. Decisions the client must make are ADRs in `proposed` status with the client owner named.
8. **Plan migration waves** per §5 of the method: wave criteria (risk, dependency, business value, freeze windows), per-wave scope, entry/exit criteria, rollback approach, parallel-run strategy. Wave membership for interfaces comes from the assessor's wave assignment when it exists.
9. **Security, data, and operability views** at the depth the audience needs: identity and access model, data classification and residency, secrets, observability, environments and promotion path, DR.
10. **Review mode**: read the draft fully; check each section against the review rubric in `references/architecture-review-rubric.md`; produce `[KEEP] [SHARPEN] [CUT] [ADD] [TBD]` findings with rewritten content; deliver the clean version.
11. Run the self-check.

## Output
- `architecture.md` (Mermaid blocks inline, for Git and Confluence) and `architecture.html` (the same document, printable, diagrams inline; Print → Save as PDF)
- `diagrams/context.svg`, `diagrams/container.svg`, `diagrams/deployment.svg` (C4 pictures for slides) and `architecture.drawio` (every view, editable in diagrams.net / Confluence)
- `adr/ADR-nnn-<slug>.md` per decision, with the weighted option scores; `nfr.csv`
- Sections: Bottom line (target state in one paragraph + top 3 decisions) · Drivers and constraints · Current state (diagrams + gaps) · Options and recommendation (scored table) · Target state (diagrams) · Integration map · NFRs · Security and data · Operability and environments · Migration waves · Decision log (ADR index) · Risks · Open items with owners
- Appendices: `adr/ADR-nnn-<slug>.md` per decision (template `assets/adr-template.md`)

## Self-check
- [ ] Current-state boxes each carry a source; unknowns dashed and listed as gaps
- [ ] ≥2 options scored on stated criteria before the recommendation
- [ ] Every NFR has target, measurement method, source, design response
- [ ] Every significant decision has an ADR with owner and status
- [ ] Every volume, SLA, count sourced or `[TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]`
- [ ] Waves have entry/exit criteria and rollback
- [ ] Product names appear only where decided; otherwise placeholders marked
- [ ] Diagrams render (valid Mermaid); each has a one-line caption stating what it shows
- [ ] No other-client architecture details, no author history

## References
- `references/architecture-method.md` — depth by audience, current-state evidence rules, option scoring, wave planning, views
- `references/architecture-review-rubric.md` — review criteria and scoring for existing documents
- `assets/mermaid-c4-templates.md` — Mermaid C4 context/container/component/deployment templates
- `assets/nfr-checklist.md` — NFR categories with target patterns and measurement methods
- `assets/adr-template.md` — ADR template

When you can run commands, put the facts into `components.json` (layout: `evals/fixtures/northwind-order-hub.json`) and run `python3 scripts/run_skill.py presales/solution-architecture-doc --input components=<file> --input client=<name> --out <dir>`; report `run.json` and hand over the deliverables it writes (below) instead of re-typing them.
